Blue therapy is a thing 💙

Studies have shown that time spent near, in and on natural healthy waters can have fantastic health benefits and argues that this “blue prescription” should be in every doctor’s toolkit alongside mainstays like exercise, a good diet, and sleep.

At the seaside, the air we breathe is charged with negative ions. These molecules are believed to have a positive effect on serotonin levels and thus improve our mood.

Over 71% of our planet is covered in “blue space”—including lakes, rives, wetlands, oceans, and all waterways.

Spending at least two hours in nature's blue every week can have a significant impact on physical and mental well-being.

The idea that we exercise to get thin may be more dangerous than ever, @xochitltheg writes. ⁠
⁠
“Fitness can be a complicated thing. For some, the motivation is health, and for others it’s pure enjoyment of the sport or physical activity. But for many—especially the Gen Xers among us, who, if we weren’t given an eating disorder by our Boomer moms, picked one up at college or from our Cosmopolitan and Vogue magazines—the real point is weight loss. Yes, exercise has health benefits, but those are side effects of the aesthetic goal,” Gonzalez writes. ⁠
⁠
This was how she had always approached exercise. “I worked out because of eating issues and body-image challenges cultivated early in my life,” she writes. But after a friend died suddenly, Gonzalez was drawn by another friend to a SoulCycle class and began to see a different side of what exercise could mean. “Exercise can be an act not of vanity, but of psychological self-care. Many wars are being waged against women—against our bodies, our rights, our sizes, our images of ourselves, and who is and isn’t allowed to claim this identity. For a long time, I felt that by rejecting movement, I was rejecting an idealized and impossible body image, that I was learning ‘self-acceptance.’ But really I was just sabotaging my own mental health,” she writes. ⁠
⁠

If they can now stay skinny with just an injection and a few picked-over meals, will they abandon fitness? My fitness journey…

I grew up playing sports and loved any and all kinds of physical activity. I did gymnastics, basketball, cheer, and track. Because I was such an active kid, I always remember being “in shape”, but never like the pictures I had saved on my Pinterest boards.

After high school I felt a little lost. I still loved being active but didn’t really have any fitness goals or a coach telling me what to do and when to do it like I used to. I was also super intimidated by the massive college gyms and WAS NOT walking across campus in the dark lol.

During my sophomore year I started running after I got off work. I was close to my old gym but was still scared of the free weight area so the treadmill and stair stepper became my best friend. That was the ONLY time in my life I can say I enjoyed running for distance🤣 I would get there around 10pm and run 3-5 miles.

Chris finally convinced me to lift with him by promising to workout with me in the evenings. It didn’t take long at all before I fell in love with weight training. I was seeing the best results I had ever seen but STILL not like the picture I considered to be “goals” on Pinterest.

Shortly after I started working at lululemon and met a handful of people in the bodybuilding world. I was missing the competitive aspect of sports and already eating a pretty strict diet and working out a bunch and figured why not try out a bikini competition! 

I dieted for three months and followed strict meal plans. I’d eat the same thing for three weeks and then get a slightly different meal plan. Although I absolutely loved the journey, I was anything but easy! I had to be SO STRICT and EXTREMELY SELFISH. Food at family gatherings was off limits, date nights weren’t a thing, and I basically lived at the gym - lifting 5-6 days a week with cardio once or twice a day.

But guess what?? 

I started looking more like the pictures I had saved on Pinterest. It BLEW MY MIND that the bodies I had been looking at as “goals” since high school, were literally completion physiques…AKA bodies that only looked like that for a short period of time.

Leroy's teacher sends him to find a master who can teach him about the glow. He ends up at a fortune cookie factory, where he's told there is no master. Feeling down, he goes back to his teacher, who tells him that the master he was looking for is inside of him, and he already has the glow. At the end of the movie, Leroy finally achieves the glow while facing his toughest enemy.

This message speaks volumes to me. I’ve searched around, taken courses, hired mentors, sought out knowledge,guidance, and learned from others, but it's crucial to remember that our most valuable resource is within ourselves. BELIEVE IN YOUR OWN POWER!

Friday Thoughts:

You are never too young to purchase a Grabber off Amazon😂

It comes in handy when you can't bend over or pick up things that fall on the floor.  I have struggled with back pain and disc issues for a number of years. Every once in a while I get reminded of my true age and I can't do back flips anymore.  Not being able to move or move well is stifling to one who moves for a living. So what to do with all that time resting you may ask:  Well, if you are struggling to hang in there we can navigate injuries and come out better in the end. Here are some tips:

1. Spend some time in prayer and catch up on your Bible Study

2. Connect with friends by phone, letter(remember those)

3. Order your Grabber off Amazon and anything else that looks fun. I ordered new pink lululemon shorts and they make me feel better. 

4. Keep your sense of humor and watch LeAnn Morgan on Netflix, she is hilarious!😂Laughter is the best medicine

5. Enjoy watching your husband pick up the slack.  Steve is amazing and can clean and cook with the best of them.

6. Work on your mindset-ask me and I am happy to share what is working for me. Join my positive mindset program.

7. Dial in your nutrition to help you feel better, heal faster and come out on the better end of things when you get back to moving.

8. I focus on what I can do and not what I can't. I can lay flat, bridge up a few times, I can lay on my side and do some leg lifts and that's a start. I can still coach or train you, just use my brain instead of my body. Trainer might be down but not out. 

9. Soak in the tub with Dr. Teals. I mean the bath salts silly😝

10. Enjoy the down time, sit outside and soak in the sunshine and just be still.  It's going to be ok. Time will heal. Ask yourself what you can learn from this.

Grupo Crystal, el tercer grupo textil que más vende en el país y el segundo que más vende de Antioquia – según cifras de la Superintendencia de Sociedades–, empezó su historia en un pequeño local en el centro de Medellín vendiendo medias veladas hace 84 años. Hoy, ya cuenta con 250 tiendas en Colombia.

Dos hermanos paisas, Octavio y Julio Echavarría están detrás de su fundación. Por años se enfocaron en convertir a Crystal en un jugador importante en la fabricación de medias en Colombia a través de su marca propia Galax, pero fue el hijo de uno de ellos, Carlos Manuel Echavarría, quien dio el salto hacia la internacionalización y la diversificación de su portafolio.

La receta le funcionó y actualmente Grupo Crystal emplea cerca de 7.000 personas en el país y registra ingresos operacionales por más de $800.000 millones de pesos. “Hoy nos dedicamos al negocio de construir y comercializar marcas de moda, estamos apalancados en un retail propio para el mercado latinoamericano y gracias a nuestra trayectoria también nos dedicamos a la fabricación de marcas para terceros en el mercado americano”, explica en conversación con Forbes Luis Fernando Restrepo Echavarría, presidente Corporativo de Grupo Crystal y miembro de la tercera generación de los Echavarría Hernández.

Sus marcas Punto Blanco (española, adquirida en 1969), Gef (francesa, con la que se quedó en 1989), Baby Fresh, Casino y Galax son referentes en sus segmentos. Solo en medias, la compañía produce 7.000 docenas al día, es decir, 14.000 unidades. Además, fabrican en Colombia productos para gigantes internacionales como Lululemon, Spanx, Michael Kors y North Face, entre otras. Según el directivo, el 30% de sus ventas proviene de la exportación de sus marcas propias y de los que fabrican para terceros.

México, Perú y países de Centroamérica están en la lista de los 13 países a los que exportan.

This week’s “Business Spotlight” is @vidabealeconsignment, which is located at 29 S Church Street. 👗 We sat down with the owner, Kirsten Gross, to get the inside scoop.

1. Tell me about your business and what makes it unique.

Our vision is to empower women so they feel confident in their own unique style, present their best selves to the world, and not be forced to compromise on the affordability of today’s most desired fashion trends.

2. What services or products do you offer?

Vida Beale Consignment exists to provide cost-savvy, fashion-conscious women the ability to purchase on-trend, upscale, used clothing and accessories at an affordable price. We also sell furniture and home décor.

3. How long have you been in business?

We’ve been in West Chester for 1.5 years!

4. What do you love most about being located in West Chester?

I mean, what’s not to love?? West Chester is a destination! It’s a unique place with so much charm and small, college-town appeal. It has an energy all on its own. The community is particularly supportive of small businesses, which is something I’ve been very grateful for. I feel fortunate to both live and work here in the Borough. 

5. What can you tell me about the culture or atmosphere of your business?

A visit to Vida Beale is kind of like going on an upscale treasure hunt! You can trust the impeccable clothing, accessories, and home furnishings you find here. Consignment stores like Vida Beale are unique in the retail industry. You will discover numerous brand names like Anthropologie, Lululemon, Athleta, J. Crew, Burberry, and so many more. We shop consignment too! And like you, we are watching our wallets and finding value in a good deal. 

Everyone is welcome at Vida Beale! We value our customers as we do our friends. 

6. Is there anything else you would like to share about your business?

We have new, spring inventory arriving daily. We are constantly restocking our clearance room with items at up to 75% off the original price. We also hold private shopping and social events here at the store. Call to inquire!

Last week vs. Prior 4 week avg
🏃🏻 9:49, 45.5 mi, 4,987 ft ⬇️ 10:02, 50.3 mi, 6,813 ft

•
You must believe that the journey is just as important as the destination. 
•
What? Did you think you weren’t going to get a training update because of a poor race?

The good: My run volume wasn’t too far below my usual, but the elevation gain took a dip. I cut-back on the incline hikes to save it for the race. Another loop of the 🧨 course would put me over the top on both mileage and vert. I happily banked more time in the saddle earlier in the week due to the anticipated race weekend. I’d like to find a way to keep this bike volume up. 

The bad: Strength and mobility were down. I gave myself a planned deload week of strength because of the race, but my mobility work was down way more than I would have liked. I will find time to sprinkle mobility breaks in during the day. 

Grade: B minus. The overall training load was good. I just need to work on balancing it out better.

Hard work (NO PAIN, NO GAIN) mentality doesn’t work for most people.
.
Technique, building habits, being world-class at the basics (+ hard work) does.
.
The latter was my focus when I coached on a professional athlete/coach visa in the States. I wanted my swimmers to succeed where I failed in the sport. (I injured myself out of the sport in the lead-up to Olympic trials in 2012).
.
The reason I had to call it a day on my competitive swimming career? I had used up my ability to work hard. My body had nothing left to give. Chronic injuries were keeping me up at night with chronic pain. I knew it wasn’t sustainable and that meant that unfortunately I couldn’t continue competing.
.
The reason I had used up my ability to work hard wasn’t because I wasn’t because I didn’t have more energy to give, it was because (and this is more common that anyone in sport and fitness would like to admit), I had never learned how to train sustainably.. with better technique, habits and basics.
.
I watched ~15 different people get surgeries on my Div 1 university team over 4 years, half of them needing second surgeries before their career was finished. What’s crazy was, with all that hard work and intensity of training to the point of injury, our team wasn’t the best. The top performing teams had moved on from “just work hard”, to sophisticated systems of bettering technique, habits, and most importantly, becoming brilliant at the basics. Yes - they still worked hard, but intelligently with longterm health and goals in mind - not “just making it to the end of the season”.
.
Some of my former swimmers have moved on from the sport, and some compete at the top level of the sport in the NCAA and in the States. If there is one thing I’m most proud of achieving with them, it’s that I helped them learn how to train more sustainably and enjoy themselves.

I have been through a lot of ups and downs in my life. I have gotten to travel the world playing the sport I love. At one point I wanted it to be my full time job.

And then I found racing…

Nothing quite compares to the feeling you get when you cross a finish line after everything you put yourself through to get there. 

The emotions that flood your system. The pain, the joy, the triumph all hits you at once. Realizing the late nights, the early mornings, the sacrifices the dedication, the pain and hard work that went into that. It all comes to the surface. 

It’s a feeling that can never be explained until you feel it for yourself. Whether you’re racing to win or racing to beat yourself or your mind; the emotions are incredible. 

February I came up short on my goals. It was still an amazing day, the best run I’ve ever done, some of the most pain I’ve ever experienced and I loved it. But, I still came up short. 

2 years straight I have been training non-stop. All in, sometimes all consumed by my goals. When I first started running I didn’t even think I would ever be able to run a marathon and now in 6 weeks time I will run a marathon in under 3 hours and qualify for the 2024 @bostonmarathon 

@buffalomarathon tell them we’re coming. Im working harder than I ever have. Im fitter than I’ve ever been and I’m focused and locked into full sending straight into the pain cave and out the other side. 

I can’t wait to have this feeling again. This time, with the goal achieved. 

Keep going.

Happy #TechniqueTipTuesday! 

This week we will be discussing an exercise you will see a lot in Classic—extensions during triceps!

-You will sometimes hear your teacher cue “tiny bend, extend” during class. What they mean is to only bend your elbow the tiniest bit, and then fully extend your arm all the way by squeezing the back of your arm (tricep). Try to keep this movement tiny so you can control the muscle you are trying to work, and minimize shifting your body. 
-Really hinge forward from the waist and keep a flat back. If you are not hinged forward enough, you are not getting as much work out of the exercise. If your body is too rounded forward, the work will also be lost because alignment is off. 
-Squeeze your blades together, and press your shoulders down and away from your ears. You want to imagine your arms are getting longer every time you extend them. 
-Keep a soft bend in your knees, and shift more weight into the balls of your feet, rather than sinking back onto your heels. 
-Remember that you don’t NEED weights to get a good shake—sometimes working without equipment can be a big game changer!

Here are my tip running tips that I’ve learned over the last 4 months while training for my half marathon🏃🏽‍♀️⚡️

before you say, you’re not a runner…either was I. 

I barley could run over a mile when I started and by the end I finished 13.1 feeling better than ever 🤍

1. Start slow  —— jog at the beginning don’t think you need to run fast. Consistently is important just take it with ease  2. Find routes & mini routes you enjoy  —— I had 3 main routes I’d run and that I knew well  —— I also had mini routes (2-3 miles each) that I’d do on my long runs to mentally break it up  3. Treadmills… —— avoid looking at the time / distance  —— break it up and do interval runs (a few miles rest repeat)  4. Have multiple playlist read to go  —— i got sick of the same songs quickly ; mixes are helpful like big bootie mix  —— Spotify has “running” playlists already created I enjoyed  —— when runs for really hard , I’d listen to motivational mixes like (David goggins)  5. Dress properly  —— fitted stretchy and dry fit clothes are best  —— i used a running buddy to hold my phone keys and airpod case  —— gymshark running leggings & Lululemon define jacket was my fav  —— headband and gloves saved me so many times from wind and cold  6. Proper hydration, fuel, and rest is critical  —— drink tons of water before and after (pretty much 24/7)  —— eat right & enough…you’ll likely increase your appetite the more you run & honor that! Listen to your body when you need a rest day, take one. Prioritize sleep, that’s when your body recovers 7. Understand not all runs will feel amazing —— its going to be physically and mentally hard sometimes but that’s okay  —— stay consistent and disciplined  —— pre-plan your runs  8. Underhand majority of it is mental  —— control your thoughts before and during your runs  —— it’s only as hard as you tell yourself ; keep a positive mindset  9. Find the right running shoes  —— its best to go to an actual running store and have them fit and test you to find the right fit. —— size up .5-1 size because your feet will swell. It’ll help avoid blisters or losing toenails

Takeaway: Despite the official DNF, I got everything I needed on the trip from a training perspective with 20 miles and 4K feet of gain. I tested out new fueling and hydration. With 2.5-3 less race hours on my body, I’ll be able to pick up my training this week where I left off. 

Bonus: I always enjoy being able to run the same race with my athletes. It was great to share the course with Taylor and Julianna. 

Salt in the wound: The weather the following day in Dallas was a real feel of 42 degrees. Seriously race gods? Such is life.

I had to stand in my power and acknowledge the worthiness inside of me simply because I was breathing. 
Not being clear on my values allowed me to discount myself, and although I love a great deal, I AM NO clearance rack type of girl, and neither are you!

💕6 tips to practice conscience dating:
 
1️⃣Get clear on your values and what you are looking for in a partner. Write them down and use them as a guide when dating.
2️⃣Be present during dates. Put away your phone, focus on the conversation, and pay attention to body language and nonverbal cues.
3️⃣ Listen to your intuition. If something doesn't feel right, it probably isn't. Trust your gut, and don't ignore red flags.
4️⃣ Communicate your needs and boundaries early and clearly. It's important to be honest and upfront with your partner about what you want and need in a relationship.
5️⃣ Take things slow. Don't rush into a relationship or make decisions based on societal pressure or external expectations.
6️⃣ Practice self-care. Take care of yourself emotionally, physically, and spiritually so that you can show up fully in a relationship.

Remember, it's not just about finding the right person but also about becoming the right person for the relationship you desire.

When I found my teacher I was led from the heart and fell heart-first into a lineage based practice. It has served me well and I am so grateful. There are so many people teaching (which I think is good) and yoga is available everywhere (also good). I suggest we learn to apply our analytical mind a bit so that we can find the teacher that best aligns with our path.

What do you look for in a yoga teacher? What is the difference between a teacher, an instructor and a guru? Do you think you need a teacher or a guide at all?

I feel like whatever keeps us on the path and supports us to keep practicing is to be cherished, honored and respected. I doubt I’d be practicing toddy without the constant steady presence of my teachers on the path. But what about you?

對於瑜伽人而言，在練習的路上總會出現跟自己價值觀相近的僧寶同路人。我們一起學習、一起經歷人生的高低起伏，也一起透過瑜伽變健康。三年多的疫情已近乎尾聲，蟄伏已久的動能蓄勢待發。這兩年的高雄熱熱鬧鬧，整座城市充滿了不同的活力。接續這股熱情的感染，是時候讓瑜伽也走進更多人的生活裡。念頭一起，便催生了瑜伽馬拉松的想法。
​
今年六月，想邀請你與好友們，一同來參加高雄難得舉辦的大型瑜伽活動。我們集結了四位風格迥異且各具特色的老師，將帶領四種不同主題的瑜伽課。有專精於基礎動作分解的Ingrid與Ken，幫大家打造穩固的根基；接著由最資深的內觀流指導Emma老師，將瑜伽動作帶入與音樂的結合；最後統整所有能力並與夥伴通力合作，由咪咪老師帶大家完成雙人瑜伽。每個看似獨立卻又不可劃分的主題，引導大家從不同的入口，進入身心合而為一的目的地。
​
本次活動將由總是鼓勵人們享受『熱汗生活』#thesweatlife 的加拿大運動品牌lululemon高雄漢神巨蛋店，提供專業瑜伽墊讓大家使用。參與者只需要帶著輕鬆愉快的心，來享受呼吸與身體的脈動，愉悅與汗水交織的美好下午。歡迎在炎熱的夏天來臨之際，與我們一起在百年歷史的糖倉中感受身體的流動。
​
​
◉‿◉ 
馬拉松式的瑜伽課，補給怎能忘記！我們將在活動中提供可口的下午茶點，讓大家在揮汗之餘也能補充能量。還有！活動結束後一個月內（7/10前），至好好：瑜伽官網私訊告知姓名，即可任選一堂價值$500元的免費體驗課（新舊生都有喔）。還有！可能也還有新的驚喜，但現在還不能說。

PROJET CLIENT #4 - Édition 2021

Un projet que j’ai adoré faire !
Léa, la fondatrice du @leyogascope avec qui j’avais déjà travaillé m’a proposé de créer un visuel pour une collaboration avec une de mes marques favorites ever @lululemon ! J’ai découvert cette marque lorsque je suis partie vivre au Canada, est c’est LA marque de référence quand il s’agit de sportswear donc j’étais trop trop trop heureuse !🙌🏻

Pour ceux qui ne connaissent pas le Yogascope, c’est une agence de voyages spécialisée dans les retraites yoga. L’idée était de créer un woven label qui serait cousu sur toutes les pièces de la collab, brassières, leggings, t-shirts, cyclistes, pantalons lounge wear, etc. Il fallait créer un visuel qui soit tout terrain et qui puisse s’adapter sur un format portrait mais aussi un format paysage. Léa m’avait donné pas mal de références graphiques qui correspond à l’univers de sa marque, notamment l’oeil pour le Dieu égyptien Horus, le soleil, les plantes, et le serpent ! 

Et oui, le serpent n’a pas toujours mauvaise réputation en terme de symbolique, il représente, dans certaines cultures Africaines, une source de vitalité et de souplesse, une signification tout à fait à propos pour une agence de voyage spécialisée dans les retraites yoga. 🧡

J’en ai profité de mon coté pour la broder sur ma casquette préférée 🌞

Alors, vous aimez ? 🐍

@maggiegrindatti I lost discipline 🪫 

But today I am Proud 🐆

For the first time in my life I lost discipline. As everyone knows and the memes say, “motivation comes and goes, it’s discipline you have to have.” And this is 💯. Clichés are clichés for a reason. 

I didn’t workout for two weeks and as “okay” as that might seem for some, it’s not and no one should do that. Our bodies not only need exercise but they need routine to feel the best, inside and out. 

Not having a routine for the last 3 months was wild and also a first for me and when I started putting CHAMPIONFIT together that’s where all my focus went and the nerves, excitement and anxiety from that, my exercise and eating routine went out the , when I truthfully probably needed it the most. 

BUT TODAY I finished my week, completing all my workouts and trainings, I function off a 6 day program and completed it and for that I am proud. 

YES rest days or two days are okay but stop telling yourself, all that time off is “okay” because it’s not and if you have to convince yourself of it, there is your answer right there! 

Losing discipline for the first time is 30 years, ain’t too bad but making a promise to myself that from now to 60 we don’t do it again 😅 And to say im being hard on myself I’m not, my standards that I hold myself to, are what have gotten me to where I am today. 

Now time to head to @ralphgraciesac for a seminar!

Not having a routine for the last 3 months was wild and also a first for me and when I started putting CHAMPIONFIT together that’s where all my focus went and the nerves, excitement and anxiety from that, my exercise and eating routine went out the , when I truthfully probably needed it the most. 

BUT TODAY I finished my week, completing all my workouts and trainings, I function off a 6 day program and completed it and for that I am proud. 

YES rest days or two days are okay but stop telling yourself, all that time off is “okay” because it’s not and if you have to convince yourself of it, there is your answer right there! 

Losing discipline for the first time is 30 years, ain’t too bad but making a promise to myself that from now to 60 we don’t do it again 😅 And to say im being hard on myself I’m not, my standards that I hold myself to, are what have gotten me to where I am today. 

Now time to head to @ralphgraciesac for a seminar!

It doesn’t always need to be deep and powerful. It just needs to be one step along the path.

It doesn’t always have to be miraculous and world-changing. There is wisdom to be found in ordinary moments in the mat.

Instead of looking for a quick fix, the path of yoga offers a slow, steady route to gently bend the arc of life towards more happiness, wholeness and love.

The 50k Bear Mountain Race - my 2nd (training) race of the season.

Beautiful weather for this sold out @sassquadtrailrunning Trail party 🌞 

Started out strong but had to slow down during the 2nd half due to rolling my ankle and bustin up my knee pretty bad.

The trails out there are gnarly and hard to run.

Big vert day with over 7,000 gain & loss over the 31 miles.

One of the things I wanted to test out during this training race is seeing how much fuel I could take in.

While I was able to stay on target during the first half of the race, consuming 120g of carbs/hour, I slowed down a little bit at the end, averaging 107g of carbs/hour over the 7-hour race.

Not only did this higher carb intake lead to a better performance on the day, but I believe it led to a faster recovery in the days following it. (I'm feeling much less sore than I would from an effort of this length/intensity.)

PMID: 32403259 Showing that adequate carbohydrate intake during exercise optimizes athletic performance and could limit exercise induced muscle damage, reduce internal exercise load and, thus, improve recovery.

They compared mountain marathoners fueling with 120g carbs/hr, 90g/hr, and 60g/hr.

While there was not a large difference between the 90g/hr and 60g/hr groups, measurements showed a significant difference in the 120g/hr groups biomarkers.

The 120g/hr group had significantly lower levels of creatine kinase, lactate dehydrogenase, and glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase after the race. 

If you're not fueling your activities properly, you're missing out on potential performance and recovery benefits.

So - eat up my friends! 😋😋😋

Yoga for Self-Care

5 ways that yoga can help with self care 

Yoga can be a powerful tool for self-care, helping to improve both physical and mental well-being. Here are five ways that yoga can help with self-care:

Reduces stress and anxiety: Yoga has been shown to reduce levels of the stress hormone cortisol in the body, which can help to alleviate feelings of stress and anxiety. Practicing yoga regularly can also help to regulate breathing and calm the nervous system, which can help to promote relaxation.

Improves physical health: Yoga is a low-impact exercise that can help to improve strength, flexibility, and balance. Regular yoga practice can also help to improve circulation, boost immunity, and reduce the risk of chronic diseases like heart disease and diabetes.

Enhances mindfulness: Yoga can help to cultivate mindfulness, which is the practice of being present and aware in the moment. Mindfulness can help to reduce negative self-talk, increase self-awareness, and improve overall emotional well-being.

Promotes better sleep: Yoga has been shown to improve sleep quality and reduce insomnia. The physical postures and breathing exercises in yoga can help to calm the mind and relax the body, which can make it easier to fall asleep and stay asleep.

Fosters self-awareness: Yoga can help to deepen self-awareness, which is the ability to understand one's own thoughts, emotions, and behaviors. This can help to increase self-acceptance and self-compassion, and can also help to identify areas for personal growth and development

Be back soon!✌️ I suffered a set-back two months ago with a partial tendon tear in my foot. It took what felt like forever to diagnose the injury and even longer for me to accept it. That and the fact that I would need to stop running/cycling/walking for a significant amount of time to rest my foot and allow the tendon to heal. Feeling frustrated at having to cancel all of my spring goal races and my inability to get around as easy as I used to but blessed that it’s not a more serious injury. 

As I scrolled back through my training log I can see that two weeks before the injury I was noting that my foot was hurting me, it was likely bothering me a couple of weeks before that, and I was modifying my training plan by taking extra rest days and running easy miles here and there instead of doing a tempo workout or hill repeats. This would have been a great time to take a couple of weeks off for some proper rest. This is also a great example of why it’s useful to keep a training log. It allows you the opportunity to look back at your training and identify what is going well and what is not. 

Currently trying to work on strength and mobility as well as some real life matters that tend to get neglected while all of our efforts are focused on training. 

Thank you to everyone for reaching out to see how I’m doing. You make this difficult time less difficult. ❤️🙏🤗

Hard to believe it’s already been 2 wks since I was deep in the pain cave on Night 2 of the 48Hr race! 

People had said 48Hrs may be the toughest event because you can’t properly sleep if you want to put up big numbers. I already knew how hard 24Hrs is. Doing 24Hr x 2 was scary and overwhelming to think about 🙀.

How would I eat the elephant 🐘🤔? One bite at a time 😋.

We intentionally set up mileage milestones to keep me focused, motivated, and inspired. I kept going and working towards each goal ✅🎉! 

I knew power naps could be a game changer, as they had helped me extend my 24Hr World Record by almost 8km. I put the theory to the test, taking several power naps on Day 1 and again on Night 2 (6-25 min). I would be sore/cold/stiff re-starting- like my body was in a state of rigor mortis 🧟‍♀️. 

I piled on the clothes until I warmed up (10-15 min), re-found my rhythm, and would shed the layers. Thank you to @lululemon for all the great gear to work with 🌧️☀️🩳👚🧥🧢🧤. One of the final naps felt like it “stuck”, and I was refreshed 🧠🔋 (3-4am). I got going again, and I knew I felt mentally strong enough to power through the last 6 hours 👊🏃‍♀️🏃‍♀️🏃‍♀️.

I broke free of the pain cave and became the rocket to the moon, reaching the World Record with under 3 hrs left 🦸‍♀️🚀🌖! 

Mike Dobie graphed my progression (pic 2, green line) with other 48Hr performances. I think it shows the power of micro-sleep for improving performance for 24Hrs and beyond. I didn’t have any hallucinations. I laid down when my brain felt woozy 🤪. 

I stopped for a little bit of Coke, but I don’t personally like taking much caffeine during the night or during the day. Sleep, keeping up the calories (@corosglobal Nutrition timer ⏱️), and staying warm/dry kept the battery charged and motoring along 🔋🏃‍♀️🏃‍♀️🏃‍♀️. 

I’m totally hooked now on the multiday races and already daydreaming about going further- 6 days and beyond 💖!

Launching our first @urbanfitnessretreat with @andrewballpt (and about to have our 7th in a couple weeks time).

Becoming a @lululemon ambassador with a special group of legends

Launching the @everymoveacademy with my partner in crime @_sarahlfit in lockdown which has built in something seriously special.

And to taking two teams of clients to the @turfgames winter festival and having a positive impact on peoples lives all over the world.

It’s been a pretty wild ride over the last 5 and a half years.

But, the thing is, I really do feel like I am only just getting started. 

I know I have so much more to give. 

And I know the @everymoveacademy is going to keep growing and growing.

Here’s to the next 5 and a half years 🏆

3 Steps to repair your relationship with fitness overnight.

1 - Do not workout with the goal to burn the most calories every workout. You will burn out and become discouraged from the lack of progress, fatigue and injuries.

2 - Build a strong foundation - work on your core (not crunches, but bridges, bear planks, front rack squats), stability, balance and mobility. This will set you up for success long term and reduce your risk of injuries, making your fitness journey more enjoyable.

3 - Change they way you view food - it is a source of energy, not a punishment, not a reward. It is what your body needs to workout and recover from working out. Repairing this relationship was the hardest for me. You do not need a detox, you need more water. 

You do not need to workout to lose weight, fit in a certain size of clothing (my sizes vary in lululemon from a 4 to a 10), and you do not need to change your body AT ALL! You can just workout to be healthy and move better.

They can help you unlearn all your bad habits and get in proper alignment (if you surrender and allow them) or you resist them and push them away and you just keep building those same old bad habits and wonder why you never see different results. The reality is even though you may not “need” them, it’s makes practice/life a lot nicer having them around. It can be in power or flow manner where they help you build functional strength or it can be in restorative sense where they help you to settle in and provide comfort; regardless, they add value.

This might sound ridiculous to you, but I am so enthralled with nature and the wild. I live very consciously and intentionally make an effort to lower my impact on the planet. 

Here are some easy & free things you can do:
- Literally unplug all chargers from the wall when they’re not in use.
- Whenever possible, walk or ride a bike instead of driving. Or carpool!
- Be strategic about your errands in a given week. Don’t drive across town 6 times in two days, plan ahead, makes lists.
- Eat less meat and choose local in season produce often.
- Bring your own tote bag Every. Single. Time. You. Shop. Groceries, Walmart, Bloomingdales, tjmaxx, lululemon, CVS, etc…
- We all own them.. USE your nalgene, swell, yeti, corksicle, or any brand water bottles. Breakup with water in plastic.
- When you see random trash on the beach or street, pick it up and throw it away.
- Turn the faucet off while you’re brushing your teeth and don’t turn the shower on until your actually ready to get in. 

You can start small, you don’t have to be a full blow off the grid zero carbon foot print person tomorrow, or ever! 

I’m going to continue to drop little nuggets of eco wisdom throughout April (Earth month). Small changes add up. Do more than nothing 💛🌎

At the start of a new adventure. No idea what was headed our way... All I could see was snow and excitement and James. 💛

And through it all, all the snowy & sunny days that were yet to come… over a decade of good times, hard times, dodgy DIY 😂 and our kiddos, we muddled on through together.

Gaining wrinkles and experience along the way. There’ve been tears (mainly at the dodgy DIY 😝) but God there've been some laughs…

And as I sit in the sunshine now, watching you play football with the boys whilst you have a break from decorating… I know that despite the day not being filled with hearts and romance. It’s been pretty wonderful all the same. The sun’s been shining and we were with our boys. Oat milk latte happily resting on my bump. 

And that seems like a pretty good day to me. 🥰

Now, break times over - there’s another skirting board with your name on it! 😂 💛

Roll on the next chapter… I can’t wait xxx

That's the face of a dog who LOCKED ME OUT OF MY OWN CAR.
.
Yep, gather around friends, it's story time. Jackson takes a daily drive with me in the mornings, shuttling off the tiny humans to school and activities. As I hopped out to take our littlest inside to preschool, this lovable large dog sat on my Lululemon belt bag (The trusty "fanny pack" fad proved to be devil today!). My car locked with it still running.
.
The oblivious dog continued to sit in the front seat, relaxing and enjoying the view while I spastically raced around the car (IN THE POURING RAIN) trying to get him to sit perfectly back on the belt bag, in hopes that a miracle would happen and his tush would magically unlock my car.
.
NOPE. This dog continued to stare off into space as a fellow mom asked if I needed help. She raced me home to grab my extra key, only for me to figure out that THE KEY FOB BATTERY WAS DEAD!
.
Folks, I can't make this stuff up. The same energetic dog was now going on 30 minutes, chilling out in my air conditioned Jeep listening to country music as I scrambled and panicked like the scatterbrained mom I am. Well, I learned something new today: The key fob has an actual key tucked inside!
.
Yes, the same dog who is absolutely wild with energy, the same pup whose strength gave me a massive black eye, just sat there as I open the car door, like I had only been gone a second to drop off the tiny human inside. Turns out...THE DOG WAS SLEEPING SITTING UP. Apparently I bored him to sleep.
.
Moral of the story, mom brain is a real thing. We may look like we have our Sh** together, but it's all an act. Oh, and don't leave your keys in the car where your dog can sit on them and lock the car sparking a massive chaotic chase to get back inside. THE END.
.

Nothing helps me get into more than feeling great in my clothes and the Align pants are my ultimate go to! There’s a trick that makes these the perfect pair of leggings…

Because Aligns have a buttery, soft, dreamy feel they’re not compressive or restrictive. I love this because it’s better for our body and helps our lymphatic system and overall flow! 

However, a softer feel sometimes feels like a looser fit. It feels good to have your leggings hug all the curves and stay in place…so the trick is to size down! I wear my smallest size in my Aligns, where as compression leggings I wear my true size. 

I probably wear my Align leggings 75-80% of the time (Wunder trains come in second for me 😍) so naturally I wore them in my Ambassador shoot. I’m curious what you’re go to style is?

We fired 🔥 our cleaning people. Hear me out. There was a season that it was super helpful. We had 3 little little kids, we both worked full time outside of the house, we were getting a business off the ground and had zero time to keep up with housework. We’ve entered a different season though. 

Our kids are older. They are starting to learn how to care for themselves and take responsibility for their things (phones, chrome books, etc). They are more than capable of contributing to the house in a bigger way and based on the amount of screen time they are abusing…they must be bored. They hit us up for money all of the time…the list of “wants” Macie has at Sephora and Lululemon is insane. It’s time to start teaching them about earning, saving, spending and investing. 

The kids each have a 15 minute chore each day and they get paid at the end of the month. Travis and I took on a little more housework because modeling for your kids is one of the biggest influences on them. At the end of the day, we are trying to raise adults…not kids. 

To my surprise they are actually excited about it. Check out the youth account through Fidelity! They can get cash out, use it as a credit card, and even invest (must be 13). Let me know if you have any questions and I’ll check back in later to let you know if we’re sinking or swimming 🏊‍♂️ 

P.s. so far our house and laundry situation is the best ever. Toilets are getting scrubbed weekly instead of every other week.

People often ask me how I stay inspired. The truth is that I’m not always inspired. I go through highs and lows, in practice, teaching and also in life. I have doubt about what I’m doing, whether practice, teaching or life. Things shift and change, whether it’s me that changes or the world around me that does, and those shifts and changes bring about different experiences. What once felt safe and secure suddenly feels uncertain and dangerous. Sometimes there is pain, grief and loss. And sometimes there is joy, happiness and love. I choose to belief it’s worth it, that I’m here for a reason even if that reason isn’t always so clear to me. I actively look for purpose and meaning even and perhaps especially when things feel random and meaningless. 

I’m sharing this because I want you to see me as I am, human, flawed, stumbling, imperfect. I don’t always feel super inspired about everything. Yoga has been in my life for over 25 years and I’ve maintained a daily practice for over 23 years. It hasn’t been easy, but the journey have given me the tools to find the diamonds in the darkness. 

I’ve talked about a shift in my teaching and it’s hard to put it into words. I am more and more interested in truly supporting sincere seekers on the path. I want to create opportunities for those who might benefit from practicing with me to do just that, practice with me. I want to find ways to give more in ways that matter. I know that the thousands of students all over the world find support for their practice on @omstarsofficial and I am so grateful to the yoga family we are. Stay tuned for more.

⁠
With yoga pants and comfortable athleisure wear at its core, Lululemon certainly benefitted from the home workout and general fitness boom brought about by the pandemic — since 2019 the apparel company’s seen sales more than double, helping to bolster its direct-to-consumer division as customers increasingly move online.⁠
⁠
Stretching⁠
⁠
In that time, Lululemon’s expanded its exercise empire further, slipping into the shoe business, acquiring the at-home fitness product Mirror in 2020, and even introducing a subscription model offering exclusive access to items, fitness classes, and a new app later this year. Stretching out in general seems to come pretty naturally to the company. ⁠
⁠
Revenues at the fitness-focused firm have increased 37% on average each year since 2004, though the last few years have seen the company’s sales figures seriously bulk up. In 2019, Lululemon made just shy of $4 billion in sales, which rose to $6.3 billion only two years later and now sits at a very healthy-looking $8.1 billion for 2022. ⁠
⁠
The company’s financials elsewhere are in good shape as well — thanks to slick marketing and an almost cult-like customer base, Lululemon squeezes out some pretty juicy operating profit margins compared to huge competitors like Nike and Adidas.⁠

It's becoming clear that Lululemon (LULU) burned roughly $500 million in shareholder capital via the ill-timed purchase of the connected-fitness platform Mirror.

Buried in Lululemon's late Tuesday earnings release — which was solid overall and drove shares higher as of Wednesday morning — was a $442.7 million post-tax impairment charge in the fourth quarter related to the Mirror business, which was meant to rival Peloton.

"The overall at-home fitness space remains challenged," Lululemon CFO Meghan Frank said on the earnings call in explaining the impairment. "Mirror hardware sales during the holiday season came in below expectations."
Frank added the business is a "very small portion" of management's five-year plan. After factoring in Lululemon's write-down in Q4 of 2022, the business has now almost been entirely written off.

CEO Calvin McDonald, who has helmed Lululemon for nearly five years (and joined Disney's board in 2021), signed off on the purchase of Mirror for $500 million in June 2020 at a point in the COVID-19 pandemic when valuations for at-home fitness equipment like Pelotons and Tonals were skyrocketing.

As the waning pandemic led to a cooling of the home fitness market, Lululemon unsuccessfully attempted to integrate the Mirror acquisition operationally, culturally, and from a sales perspective. Mirror Founder Brynn Putnam stepped down as CEO in September 2021.

Smiling Helps You Live Longer-

Happy people seem to enjoy better health and longevity, but more research is needed to understand why. Research indicates that happiness could increase lifespan by years—suggesting maintaining a happy, positive mood may be an important part of a healthy lifestyle.
-

Smiling Elevates Mood-

Smiling can also help make you feel happy. Next time you are feeling down, try putting on a smile. There's a good chance your mood will change for the better.

The physical act of smiling activates pathways in your brain that influence your emotional state—meaning that by adopting a happy facial expression, you can "trick" your mind into entering a state of happiness. This affect works whether or not your smile is genuine.
-

Smiling May Lower Blood Pressure-

Smiling could have a beneficial impact on your blood pressure. Laughter specifically seems to lower blood pressure, after causing an initial increase in heart rate and breathing.

While smiling has been shown to lower your heart rate in the face of stress, more research is needed to determine how it reduces blood pressure.
-

Smiling Reduces Pain-

Studies have shown that smiling releases endorphins, other natural painkillers, and serotonin. Together, these brain chemicals make us feel good from head to toe. Not only do they elevate your mood, but they also relax your body and reduce physical pain. Smiling is a natural drug.

“Buy it yourself.” And so she did. 

My 10-year old older daughter started having “caviar” taste this year. She wanted Jordans, Sephora & Lululemon (it could be worse, but still). 

Sure I could buy it all for her….But where is the lesson in that? 

I want her to know this stuff doesn’t come easy. 

That when it “looks easy” for me, it’s bc I’ve been working my 🍑 off for 20+ years. 

I want her to understand that know so she knows what it takes to be successful in life, whatever that means to her. 

When she wanted a $120 sweatshirt from Lululemon, I said: buy it yourself. 

Aside from the fact I don’t think a 10 year old needs a hoodie that expensive, I want to give her the opportunity to see how hard it is to earn a dollar and then decide what makes her happy enough to spend that dollar. 

For the last two months, I watched this girl do loads and loads of laundry, take the garbage out in the dark rain, & unload dishwasher just to earn enough allowance to buy this hoodie. 

Yesterday when she got it, she felt so proud & thanked me lol 

She said - “that felt really good! Now I get why you are so proud for all you have. It feels awesome to go out and get it yourself!”

Yes girl. Yes it does 🤍💫

I’m so proud of her for working hard, setting a goal and achieving that goal. 

Right now, the goal is just a hoodie. But who knows what she’ll strive for in life, knowing that if she puts her mind to it, she’ll find a way.

心身共に全く準備のできなかったレース。
今年に入ってずーっと心ここに在らずなトレーニング…
案の定結果もボロボロ。

少しレースを振り返ってみる👀💡
jogを怠ってポイント練習だけで繋いだレース。
どれだけポイントの質が上がっても、点と点が線となって繋がらなかった感覚。

直前に痛めたふくらはぎが心配でスタートしたレースだったけど、
ふくらはぎの痛みはどこへやら😂
全く痛みは出ず、順調ww
レースもずーっと3'30"を切るペースで進んでいたところ、ハーフ手前でじわじわと差し込みが出始めて、ハーフを通過した時、一気に集中と気持ちがぽきっと折れて、その途端差し込みの痛みが増しきた…
そこからは止まったり歩いたり…
また、走っては歩いて…
23キロくらいのところで、もう辞めちゃおうと初めて本気でレースの棄権を考えるほど気持ちが切れてしまった🙄💦
だけど辞めることはできずとりあえず前へ前へと足を進める🐾

27〜8キロくらいで、差し込みの痛みは緩んできたからまた走り出したけど、前半のオーバーペースなせいで足は完全に売り切れで動かない😂
また止まったり歩いたり、少し走ったりとレースにならないような感じでなんとかゴールまで辿り着けた🤣

現役を引退したはずなのに、走ることを頑張れない自分は、なにもできないように感じて、大きな東京の街にポツンと喪失感を感じたレースだった😂😂😂

終わった後は、悔しさも感じないほどの絶望感だったけど、そもそも練習不足。
やる事をやってないんだなーと大反省🤣

今までは走る事で自分自身を表現してきたけど、今年は仕事で大きく成長できる年にしたい❣️❣️❣️
走ることは辞めないけど、表現方法を変えて成長していきたい😊

それにしても前半のハーフ1°14"02は
予想外過ぎて、驚いた😆👏
こんなに速く走れるんだと自分に驚きと、そんなに速く突っ込んだら、後半激タレするわなと納得笑
1人だけ東京ハーフマラソンになりましたwww🤭

Ep. 196: Alpine Fit/ Jen Loofbourrow // This week Clint and Dawson sat down with Jen Loofbourrow. Jen is the Founder and owner of Alpine Fit. Jen shares some adventure stories and how they guided her professional path to entrepreneurship. 

In her early twenties she fell in love with expeditions kayaking the outer islands of Alaska's southeast coastline. Inevitably, she and her friends experienced variable conditions, sun to rain, and everything from freezing water temps to natural hot springs.

With no access to laundry for weeks at a time, and limited space, she could take only essential basics, and each piece of gear had to perform. She refined and honed her packing list and found substitute products for what she really wanted, which all too often weren't available. 

Since then, she has embarked on many extended traveling and backpacking trips, in addition to the activities she likes to do regularly in her normal life.

Her journey in apparel began as a materials developer at lululemon in Vancouver, then lingerie and swimwear retail store owner in Ireland, and later, a wholesale and operations manager at Swedish women's brand Skhoop in Anchorage, Alaska. These jobs formed building blocks for what she would realize is her passion: making outdoor gear basics for a multitude of adventures and activities, with fabrics she believes in, while being an excellent employer for her dedicated and creative team.

More than that, she knows that every person has unique body characteristics, and that the standard fit offered by most brands does not work for all. At Alpine Fit, they work tirelessly to design and refine products that are offered in twice the fit options, and therefore twice the number of size combinations for more people to be able to find their perfect fit with their clothes.

*️⃣Most asked questions:
.
1️⃣What do you eat? What do you think about Keto and intermittent fasting? 
✅ I am a clean eater, meaning not processed or fried foods. I love fresh fruits and veggies, chicken, fish & nuts. I basically think of foods that grow or were once alive as my go to’s. I am not perfect at this as I have a real sweet tooth, but I do my best. 
I think Keto and intermittent fasting and any other diet may be great for some people for a short time, but for me keeping it simple and clean works best. I eat 5 smaller meals rather than a 3 big meals. I have a protein and carb with each snack and meal so my blood sugar stays level and I don’t get starving and grab the easiest thing which is usually not the best choice. When I feel I am getting off track, eating too much or poor choices I start to track my food and it brings me back. I always suggest this to my clients. *Remember to lose weight you have to be burning more calories than you are eating, so MOVE MOVE MOVE!!

2️⃣How many day a week should I be doing weights? Am I going to bulk up?
✅I recommend getting at least 3 days a week of weights. A good way to break that up is doing, Day 1: Chest, Shoulders, triceps. Day 2: Legs & core. Day 3: Back & biceps. No, you will not bulk up! You will definitely tone up and feel stronger though. 💪🏽 It’s so fun to see my clients feeing stronger and seeing the inches drop off! 

3️⃣How do you stay motivated?
✅I am addicted to how I feel when I workout! I love to feel strong! I am energized and proud of myself. My goal is to live a healthy life and always be able to be active and keep up with my kids. When I feel unmotivated I remind myself how much these things mean to me and how good I will feel once I’m finished. That doesn’t mean if I’m burned out I don’t let my body rest. I always take a rest day during the week and try and get plenty of sleep. 

❤️Exercise is fun and rewarding. Find what you love and you will never regret the lifestyle you will be rewarded with.

Throughout Women’s History Month, we’re spotlighting remarkable women who are cultivating collective spaces across creative industries. Meet Necat Akman—equal parts style maven and star athlete. 🌟
Born and raised in Izmir, Türkiye, where she was once the number one tennis player in the country, Akman is now the designer and Director of Retail for @aarmy; an NYC-based athletic training facility and eponymous sportswear brand known for their collaborations with @fearofgod, @nike, and @lululemon. 

Akman began her career at 21, in production and editing, with the @miamiheat on their series “Inside the Heat.” Working part-time as a sales associate at Ralph Lauren, she eventually became more involved in the fashion world—opening four RRL by @ralphlauren stores, and working with A-list clients like @davidbeckham and @jeremypiven—all before the age of 25. Soon-after, Akman became an image consultant and stylist working with high profile talents like @mslaurynhill, who deemed Akman her “eye in the streets”—appointing her as Creative Manager of the Ms. Lauryn Hill camp. 

Her approach and connections in art, entertainment, and music have successfully attracted a passionate community through her events and styling work. Forever an innovator ♈️ in 2016, she founded @92dreamteamnyc, a branding company specializing in experiential marketing, and in 2020, she launched a swimwear collection, @naeya.us. I am a graphic designer and an artist, but I also had the opportunity to be an ambassador for @lululemon. Random? Not really. Let me explain...
.
In March 2020, I lost $50,000 of work —signed contracts!—over a 5-day period 💩
.
A devastating hit for what was at the time a 1-man business. Especially after having just bought my first house.
.
I was ultimately able to recover and have a fine year. How? Because I was able to pivot away from murals (the majority of the work lost) and into web design, more traditional graphic design, affiliate marketing, lettering, and branding.
.
It was because of my diverse background doing a little bit of everything that I was able to pull through (mostly) unscathed.
.
The creative industry will implore you to niche down. And, I agree, to an extent. However, by embracing the mindset of hybrid professionalism — the idea of working at the intersections of disparate identities — I have not only found more fulfillment in my career but far more success and opportunity.
.
Your career is just a small cog in the wheel of life. This "experience" that we have a privilege to enjoy should be a joy. I am so grateful for the opportunity to implement my disparate interests into this wild career pursuit. Opportunities like my ambassadorship with @lululemon is definitely top of the list.
.
Of course, I can't not acknowledge the network of incredible individuals who made such a partnership possible. You know who you are and I just love ya for it 🥲🫶🏼
.

our bodies N E E D nutrients + fluids…
for strength + endurance during the run, but also to assist with recovery

in general:

🍞 carb UP
carbs fuel the body with glycogen. this fuel is then stored in our muscles, which helps them perform. not having enough carbs will make us feel sluggish + fatigued - the worst!

🍗 pack plenty of protein
protein helps build + repair our muscle tissue. the right amount of protein promotes muscle growth, especially when strength training - the best!

🥜 become friendly with fat
stored fat is an important source of energy for endurance athletes. dietary fats also help us feel more full + absorb vitamins.

🫙lots of liquids
when exercising, our muscles generate heat + we sweat to get rid of it. this loss of fluid needs to be replenished DURING + after a run.
living #thesweatlife

remember, everyone is different. take the time to try different fuel sources, amounts + timing to determine what works best for YOU.

my pre-run go-to:
1. water, ☕️ + more water
2. a piece of toast with almond butter, 🍌 + cinnamon smeared on top

Animal cruelty in fashion is unacceptable and many fashion designers have implemented bans on fur. Recently, fashion brands have moved to become more sustainable and cruelty-free, with designers using bio-materials and leather alternatives such as faux leather, cork, pineapple leather, mushrooms, recycled plastic fibres, waxed cotton, and Piñatex. 

Ethical fashion pioneer @stellamccartney has created a collection without the use of leather, feathers, fur, or any other animal skins, crafted with 80% eco-friendly materials. She is committed to not compromising on either desirability or sustainability and introduced plant-based biodegradable shoe soles in 2012. 

Moreover, she formed a consortium with @kering_official, @adidas, and @lululemon to invest in the development of Mylo, a sustainable material grown from mycelium, the underground root of a mushroom. 

However, the fashion industry still has a long way to go, with more than 40% of the 250 brands assessed as part of Fashion Revolution’s ‘Fashion Transparency Index’ last year having no animal welfare policy in place.

The Common Law Of Life

The tree that never had to fight
For sun and sky and air and light,
But stood out in the open plain
And always got its share of rain,
Never became a forest king
But lived and died a scrubby thing.

The man who never had to toil
To gain and farm his patch of soil,
Who never had to win his share
Of sun and sky and light and air,
Never became a manly man
But lived and died as he began.

Good timber does not grow with ease,
The stronger wind, the stronger trees,
The further sky, the greater length,
The more the storm, the more the strength.
By sun and cold, by rain and snow,
In trees and men good timbers grow.

Where thickest lies the forest growth
We find the patriarchs of both.
And they hold counsel with the stars
Whose broken branches show the scars
Of many winds and much of strife.
This is the common law of life.

Health is not just about what you eat and how you exercise. I talk all the time about what products we use on our skin because our skin absorbs everything it touches. That also goes for clothing.

Polyester is in 80% of the clothes we wear and is even in those expensive brands we love like Lululemon and Vouri. Polyester is essentially plastic and plastics have the unique property to disrupt hormones. Because the plastic molecules resemble hormone molecules, plastic often tricks the body into thinking theres the presence of that hormone. Add tight fitting clothes, heat, and sweat and that process is excellerated. 

Fabrics full of hormone disrupting chemicals to avoid:
 - polyester 
 - acrylic
 - nylon
 - anything with ‘tm’ after it
 
Alternatively, stick to naturally occurring materials:
 - cotton
 - silk
 - wool
 - cashmere
 - linen
 - hemp
 - jute
 - leather
 - fur

These synthetic fabrics are not “good for the environment” because you ARE the environment. What’s good for one is good for both.

The @rivershalfmarathon is my favorite spring time event. Each year I look forward to running this awesome event for a great cause, with the most amazing people. Brrr! 24 hours later, I’m still warming up! 🥶🌬️ 

For 12 weeks I trained for the 13.1, but ran the 5k. Until Saturday afternoon, I planned to run the half. Then around 3pm Saturday, a giant wave of exhaustion hit with some force. I’ve been double clutching it for months now and something told me not to try to power through this one. Part of my work (especially over the past year) has been paying more attention to my intuition, my body, my mind and adjusting accordingly. 🧘🏽💭

Dropping down is not an easy decision, especially when you put in the time, mileage and effort. And, until this year, I would’ve been way too hard on myself to make that decision. Yet, finding acceptance so quickly in all of this, made fun-running & crossing this year’s finish line (29:59 - 4th in my AG) to receive the 5k medal from my beautiful wife, one of my all-time proudest racing moments. Joining @melissachilderswellness with the other finish line volunteers in celebration of so many amazing finishes was the absolute highlight! 🙏🏽🏁🫶🏽

If you take my class with any regularity, you've heard me say--laughter in yoga is good. 😊And this isn't to say we make a joke of the practice; quite the opposite. You might have heard the sentiment, "we take the practice seriously but ourselves lightly." Shannon @getdowndogyoga used to say this all the time and it became imprinted on my brain many years ago. Approach the pose seriously, offer your best, and when you fall out of it--let yourself laugh if that's your inclination. 💗

The reward isn't in the execution of the pose itself, it's in the willingness to show up and learn something through that process. If we allow it, the process will slowly unveil the truth of ourselves, unveil lessons that are far more broad and useful than balancing on our hands or head. So today, I hope your practice leads you to greater lightness of being, greater clarity, greater compassion for all beings, and maybe a little laughter. 💫

打掃 安排位子 走向 淨化環境，

Stoked to get my first win here in Madeira and to share it with @_filipe__ferreira_ 

In all honesty, I hoped to maybe make the podium but really not to blow myself up on the uphill and lose by 20 minutes. That’s what I told my friends the night before.

Today I climbed well and found myself leading from early. It’s an interesting position to be in because it feels like you’re being hunted the entire time. The downhills were fast and I know that’s the strength of the Madeiran’s. I held position till it flattened out and kept my position. 

In the tunnel, I launched and hoped not to hit my head. Knowing that could end in concussion at the pace we were running.

The mountain bike track tested me again, and we were flying. Until I became one with the dirt. Adrenaline propped me up and I kept going.

The last 8km was a true race with @_filipe__ferreira_ 

The downhill speed was hard and fast and my legs nearly turned to jelly on the hike stretch. We agreed to cross the line together. 

Without @_filipe__ferreira_ on my heels today, I know I wouldn’t have run as fast as I did. That’s what I like most about racing, you can go to places you don’t in training. And once you’ve unlocked that new part of yourself, you’ve levelled up.

I’m proud of the small wins and the improvements. On heavy legs and a tired body, some days you don’t imagine you’re improving. With rest and the right race, the truth is revealed.

One month to MIUT, cherishing every moment here.

【#SSW綠色生活】Manduka瑜伽墊環保用一世減浪費 Lady Gaga都愛用

美國品牌，德國製造的Manduka瑜伽墊，是Lady Gaga愛用瑜伽墊，除了是資深瑜伽導師都推介，更有不少專業瑜伽中心都會選用，當中的Pro系列尤其受歡迎。到底為甚麼Manduka連Lady Gaga都用？為甚麼品牌與lululemon會常被互相比較？為甚麼說Manduka可以用一世？

令練習更輕鬆安全
Manduka的Pro系列最受歡迎，厚度達6mm，緩衝力好，耐磨耐用，不易滑動，讓動作更扎實，深受專業導師歡迎，就連在YouTube上擁有1190萬訂閱數的知名瑜伽導師「Yoga With Adriene」也是使用Manduka。

承襲建築美學

THE INTERNET GIVES ME IMPOSTER SYNDROME 👀⁣
⁣
Sometimes I find myself doom-scrolling my feeds, pouring through videos of indoor cycling classes from all over the world, wondering why my classes aren't full like the videos I watch... worrying my classes are too easy compared to the insane choreography you can find in two clicks... comparing my motivation to sound bytes... letting my light dim.⁣
⁣
This isn't healthy. ⁣
⁣
Can those videos be valuable resources and thought-starters? Absolutely. ⁣
⁣
Are those videos accurate reflections of my classes? Most cycling classes? Even accurate representations of the classes that are being filmed? No. ❤️⁣
⁣
So what do I do to come back to reality after doom-scrolling through #SpinTok? ⁣
⁣
I remember what I'm 𝘣𝘦𝘴𝘵 𝘪𝘯 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘭𝘥 at. ⁣
⁣
When I worked for lululemon, we did a leadership workshop where we took the time to figure out what made us "𝘣𝘦𝘴𝘵 𝘪𝘯 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘭𝘥" -- a skill we have that is uniquely ours because of who we are and where we came from. At first, I laughed off that workshop thinking it was ridiculous that I could be best in the world at anything.⁣
⁣
But looking back, it makes complete sense. ⁣
⁣
I am best in the world at making people feel calm, comfortable, and welcome in spaces that previously intimidated them. I am best in the world at creating special moments that go beyond fitness within the sacred walls of the studio. I am best in the world at teaching a class like me. ⁣
⁣
I do not have to be mind-blowingly innovative, Ted Talk-worthy, or teacher of the masses to be best in the world.⁣
⁣
I am enough simply because I am me.⁣
⁣
And you are enough simply because you are you.⁣
⁣
Love you, mean it. 🤟🏼⁣
⁣

지난 세계여성의날을 맞이하여 저의 이야기를 나눌 수 있는 기회가 있었어요. 
나다움,자신감, 성장과정에 대한 주제로 삶에 대한 진솔한 이야기를 들려드리고자 고민했고, 인터뷰의 질문에 대해 저의 답을 적어보는 과정에서 다시한번 스스로 나를 알아가는 기회의 시간을 가질 수 있었어요 ☺️ 

여러 멋진 앰배서더분들과 인터뷰를 함께 나눌 수 있어 영광이었고, @lululemonkr 피드에 담기지 못한 저의 이야기를 조금 더 나누고 싶었어요. 

다시금 제 자신을 알아가고 탐험할 수 있는 기회를 준 @teamparnas 룰루레몬파르나스팀에게도 감사를 전합니다🤍

▪️나 자신의 어떤점이 좋은가요?
-열린마음? 잘 포용하는 점이라 생각해요. 
많은 다양성을 인정하고 모두가 가지고 있는 가능성에 더 집중하면 결국 그 안에서 함께 조화로워지더라구요. 

포용하는 자세는 결국 긍정적인 마음으로 이어지고, 저의 삶의 원동력이 되어주고있어요. 

▪️진정한 ‘나 다움’이란 무엇이라 생각하나요? 
-‘누구에게 보여지기 위한 내가아닌, 스스로 삶의 주체가 되어 살아가는것 ‘ 이라 생각해요. 

고유한 삶은 능동적이고 주체적인 움직임을 만들어내고, 긍정적으로 사고하는 힘을 줄 수 있어요. 
그 생각들을 적극적으로 표현해보면 어떨까요? 말로도 몸으로도요 ! 

춤을 추거나, 달리거나, 운동을 하거나 하는 모든 움직임의 표현들이요. 특히 몸의 표현이 많아질수록 더 즐겁고 역동적인 삶을 살 수 있지 않을까요? 

▪️’나 다움’을 지키기 위한 팁 
-먼저 자신을 아끼고 돌보세요.
꿈을 향해 달려가는 나, 오늘의 약속을 해낸 나, 어떤 모습의 나여도 스스로에게 하루에 한번 따뜻한 응원을 보내기 ! 
다독이고 격려하며 성장하는 나자신을 만날 수 있을거에요.

▪️다른 여성들에게 신체뿐 아니라, 마음과 관계까지 건강한 삶, 웰빙의 삶을 지켜가기위해 조언해주고 싶은것이 있다면? 
- 목표를 이루어가는 과정은 결국 반복되는 도전과 반복되는 실패의 연속으로 쌓아가는거라 생각해요. 
‘몸’ 이라는 말은 모으다라는 명사형이라고 해요. 
삶의 경험을 모으고 담는 내 평생동반자인 몸을 행복하게 하는 습관은 결국 웰빙라이프에 한단계 더 다가가는 경험을 줄거에요 ! 

여러분이 생각하는 진정한 ‘웰비잉’ 이란 무엇인가요? 
진정한 ‘나다움’ 에 대해 , 스스로를 즐겁게 탐험하는 시간이 있으신가요?
 지금부터라도 우리 함께 즐겁게 움직이고, 알아보고 탐험해 보아요 ✨

It was really fun to reflect on my last ten years during this IWD panel with @lululemonsg & @voguesingapore !⁣

I started out young, doubtful of my own abilities and potential. I was also the youngest employee and the least fit of the small team we began with. So I had a lot to prove to myself, in order to gain respect from others. My initial instructor training was pivotal - I learnt that if you don’t believe that the end of the tunnel exists, you’ll never arrive. ⁣
⁣
I learnt to never sell yourself short, or to allow yourself to fail before you even finish. From then on, I’ve been able to unlock many challenges along the way not just fitness-wise, but business-wise. I’ve learnt to not just be more assertive, definitive and confident, but also more forgiving and compassionate with myself when things go south. ⁣
⁣
How you stay composed during tough times won’t define you, they refine you. ⁣
⁣
A journey exists inside of all of us, albeit having different twists and turns. Sweat and movement is a powerful activity that supports us in our path to success. ⁣
⁣
lululemon celebrates how we can all look and feel our best not just today, but everyday. Getting into your own confidence is central to wellbeing, and I believe that being comfortable in your own skin and simply being yourself is way more effective than trying to prove you’re important. Last year was challenging for Farfetch, but there was at least one bright spot for the company.⁠
⁠
Farfetch’s app was its “most profitable and fastest-growing channel,” Stephanie Phair, group president, said on the company’s earnings call in February.⁠
⁠
Companies such as Nike and Levi’s have also pointed to their apps as key drivers of digital sales. For fashion retailers, an app that gives them real estate on a consumer’s phone screen and a direct line of communication through push notifications is enticing. Consumers can check their devices more than 50 times a day. More and more often, they’re doing so to shop. The share of US retail sales happening via mobile is forecast to reach 8.7 percent in 2026, according to Insider Intelligence, up from just 4.1 percent in 2019.⁠
⁠
So should every brand have an app?⁠

Get rid of lower back pain by getting STRONG 💪🏽

If lower back pain and flare ups is a thing for you, consider working on hip strength/activation. This can make a big difference in providing more stability for the pelvis and prevent the lower back from taking more load/force. 

Here are some exercise ideas targeting hip strengthening. For all of these be sure to ENGAGE THE CORE to prevent the spine from moving

1. Single leg hip bridge off bench - targets glutes and hamstrings

2. Hip thrust off bench - glutes

3. Wall mountain climber with band - hip flexors 

4. Wall clams - lateral glutes. Make sure to keep your foot flat on the wall and lean forward/hinge 

*these are more appropriate for chronic lower back pain (not acute/new).

In 2020 @yo_mk, @mo_on_the_run and I held our first IWD community run. We wanted to foster a welcoming space to bring women of all run experiences together to share our love of this sport and how it can really build and support community. 
…..
Pandemic hit shortly after and we took it virtual in 2021 with an incredible panel chat around mental health and running. And then life hit and we took a pause in 2022.
…..
This year, with Mo off crushing the Tokyo Marathon, we recruited an all-star, @tomatotown, to join our team to help curate an art run. 
…..
We wanted our run to feature inspiring artwork created by women and wanted celebrate themes of community, bravery, disruption and empowerment. To talk about equity and share important spaces in our city that have been used for rallies and marches that impact women’s lives and women’s rights. ✊🏽
…..
Thank you to @parkdaleroadrunners, @lululemon and @eastboundbeer for supporting our run.  Partnerships like this are so appreciated. We kept it grassroots and were really blown away by the support. Meeting all the runners who came, bringing partners, friends, kids and dogs, old friends and new, was exactly what we envisioned. Thank you to the crews and run community members who shared our eventbrite, and THANK YOU to the runners who came and shared your day with us. Heart was full of gratitude!! 
…..
Thank you @misterhawaii for always supporting what we do and running intervals to take photos of our run! 📷🫶🏽
…..
Thank you MK and Karolina for being incredible event partners. Grateful for you both. 🖤🖤🖤 Parkdale Roadrunners is doing a donations drive all of March for Sistering, to help women leaving violent situations at home. Physical donations every Tuesday at their run. Also accepting financial donations. Please reach out to them for detailed info.

Neben den Kursen kannst Du unseren Vorträgen lauschen, rund um das Thema Wohlbefinden. Der zweite Vortrag dreht sich um Ayurveda, ein traditionelles indisches Heilsystem, das sich auf die Harmonisierung von Körper, Geist und Seele konzentriert.

I’m thrilled to announce Yuja Soul: Yoga for Black Women will continue in community with @lululemon with monthly rituals being held at the SoHo Loft location!

The March ritual is one week away.  All Black Women are invited to join. Head to the link in my bio to register. 🖤✨

Yuja Soul: Yoga for Black Women
✨ Nourishing the Inner Child
✨ journaling • somatics • yoga • rest

✨ Friday March 17, 6:30pm - 8pm
✨ lululemon SoHo Loft (520 Broadway, NYC)
✨ suggested donation: $5 - $15  per person

Many of the patterns, wounds, stories and sense of self we currently carry are imprints that date back to infancy and childhood.

This Yuja Soul: Yoga for Black Women New Moon Workshop is a space dedicated to meeting and tending to the Inner Child. This workshop consists of Somatic Experiencing journaling and Yoga focused at the spine, the center from which all movement radiates and the housing of the nervous system which receives initial patterns and imprints during childhood and development. 

Students will be invited to a meditation, specially designed to cultivate awareness and connection to the Inner Child, and affirm our ability to heal in alignment with the New Moon lunation. Somatic work and Yoga practice will end in Restorative holds before rest.

This workshop is open to all Black Women at all practice levels.

Be sure to bring a journal and pen.  Mats and props will be provided to support your practice and rest. 

Head to the link in bio to join us. 
See you soon. 

Yours,
-Tonie

I read a “day in the life” piece about @calvinmcdonald’s (CEO of @lululemon) which nearly sent me over the edge. What was meant to be insightful/inspirational (he works our twice a day, takes kids to school, has a super regimented skin + diet plan AND looks rested AND is running a multi- billion dollar company + 10 triathlons) send me into a death spiral of questioning career/life choices specifically regarding my daily water intake (who the f— drinks 64 oz?? Like, how?) + non sleep I get. As I angrily stomped back from the gym, I realized McDonald has one thing not mentioned in this piece: he was gifted the time to accomplish all of this. How? He prob makes his goals a priority AND THEN ASKS FOR THE TIME to make it happen from his spouse, kids, colleagues, etc. So in honor of a late #internationalwomensday post, I want everyone to ask for the time. From your spouse, sig others, family, friends, bosses. Get specific. And the hype girl shiz is great, but real support is giving the overachieving big dreamer women in your life the gift of time to accomplish greatness. Take on more kid related stuff, stupid stuff like buy groceries or STFU if your roommate needs to do a Zoom call in the middle of the night with the chairman in Japan (or maybe get her snacks if she is working late). And ladies, if your family, friends, husbands, wives, girlfriends, bosses give the extraordinary gift of time, organize and execute your plan. Remember to say thank you. Nothing is worse than zero appreciation + wasted opportunities. On that note, here is a “by the numbers” on women in leadership roles. And H/t to @averyfrancis for originally posting this image (source unknown). It’s amazing how hair plays such a huge roll in all this boy/girl stuff. I spend so much time and energy on it. I was chatting with one of my besties @solireid yesterday and she said all women do which kind of surprised me but really shouldn’t have. This western ideal of women having luxurious thick hair on top of their heads and being hairless from the neck down is obviously unnatural and for most women impossible. It’s also leaked into male cultural norms too. The Adonis with laser cut abs and a lions mane. Definitely a fragmentation with men though. Grizzly bears, bald sex symbols, and dad bods are everywhere if not the large majority. 
A few weeks back I was chatting with a female friend at the gym and she mentioned how she was getting some facial hair and wanted it removed desperately. I know how much I worked on having mine removed. 40 hours of electrolysis and a dozen laser sessions later and more than 99.9% of it is gone. Thankfully. I still shave my entire body. I’m averse to any of it. A lifetime of social programming has ensured that. 
These days, I see tons of men with shaved legs and arms, in the gym at least. But still likely very faux pas for most. Bodybuilders have been doing it for decades. 
On top, hair is a big deal. Definitely less so for men, but I’m sure many agonize about it anyways. 
For me, I’ve had three different procedures, hairline advancement and 2 hair transplants. Even now, I can’t help but spend countless hours thinking about it. I also constantly look at other women’s hair and think about how beautiful it all is. Lol 
All this for silly little keratin helix strings. Lol

One of the best pieces of advice I can give someone about training… JUST SHOW UP!
👇🏾
One of the biggest questions I get asked as a trainer and athlete is how I stayed motivated. What I always tell people is that I try to stay consistent and JUST SHOW UP. And although it sounds incredibly basic (something I’m known for), it’s better than doing nothing. Although I may not crush every workout, showing up and doing something helps me stay consistent and pushes me closer to my goals.
👇🏾
A prime example of this was doing the @crossfit Open this year. I usually do it with my SCORCHED crew for accountability and that extra push but was unable to.
👇🏾
I was fully ready to not even attempt it. I didn’t have my group, rugby had just started, I was tired, it didn’t fit into my training, I’m too busy… these were thoughts that came to mind. 
👇🏾
But then I thought about how I would feel a week/month from now and how disappointed I would be in myself. Although I don’t train exclusively in CrossFit, I do mix it into my workouts and have been participating in the Open for 4 years.
👇🏾
Although I didn’t do as well as I wanted and was pissed that on the first workout my score was deducted by a third (because they said the didn’t see me measure the wall ball height even though it was marked, but I’m not bitter 🤣), I was proud of myself for completing it. I may have not had the best workouts but I know I got better physically and mentally tougher because I SHOWED UP. #drobfitness #crossfit #crossfitopen #crossfitopen2023 #lululemon #lululemonambassador #thesweatlife #fitnessmotivation #showup

I asked Andy to take this picture of me the other day as the dogs were coming to greet me. The moment I put my shoes on they are right here with me ready to go play! I wanted this picture of me and my fur babies.

Then I started looking at it. I'm glad I had him take this picture. Let's face it ladies physical appearance is something we can all struggle with at times. I've always been active and I have always tried to take care of myself. Did you know when Andy and I started dating I was 88-90lbs? I hardly ate and any exercise I did was cardio. Now I weigh between 115-116lbs. I eat donuts, I drink wine, we eat out 4-5 times a week, I snack at 1am, I eat tacos, burgers, fries, you name it. 

One thing that has tremendously helped me was being consistent and doing things in moderation. Be consistent with your activity levels. Go for a walk, run, go to the gym, get your sun and fresh air. Eat the things you love, enjoy that cake at your kids birthday party, and have some wine with your man and do all of this in moderation. I’m far from a planner. Some nights we’re in bed at midnight other nights it’s 4am and we get 3 hours of sleep. You don’t have to live this crazy strict uneventful life. You have to enjoy some of it!

And ladies here me when I say that there is no perfect time to start. Start today taking control of your health.
