Visibility vs Invisibility. The shift has been profound. I went from feeling nearly invisible to highly visible. If women are looking at men, it’s done covertly. Most men it seems are not that sly. Mind you, neither are older women it seems. Interestingly, most older dudes have learned a slightly more subtle ogling. Lol. 
Sometimes, I revel in this visibility. I have tons of sexual energy, some on purpose and some rather unintentional. So when I want to be seen, I get what I want. The tiny clothes I wear don’t hurt either. Or was it it the whip n my hand? 🤔 
Sometimes though, I wish I could snap my fingers and vanish. A recent example was at an adults play centre where I garnered a bakers dozen of onlookers while I was busy. Then got told by different people how they enjoyed the show. Like, it wasn’t a show. Argh. 
It’s not like I have a neon sign with arrows pointing at me floating above me, but the shift is stark. All of a sudden, I find myself analyzing my movements. Am I fidgeting? Do I have bbq sauce on my shirt from the nuggies I ate earlier?
It is at once empowering and causes me fits of anxiety. Without question though, being highly visible is better than being invisible.  In the end, I often think back to what @theoliviabraddock said that we were made to stand out. I can fight it or I can let it shine. I’ll try to let it shine.

* 中游：纖維產品(人造/天然)、紡紗、織布
* 下游：包含染整、成衣業與其他居家織品業。
⭐三雄雖然都是紡織企業，但是生產業務稍微有差異喔！
以下為三雄主力產品～
儒鴻（1476)運動機能

📌紡織三雄基本介紹

📌儒鴻（1476)
⭐儒鴻(1476)專精於功能性彈性圓編針織布料及成衣，具有垂直整合的製造能力，包含織布、染整、定型及
成衣製造。
⭐主要客戶：Nike、Lululemon、Under Armour等。

📌聚陽（1477)
⭐聚陽(1477)為流行成衣整合製造商。提供客戶一站式
採購服務，包含了產品設計、 快速打樣與原物料整合
等服務，協助客戶快速因應流行趨勢。
⭐主要客戶：GAP、Uniqlo、H&M、 ZARA、Target等。

📌廣越（4438)
⭐廣越(4438)為成衣大廠，主要生產高階羽絨衣與樹酯棉衣(合成纖維外套)，生產基地位於中國、越南、約旦、羅馬尼亞，羽絨成衣年出貨量為全球第一大廠
⭐主要客戶：Adidas、Patagonia、North Face(VF集團)、Nike等。

📌紡織三雄股利大PK

⭐紡織三雄屬於傳統產業，並且為勞力密集業，故常往人工便宜處設廠，例如：越南、印尼等地。

【紐奧良：杜蘭大學】

杜蘭大學（Tulane University）位於紐奧良市區，
雖然這名字在台灣人眼裡很有趣，
但杜蘭大學號稱「南方常春藤」，
在美國排名也是有進前50名的～

賈老師說像這樣的學校特別重視大學部學生，
私立、排名中上，通常是有錢人家孩子來讀的，
畢業後就業也算不錯。

走在校園中，天氣舒適真是南方一大優勢，
建築有古典也有現代，更好看的是學生，
好多青春洋溢的女大學生呀～

以商學院聞名的杜蘭大學，女生佔多數也不奇怪。
在校園逛，整體女學生跟芝加哥大學很不同，
到處都是穿著 Lululemon、全套蘋果設備，
配戴低調大牌首飾的女孩子，精緻漂亮。

芝加哥大學在期中這個時間點，
大學生看起來都像剛從地獄裡爬出來…
（然後發現前方不遠處又一個地獄…）

走累了，在學生聚集的廣場上休息，
不知道能不能直接融入女大生的行列呢？（誤）

I typically practice everyday.  Sometimes I forget my dristhi, sometimes I have remind myself to “engage” my bandhas, but I am ALWAYS
“present” in my practice.  Being “present” is one of the most important lessons I’ve learned from my yoga studies.To be present is not easy to do. 

I think of my practice as a moving meditation. On my own, I am guided by memory, breath, gaze, and when I’m led by my teacher, I am graced by her guidance.  I practice daily and I practice for my wellness.  I try to do the best I can every time I come to the mat. I acknowledge how my body feels, and the impact of those feelings on my ability to explore different asanas on any given day. I’m never looking for perfection, just trying to practice with ease; experiencing the harmonious balance of sthitau/sthira, yatnah (yatno=effort), and sukham.  HOWEVA, 
I try to spend time doing my least favorite poses like garbapindasana and kukutasana  because working on them teaches me patience and grace. Practicing these poses reminds me of my courage and helps me to find stillness. But Lord have mercy,  the  position of my hands  is not always in the “official” place lol. Woo ooo wee!  I think I’m in what the great Krishnamacharya described as the Sthiti krama  phase of life. FOR  REAL!😉😁
I won’t get all yoga philosophical, but I will say that over the last year, my sadhana has truly been a sanctuary and healing space❤️‍🩹 I’m grateful for abhyasa (practice) and vairagya (detachment) and their  place in my yoga practice and my life beyond the mat. By the way, I may not look like it, but I’m having fun. 😁

To ‘Die’ is to be ‘Reborn.’

When you’re truly changing, it is as if a part of you is dying and it’s trying to fight for its life..

And that’s because that part of you IS fighting for its life.

It’s as if our ego identities are given more life through our personality and our actions, and so when we want to shed an ego identity in hopes of growth, it fights for survival - and that’s why we may feel confused, sad, or even depressed because we are literally grieving a part of us that we have been connected to for so long.

Even when we can see and feel that the future looks bright when we grow into this new version of ourselves, we still may feel down for a period.

So..

..THE 🔑 thing to remember then, is when you’re feeling that grief, sadness, or depression, you are literally being reborn. These feelings are a part of that process - to ‘die’ is to be ‘reborn.’

& If we continue giving focus and energy to the NEW us, we eventually start to settle in nicely, and that outdated version of us sheds & becomes just a memory that reminds us why we were supposed to grow in the first place.

We are - EXACTLY - where we are meant to be. Right now. Breathe into it. Lean into it..

& keep trusting.

savor the struggle. find delight in beginnings. acknowledge a season that will be gone before you know it. 

I drive a lot. like many, many hours a week. while most of my miles on the road are spent tuning into podcasts or singing along to a playlist, there are moments where I zone out and fall into my deepest thoughts. that very thing happened on my drive home from Gallup this week and I realized that I am at a place in my career with a new drug that I will never be in again. a few years down the line it will be fully launched and the (hard!) journey to get there will be behind us. I have since been reflecting on the exact moment we are in and appreciating each incremental step we have taken and will take to get to the end point. 

then this morning I was going through my running shorts to pick an outfit for this weekend and unfolded my very first pair of @lululemon shorts. I remember when I was a brand new runner and only wore these shorts for races, washing them with extreme care. I thought about those first days of running and how frustrating it felt to not enjoy most of the my runs. I wish I had embraced the suck of those early days a bit more and acknowledged my incremental gains as I started running with friends, finding more motivation to get out the door. I will never be a brand new runner again, but I can encourage those who want to start logging miles to stick with it and appreciate the journey to a point where you crave a run! 

I was lucky enough to share these thoughts with my lululemon fam during a team sweat this morning and they graciously indulged me in a 10 minute run after! most of them are self-identified non-runners and I’m optimistic I can sway at least one of them to the dark side 😉

I am going to be spending more time living in the moment going forward. I have spent 35 years reaching for the next step, rushing my college experience along, anxious to start a career, wanting to get to the finish line of any experience as quickly as I can. so here’s to savoring the struggle, taking in the full experience - the highs and the lows, and knowing the finish line will always be waiting. 🤍✨

The hardest part of running in these conditions: getting out the door. 

Sometimes the latch is frozen … I jest. It’s because I don’t wanna. -37c this am which translates to cold AF no matter what language you speak. 

I’m asked all the time how I deal with sweating while running in this kind of cold. I do still sweat. It’s hard to believe that’s even possible.  Here’s a breakdown of my layers today: 

*2 long sleeve smart wool tops
*Gortex NorthFace Jacket (new to me this winter and I swear by this thing.  Last winter I’d wear a puffy jacket and it would be soaked in sweat. Literally. It wasn’t good) 
* @lululemon mapped out tights and a pair of lined dance studio pants over top. Pretty much what I wear for -25c to -40 c. Beyond that I break out my snowboard pants.) 
*smartwool socks
*my regular runners with all the vents taped up with gorilla tape a few screws for traction 😂🤷🏻‍♀️🫶🏼 (you still love me tho) 
*Columbia mitts with hot paws inside
* @runlikeagirl_ca toque 
* today I had on my buff with a hole so I could stick my tongue out at the neighbours but I never saw any. I do have a really great gortex mask for this kind of cold. 
*head lamp is petzel. 

Just remember: often times, in training, we’re going to come up against a lot of things we don’t really like, we’re going to have to get uncomfortable. A lot. We’re going to have to get good at suffering. That’s the name of the game in ultras. Right?  Get the gear. Be safe. Be smart. Do the work! Do you have any other questions? Ask away! I’m an open book! (No I won’t marry you or but I may consider selling my dirty socks. Races are expensive … 😂😂) Here’s to a brand new week! Love ya!

The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali teaches us that "Sthira Sukham Asanam" which translates to "Asana is a steady and comfortable posture." 

As a yogic guide, I have an idea of the deeper meaning to this sutra. It is not just about finding a physical position, but also about finding balance and ease in all aspects of our lives.

In our practice, we strive to find stability in our poses while also allowing for ease and comfort. This same principle can be applied to our daily lives. We must strive for balance in all aspects - work and play, effort and ease, stability and flexibility. By finding this balance, we can experience true contentment and joy.

The lululemon website says "Our core values of personal responsibility, entrepreneurship, honesty, courage, connection, fun, and inclusion are lived by our people every day and are at the heart of our unique company culture. Life is funny. Sometimes when you think that you might be capped at your extraordinary experiences - you are gifted new humans into your life that bring you joy, fire and hope. After Lululemon stock (LULU) ripped over the past five years, with shares rising more than 285%, one Wall Street analyst says it's time to reset the lofty expectations for the athleisure retailer.⁠
⁠
Shares of the company fell around 1.8% as of midday trading.⁠
⁠
“This past year, our biggest concern on LULU has been the bullish expectations of perpetual 20%+ top line growth,” Bernstein analyst Aneesha Sherman wrote in a note to clients on Tuesday. “Now, with pent-up demand running out, a more cautious [North America] consumer, higher promotions, and new categories too small to offset a softer core business, it’s time for that reality check.”⁠
⁠
Sherman downgraded Lululemon stock to Underperform and slashed its price target to $290, more than $25 lower than where shares closed on Monday.⁠

TRX X Kettlebell Single Bridge Hold Press 🔥 

Taking inspiration from the amazing @billmaeda for this one 🙌

I LOVE a Push and Pull exercise because of the anti-rotation work required to perform the move ⛓

This one in particular works:

🟡 Grip Strength
⚫️ Core (anti-rotation)
🟡 Single Glute & Hamstring activation
⚫️ Single Pec & Tricep
🟡 Shoulders (both pulling & pushing)
⚫️ Hip stability

Here’s how you do it 👇

1️⃣ Set the TRX straps to super short so you can get under the anchor point, and change them to single strap mode

2️⃣ Hold the single TRX handle with your left hand and place BOTH feet on the floor on front of you

3️⃣ Grab the KB and place it in the ‘rack’ position then raise your left left out straight

4️⃣ Drive the KB up above the chest whilst keeping your hips stable then return to the ‘rack’ position

Repeat this 6-8 times on your left & right side 👊

I used the 16Kb kettlebell in this video, so give it a try yourself and let me know how you get on 💪

Over a decade ago a mentor (🐼) told me to ditch this idea that yoga is only for the studio. He told me if I really wanted to teach then the location didn’t matter. So I taught at bike shops, retail stores, the beach, Lake Michigan 🏄🏽‍♀️, parks, a few foreign countries, farmers markets, a horse farm, Raya’s nursery… the list goes on. All of this is to say that how we practice isn’t defined by where it happens, though the space could be a catalyst for something beautiful. Next Sunday I’m teaching a public class at a dance studio and I’m so fhaking excited! The hope is that this accessible and inclusive practice becomes more consistent so [WE] can move and grow together. 📷 @ssfoto x @lululemon

Meet our Member, Kaitlyn! 🤗

She joined PB LS right after the new year looking for a low impact workout that was easy on her joints and wanted to feel better overall.

Just a little over two weeks later, she’s attending classes every day, sometimes even doubling.

As a paramedic for the St. Matthews Fire & Rescue, she works 12 hours on night shift and lifts people along with her supply bag and monitors; which she shared, are pretty heavy - so she’s excited to be gaining some upper body strength! 🚑 🚒 

Kaitlyn shared that she loves that our studio schedule works well with her schedule because of our flexible class times and variety of classes. She’s already taken all 4 formats and Empower is her favorite; Reform being a close second.

With 12 Classes under her belt, already completing the “First 10 Challenge” and earning her free pair of sticky socks, her next stop is our 50 Class Milestone!

She loves shopping our retail and her favorite purchases so far have been her 2lb Pink @bala weights and red lululemon align leggings! She’s referred 2 friends so far and excited for them to join her for classes.

Advice to a new member: “Keep coming to class daily, it’ll help you grasp the technique quicker!” - Kaitlyn

I usually don’t post #tbt photos, however, I wanted to do this today because I wanted to have a little IG TED talk about the evolutions our bodies experience.

On the left, it was 2007 and I was 17 years old. I had a super flat stomach, only did running as a sport, and would constantly complain that my legs would never fit pants smaller than a size 6. I was always a 6 during high school because I ran all year long to just stay in shape. Throughout this time, I didn’t really lift weights because pop culture would just expose really thin women on magazine spreads, movies, etc (which I still admire to this day). I did eat whatever I pleased though and would still maintain my shape .

Flash forward to 2022, which is the photo on the right of me as a 32 year old. I actually took this after I trained last month in December. I’ve been weightlifting since 2016, got back to doing some drills I did back when I did gymnastics as a kid, box, and got back to running (little by little). I also have some more muscle definition, especially around my arms and stomach is still flat. My body also went through some fluctuations between age 27 to 29 because I went through what I call “my almost 30 crisis” and had a pretty crazy relationship with food because I was really over eating sweets due to the stress. Nowadays, I’m a size 8/9, I train hard, still eat things I enjoy in moderation, and wear the clothes that I love. 

Moral of the story is that I learned to embrace my hour glass/athletic shape along with the fluctuations my body went and goes through. I didn’t want to continue with that stigma pop culture instilled in me as a kid…don’t get me wrong though, I do love pop culture because I utilize references for my work. To me, just being “YOU” is the real deal, especially for your mental sanity. 

Just love and appreciate your bodies in every shape and form. That’s the beauty of it all. 

Of course, I gotta throw in that my jeans in 2007 were @hudsonjeans and my top was @luckybrand. For 2022c I’m wearing @lululemon aligns and a fun workout tank that says Leg Day.

ARE YOU paying the mortgage on a house you hope triples in value, so you become a paper millionaire but now some developer has gone and ruined it by attempting to build social and affordable housing nearby?

There’s only one thing for it and that’s to fire up the residents WhatsApp, call on your solicitor neighbours to drafts an objection which doesn’t directly spell out how much you hate the heroin addicted dole merchants that will surely buy up these units which are retailing at a mere €450,000.

But what happens if you don’t have a solicitor to call on and this is your first objection rodeo? Simple, just pepper your objection with some of these fool proof phrases which will win over local planning officials:

‘Severely denuded’

No someone isn’t strolling around in the nip, denuded is fancy middle-class objection talk for ‘these working-class types will ruin the area’.

‘Visual impact’

Yes, dole claimants are ugly and a penance to look at but you’re more implying that seeing new buildings of any kind can basically cause cancer of the eyes.

‘Lack of amenities’

Code for ‘we’ll need a methadone clinic here in 5 years if you let these retrobates in’.

‘Accent’

This new development would impact on the light shone on Ireland’s 47th oldest surviving mid-height ash tree planted between the years 1986-1992 in an urban area with populations greater than 10,000 people, and we can’t destroy our ancient heritage like that.

‘Tenor of the area’

As much fun as you saw me having this weekend, on the inside, it was game face. I was locked in heading into Sunday. I felt like I had an even better training season than last year. Felt like it was all the makings of hitting a time goal that escaped me last year. 
.
Unfortunately things didn’t go my way. I was cruising the first 17 then all of a sudden I wasn’t. Tried to shorten the stride and before I knew it, I had to listen to the body and walk. There’s nothing more defeating in running then having to walk or even stop and stretch and I did a ton of that from mile 18 to the finish line.
.
As I saw Plan A, Plan B, and eventually Plan C become unattainable, it became all heart and a mental exercise to get to the finish line as quickly as possible. 3:40:14 for marathon # 3. Was it the temps and humidity? Probably. But could I have done something different? Probably.
.
Disappointed yes. Ready to try it again next year?..absolutely. Each marathon teaches you something and gives you something you didn’t have before…experience. #redemptiontour2023 didn’t end the way I wanted but #destination26point2 starts today…ehhh maybe tomorrow lol, cause my legs are still sore

Forgive.  Forgiveness is powerful.  It is healing.  It builds strength 💪🏽.

✨
When I find the courage to admit my mistakes, to apologize where necessary, and to forgive myself, I build something inside of me that prepares me to better meet my next challenges.  Finding that courage is tough.  Apologizing is hard.  And forgiving myself is a process…
✨
I love this photo because it was a moment where I completely forgave myself and enjoyed a beach I had never heard of— Contadora Island in the Pearl Islands.  A beach run and splash in the surf I will never forget.  It took a helicopter to get there, and a whole lot of courage to wear the bikini you can’t even see 😂🙌🏽. I had a great weekend, but I found myself picking on my weak areas as a coach and a mom.  So I’m channeling the energy in this photo to remind myself— I’ll learn from my mistakes and I’ll be stronger tomorrow ❤️. Wishing you all an amazing week full of forgiveness and strength!

𝘿𝙚𝙖𝙧 2022, 

I have learned more about myself in this year than any other time in my life. It has been both an incredible and tumultuous 12 months. 

To me, January is more a month of reflection rather than the implementing of resolutions.

A time where I can really sit back and reflect on what has changed in the year (the good, the bad, the uneasy, the incredible, the uncomfortable, the goals, success, failures, relationships, work, health, life, family, and the balance within myself mentally and physically). 

The long-term life goals I have made, have not changed. But the process of getting there has. 

A few things to ask this January. 

What steps have I taken to progress? What could I have done differently? Did something I was worried/anxious about, matter in the end? What have I accomplished? 

I plan to work hard and succeed but also have another year of trials and errors as I continue my endeavours. -We are never too old to learn. 

My Mental Health was incredibly challenged especially this past year. And I want to thank my partner for keeping me grounded and sane. It has not been an easy year. But we got through it. To my dear friends (whom I can count on my fingers) for the support and reality checks I often needed. To my family for always telling me exactly how it is. Sometimes the truth hurts and sometimes it doesn’t. But knowing and accepting it will only help you understand and move forward. 

Like my mom always tells me. Every day is a New Years, a Christmas, a birthday -A CELEBRATION. Each new day is a day to start working towards yourself and your goals. Don’t wait.

1. Accountability partner (@trasayaa & @hope_fit0)

In 2022, I pushed myself out of my comfort zone & got in my best shape. 

Here’s what I did…

WEIGHT TRAINING + PROGRESSIVE OVERLOAD
4-5 days/week, I lift weights following a progressive overload approach… it’s the best for building muscle & shedding fat. I used my Weight Training Plans the entire year & am doing the new Q1 edition now

SUPPLEMENTAL CARDIO
I add in 60 mins (when maintaining) or 90 mins (when cutting) of cardio per week. This helps increase my overall calorie burn. I like running & the stair master best. 

MACRO APPROACH
By far, the greatest factor is tracking nutrition to ensure I was in a calorie deficit. I used my Macro Book to figure out my numbers & the cut protocol to know what I had to eat to lose. IT WORKS! I lost 10 lbs in 10 weeks. 

DAILY MEAL PLANS
I found the greatest success “pre-logging” my meals. Each PM, I mapped out the next days meals & snacks, logging them into a tracking app. I used my Meal Guide for sample meal plans & this was key in sticking to my macros!

If you want to start the New Year with the intention of being your healthiest- physically & mentally… join me! Link to the plans are in my stories!

年末時節，lululemon集結了北中南所有地區的大使一起聚會，也與過去僅有幾面之緣的朋友，有更多的互動與認識。過程中的交流，沒有掩飾或誇耀，大家前來分享彼此心中最真誠的想法，可能有脆弱的一面，也有感動人心的一刻，歡笑與淚水的交織洗滌，成就了在歲末年終之際一道暖流。

其實在這場聚會之後有著深深的感觸，每個成為大使的人都有著自己獨特性，有些人具有領導者風格，站在台上信手捻來就能把思緒整理好侃侃而談；有些人自律、目標明確，執行力滿分；有些人細心溫暖，時時刻刻專注聆聽，關心他人的需求。而我，是什麼樣的人呢？好像都不是，也或者是什麼都有一點但什麼都不精，回程的路上有點沮喪，但也意識到這樣的察覺，也可以成為未來努力的方向。但願2023年的年末回顧時，能在回頭看時給自己一個滿意的微笑。

Let’s set some new goals!! 💭🤸‍♀️🫡
⠀⠀ 
My motivation is always 100x higher when I’m focused on what actually gets *me* excited to move, instead of being vague and going through the motions 🤖
⠀⠀ 
Prioritising performance is the most important part of that and these goals are speaking to me this year 🙊
⠀⠀ 
🎯 Single arm toe to bars: my arch nemesis core movement and I’ve been stuck at 4 reps for years now because I felt satisfied and stopped trying 🫠 
⠀⠀ 
🎯 Overhead pistols

🎯 Handstand control 😍
⠀⠀ 
🎯 Pull-ups: getting my first pull-up came yeaaars into training for me. Being a sprinter + triathlete meant I didn’t speak to 1 rep max upper body work 👀 But I still get the “oh sh!t” moment every time I set a PR for pull-ups!
⠀⠀ 
🎯 Squats: after I caused my back injury (outside the gym, the gym is v safe!), squats were my first move back in the gym. I triggered an episode in my back going super light and the mental scar never left me. I don’t need to hit my PR but I’d love to slowly heal the last thing still with me 🧠
⠀⠀ 
🎯 Mobility
⠀⠀ 
🎯 Ultra-running: I have the best memories of my first time last year, even though it kicked my ass and made me question my existence 😭❤️‍🔥 Plus we supported research into spinal injuries and now it feels like fighting back 🥷
⠀⠀ 
I’m not putting pressure on myself to do all of these. They’re just reminders. Exciting reminders of what my body can 100% do if I keep learning!
⠀⠀ 
What are your goals for this year? What feels exciting and new and not just going through the motions to you?
⠀⠀ 
Side note: 📝📝 I hope you don’t ever ever compare your goals with mine or anyone else’s! We all have our own story. I might have progressed way less if I had yours, you might be way ahead of where I was at the same point in time! Progress is progress 🤍👏🙌

Happy #TechniqueTipTuesday! 

This week we will be discussing the difference between when your hands are slightly wider than your shoulders VS when your hands are underneath your shoulders during pushups. 

-When your hands are slightly wider than the frame of your shoulders, your elbows should be pointing on your back diagonals (pressed back on the 45° angle behind you, rather than winged out to the sides at 90°). This will lessen strain in your shoulders, and bring more work into your chest and outer arms.
-When your hands are underneath your shoulders, your elbows should be narrow and squeezing in by your sides.  This will bring more work into your triceps as well as your chest.
-No matter what type of pushup you’re doing, you always want to keep your core engaged and your hips tucked under. You want to avoid a pike of your hips or a sink down of your hips and arch of your back. Back should stay flat throughout the movement. 
-Your body should lower to the floor in one long line, leading with your chest.

Weight Loss In Menopause 

We talked about the best exercises for perimenopause and let me tell you that when you get to menopause, ladies, you have a hormonal advantage for weight loss: increased testosterone. 

Increased testosterone levels in menopause mean that lifting weights will be a KEY exercise for you to leverage your hormones. Lifting weights maximizes the benefits you’ll gain from testosterone because it allows you to build muscle. 

Also, it’s the best exercise for your blood sugar during menopause, too, because the lower estrogen/progesterone in relation to testosterone means you creep into one of the worst byproducts of the hormonal shift: insulin resistance. 

Insulin resistance is common in menopause because of the reduction in estrogen and the first thing I tackle for hormones is insulin resistance because that increases heart disease risk, Alzheimer’s risk, and even PCOS in younger gals. Your blood sugar matters first and foremost. {that’s the same for you ApoE4s, like me!}

Weight lifting helps reverse insulin resistance in menopause! 

Building muscle also helps maintain bone density and combats osteoporosis.

Weight lifting also helps with balance.

The best areas to build muscle are your legs, booty, and back. Don’t be afraid of getting “too bulky.” That would be a very difficult task in menopause! Those muscles will keep you healthy and youthful and trimmer than other exercise options.

🧘🏼‍♂️🛍📉Lululemon Athletica Inc. shares tumbled after the maker of fitness wear lowered its guidance for gross margin, stoking fears about profitability for a second-straight quarter.

Gross margin is now expected to shrink by as much as 1.1 percentage point in the three-month period ending in late January, compared with a previous forecast for an increase of as much as 0.2 percentage point, the Vancouver-based company said in a statement on Monday. Lululemon shares fell as much as 12% as of 9:45 a.m. in New York.

The company, best known for its yoga gear, also saw its shares tumble a month ago when it reported lower-than-expected profitability in the third quarter. Across the retail sector, companies have struggled to manage inventory levels, which can lead to steep markdowns. Lululemon is no exception, and its shrinking gross margins are “troubling” amid an inventory pileup, according to Tom Nikic, an analyst at Wedbush Securities.

Lululemon raised its fourth-quarter revenue outlook and said customer traffic remains strong both in stores and online. The company aims to double sales by early 2027 with more stores, international expansion and growth in the men’s business.

Lululemon now expects earnings per share in the fourth quarter will be in the range of $4.22 to $4.27, below the average analyst estimate of $4.30. The previous guidance was for EPS of $4.20 to $4.30.

Yesterday, @lululemon Montclair unveiled my new #lululemonambassador photo along with those of @drgenomayes & @kristenkemp .

This role is awarded to people in our community who dedicate their time to helping & supporting others- a role I am grateful to have the platform to develop.

Four years ago, when I first accepted this honor & made it on the wall, I felt on top of the world! I made a full recovery from an accident that threatened my life and my ability to run. In the photo, I was days away to a huge marathon PR and a ticket to run the Boston Marathon (finally)! But then, COVID changed everything.

I no longer feel the peak of performance perfection but I have found a much greater happiness and joy in running (and biking & swimming & climbing). The race might not happen as planned and that’s okay- the training and the friendships that come with the miles are so much more valuable & fun than one big day. And if it’s not fun, why are we getting up before the sun & gathering layers to run in 10 degrees & pushing ourselves to climb all the hills?!

The two photos, the sentiment represented in each one- they really opened my eyes to what I’ve learned on this journey and to my immense gratitude for the hearts & minds & bodies surrounding me.

Thank you.

I can’t tell you how many people I talk to who won’t wear something they would like to do, or won’t do something they dream of because they don’t like something about their body or because they’re afraid of what people will think.

It might be shorts. People say they don’t like their legs so they don’t wear shorts. Well, guess what? I have always been insecure about my legs. Cellulite, fat, too short, thick thighs, saggy skin, scars, too old, immodest, whatever. But I wear what feels good and I leave it at that. I figure if I feel good, that’s what matters. If anyone has an issue, it’s their issue. 

This is an encouragement from one flawed insecure person to another to drop perfectionism and do what you want, or at the very least, wear whatever you want. Wear the shorts. Rock the bikini. Let your hair down. Maybe it’s not your body? Maybe you dream of doing something that seems out of reach and you’re afraid people will laugh at you? Who cares if they laugh? Go out and live your dreams and when they see your soul shine, they’ll ask you what you did to become so beautiful and powerful. And you’ll say, I stopped caring if people laughed at me and just did what felt good for me. 

Which do you prefer? 1 or 2?

Maybe it’s time to find your passion and purpose. Maybe it’s time to find balance. Create new habits. Treat yourself better. Treat others better. 

Stop taking things for granted. Stop taking everything so personally. Start taking chances and living life to the fullest. Remember, what you think “didn’t work out” actually went right to plan. You just have to see it differently.

Be patient. Be strong. Be willing to trust the process. Everything takes time, and won’t always go to the plan you envisioned. It’s worth it, and it’s all out there. 💙

When I made the decision to step away from rugby it was the hardest decision I’ve ever made and hurt a lot. It hurt because it was finally a realization that I didn’t accomplish my dreams. It hurt because it was my entire life and identity since I was 14 years old. Rugby has brought me some of the most amazing friendships and brothers I could have ever imagined. It brought me around the world to places I never thought I’d get to see. From accomplishing a childhood dream of being paid to play the sport I love to travelling for free or getting to play with and against guys I watched on tv or idolized watching. I always questioned if I was good enough to be there or if I was tough enough to share the pitch with them. Realizing with the help of Covid that I was no longer in contention to achieve my dreams hurt. But never in a million years did I expect what would come from closing one door and opening another. 

I’ve always known that I was destined for something bigger. Through my trials and tribulations. Through abuse, through addiction and then triumph I could have never pictured the doors that I’ve opened and will continue to open. 2020 was heartbreak. 2021 showed me a new love for endurance and ultra endurance. It showed me I had a purpose to help the youth and motivate the masses. It also solidified my decision to move on. Although I’m still involved and will continue to be involved my dream chasing for the maple leaf on my chest is over. This led to more heartbreak and very dark times. 2022 I proved to myself that my purpose is bigger than the game. Bigger than me and more important than I could have ever thought. 

My son being born, marathons, triathlons, Ironman, a 100km ultra marathon; brand partnerships with @lululemon and @bpnsupps and over $30,000 raised for the youth in my community; I’m only getting started. 

2022 was the warm up. 2023 its time to flip the switch and #proveyourselfright 

Keep going. #OMT

One of the funnier sides of transitioning later in life is this weird feeling of being chronologically 46, but the way I feel otherwise is all over the place. 
I didn’t get to have that girl upbringing so in some ways, I’m like a 14 year old just going through puberty for the first time. Trying to adjust to a new body, emotions running me all over the place, dating for the first time as myself. So many more examples of why I feel like a 14 year old on the cusp of her quinceanera. I want to party like it’s 1991.  I didn’t have a lifetime to learn many of the skills and I have had some major cramming to do. But, I also didn’t have to learn all the hard lessons either. Cat calling, worrying about the creepy guy following me on a dark night or the inequality of the wage gap for example. 
Then, there is this other side. I’ve lived a whole life before this one. Married, divorced, kids, friends, and careers. Now, a second life. In this other way, I feel like a senior citizen wondering when the nursing home will be my new home. Let’s call this age 73 for arguments sake. All of this knowledge and experiences that have filled multiple lifetimes of an average shmoo. 
Then, I only came out 3 years ago, so in this way, I’m a baby gay. 
So since I am 46, 14, 73 and 3, my math brain is telling me to take the median. That’s 136/4=34. Ok, I’m good with 34. I wouldn’t mind staying 34 for the rest of my life.

Running tips day ONE and a view from the end of my track workout yesterday which was 2.5 mile warm up, 10x800, (yasso) 2.5 mile cool down. I swore a lot and shed one tear. 

Today is all about GEAR. What do you need?!! Running is fairly simple but investing in quality gear will help. ALL of this is on my LTK page and/or Amazon shop. 

👟 Kicks - the best way to pick a shoe is to go to a specialty running store and have someone qualified watch you run. If that’s not an option these shoes tend to work for most runners: New Balance 1080, Nike Winflo (under $100) Saucony Endorphin Pro, ASICS novablast or ASICS glider ride. A workout shoe is different - it’s a shoe you use for tempo runs/track workouts/quality sessions. For those I love the Nike Vaporflys and ASICS Metaspeed sky or edge (both have a carbon plate) 

Clothes - a lot of this depends where you run, you won’t wear the same thing in Oregon as you will in Florida but these three brands get it right: Lululemon, Handful and Oiselle. The speed up short at lululemon and the base pace tights are my go to. Oiselle creates running clothes JUST for women - you really cannot go wrong. Here are some options for less expensive gear/brands (focus on if it’s comfortable because that’s what matters) I have used and found effective 👉🏻 Old Navy, Baleaf (found on Amazon) and @senita  and the DSG brand from @dickssportinggoods )

INVEST in good sports bras for your girls. I recommend handful. A bad sports bra can ruin a great run. I should have some info on a collab with @handful soon.

Happy #TechniqueTipTuesday! 

This week we will be going over a part of our new warm up, forearm plank with the addition of your knees bending and extending. 

-Start off in your best forearm plank position. Your whole body should be in one long line from the top of your head going out through your heels.
-Your core should be engaged, and your hips should be tucked under. The tuck of your hips and the engagement of your core is what hold your body still as your knees begin to move. 
-You want to avoid shifting your weight forward and back. Instead, think of keeping your entire upper body still and your hips in line with your shoulders. 
-As always, feel free to modify as you need to either coming down to your knees, or just holding your best plank position.

BOOKMARK (save) these 10 moves to help you build bigger stronger quads! Read below 👇🏼⁣
-⁣
1️⃣. Front foot elevated rear lunge: Elevate the front foot on a couple of plates and focus on keeping your torso up as you step back and bring your knee down towards the ground.⁣ ⁣
•⁣
2️⃣. Barbell front squat: There’s a few ways you can choose to hold the barbell depending on what’s the most comfortable for you, but focus on keeping your chest and elbows up as you descend into the squat position.⁣
•⁣
3️⃣. Rear foot elevated split squat: The key to targeting the quads in this position is to keep a narrower stance and to focus on keeping your torso up as you perform each rep. ⁣
•⁣
4️⃣. Spanish squat: Loop a heavier band around a sturdy surface and put your legs inside of the band on each side right around knee height. Focus on keeping your knees behind your toes and keep torso up as you descend into the squat. ⁣
•⁣
5️⃣. Weighted squat hold: Get into a position where your thighs are parallel to the ground and hold the heaviest weight you can for time. Try to keep your torso tall in this position.
•⁣
6️⃣. Dual kettlebell squat: Keep your feet shoulder width apart and keep your chest up as you lower yourself into the squat position.
•⁣
7️⃣. Single leg bench squat: Bring your butt down slowly to a surface that’s about knee height. Keep your torso up as you lower yourself and this with as much control as possible. ⁣ ⁣
•⁣
8️⃣. Walking lunges: The key here is to keep the stride short and to keep your torso/chest up as you perform the lunge. ⁣
•⁣
9️⃣. Heels elevated goblet squat: Your stance should be hip width apart or slightly inside the hips. Elevate the heels on a plate or a slant board (as shown in the video). Focus on keeping your torso up as you descend into the squat.⁣
•⁣
🔟. ⁣ Step ups: The step ups surface should be at about knee height or slightly higher. The key is to focus on using the front leg to step on top of the surface and to avoid any kind of momentum or bouncing from the back leg.

2022 HIGHS
▪️Crossed the finish line of my first half in 6 years at 8 months postpartum! After hitting a few speedbumps along the postpartum running journey, I was thrilled to eek out a 1:28 at BK after only a couple months of consistent running. It confirmed that *something* is still there. 🤞🏻
▪️ @liftrunperform added 6 new coaches (what?!) and we launched a BQ and sub4 program, along with our pre-existing sub3 teams.
▪️I started saying "no" more often - and have tried to make an intention to focus my energy and time on things that really matter most in life (this is oddly very hard).
▪️Got a new hip! I'm so grateful this surgery was such a success and I'm REALLY grateful for the relationships the hip journey has introduced me to - both from a medical and friend perspective. Even if the road back is long...I'm here for it.
▪️Continued my relationship with @lululemon and became a @tracksmith ambassador! Very thankful to be partnering with these two brand leaders of community and inclusion.

2022 LOWS
▪️My injury took a really big hit on my mental health. There were many ups and downs with confusing MRI reports…anxiety was at an all-time high and I was struggling to sleep at night. It was difficult being in so much pain while also being unsure how to navigate the injury and knowing whether surgery would be the right choice.
▪️COVID was really shitty. For me, it took months to really feel like myself again after getting it at the end of May and rebounding after Paxlovid.
▪️I constantly feel like I could be doing more and be better - a better mom...a better wife...a better coach. Working full time and parenting two little humans is really hard and one thing I'm continuing to work on is being present with the task at hand, and making in-person relationships (whether with family or friends) more meaningful.
▪️I have a really hard time turning my brain off and relaxing. This is also something I hope to work on in the new year.

Alright lululemon runners....let's see if ur worth it.

How do you measure success? 

You are going to be seeing lots of posts right now about all the amazing things that people accomplished this year, and it is going to get you thinking if you did "enough." 

Let me tell you, I ran the least amount of kms this year that I have EVER run according to strava.  Even compared to the year I was in chemotherapy.  

But, I DON'T CARE! 

If you are measuring success souly on outcomes, you will often feel discouraged. Because we can not always control outcomes. 

Here are some better measures of success to consider other than outcomes: 

🏃‍♀️ Trying new things 

🥳 Increased enjoyment 

📅 Increased consistency 

💪 Improved form or technique 

These are things we can control and habits we can actively choose, which can lead to better outcome goals in the long run.  But if we base our success and self-worth only on the outcomes, then we will be left often feeling like we did  not do enough.

Growing up is both about embracing and rejecting where we come from — and that includes how we dress and make ourselves up. Writer Yamilette Vizcaíno Rivera, reflects on how she’s found peace with those contradictions in this essay (which you can read in full via our bio link):

“After exiting the plane, I beeline for the strategically placed bathroom in between aduanas and the arrivals runway. I’m American so I wear my Meg Thee Stallion hoodie and Adidas sneakers on the plane. But I’m also Dominican so I change into Lululemon leggings (a boxing day sale), a tiny rayon floral Reformation dress (secondhand), and red Michel Kors boots (bought with my tax return). My black Kate Spade shoulder bag (a Black Friday sale) is tucked inside of my brand new oxblood Telfar (a birthday present from my girlfriend).

The look is the embodiment of what Mami has always wanted for me (femininity, presentability, logos) and what I have come to appreciate (secondhand, sales, authenticity). There’s nothing acquiescent about my day one wash-and-go corkscrew curls, nothing approachable about the disconcerting fire-hydrant red Fenty on my lips, and there’s something a bit unsettling about the way that none of my jewelry matches because none of it is actually mine — all of it is pilfered from or given to me by loved ones over the years. I wear it all together because I’m trying to carry with me everyone who’s ever loved me, and all the parts of the world we all come from, all at once.”

【2022年結束前問自己一個問題】

即將踏進新一年，大家都紛紛回顧這一年做過什麼。做了什麼如何做？這些都不難回答。最難答的問題是：「為什麼而做？」

這一年，你大概也曾跟ZtoryTeller一樣，有懷疑人生懷疑自己的時候。這年，我們做了一個很大的決定，換了名字，換了logo，換了內容.... 為什麼？原來，我們沒提過。

從StoryTeller轉到ZtoryTeller，“Z” 是 “S” 的相反，當中隱藏的意義是「推倒重來」。不只看過去成功的，也放下過去失敗的，放棄固有模式，重新建構一個自己此刻喜歡的藝術品牌。Z也代表著創造三維世界的 z 軸，決心嘗試從線上走到線下，從虛擬走到實體，開發各類型實體故事體驗和藝術企劃。

從頭來過當然難！出書難，推廣閱讀難、辦展覽難、做藝術難、經營社交平台難.... 更難的問題是：

為什麼而做？

“Love is our ultimate goal.” 

愛是我們的終極目標，抱歉好像說得太空泛太煽情，但這真的是此刻唯一浮現腦海的句子。

你呢？這夜，祝你想到屬於你的答案，也送你來自日本的招福貓。2022若跟我們一樣曾跌倒受傷了，也不要怕，就推倒重來，跟招福貓一起舉起右手，向幸福的2023招手！

2022 the year of my highest highs and lowest lows. 
..
This year has been a hard one to process. I’ve accomplished a lot, but it was also a year of loss that weighs on me every day. Each picture in this post signifies a memory from 2022 that impacted my life. 
..
Running in 2022 was not full of its usual miles and race schedule. 2022 ended with 775 miles. My lowest mileage since I started running. I ran one marathon, which is less than usual. However, I ran that marathon pregnant! This year I also became a pregnant runner! Brody and I ran 354 miles together before he made his entrance into the world. Running for two taught me how to love my body and give myself grace and the power of rest! I’m looking forward to becoming an official mother runner in 2023! 
..
On a personal front 2022 was all about growth. 
•I grew in my career outside of running and took on a new job that was both challenging and rewarding.
•I furthered my career as a running coach with @truepotentialrunning and coached so many amazing athletes this year! 
•I was given the opportunity to be a @lululemon run ambassador. It has been so rewarding representing a brand that truly cares and has allowed me to grow and develop so many amazing relationships! 
•I became a mom! It’s only been 10 days, but I love being a mom so much and can’t wait to see what this next year of motherhood has in store for me! It’s hard but so rewarding 
..
Now onto the least favorite part of 2022. This is the year I suddenly lost my Dad. It’s been a little over 5 months and it still hurts just as bad every day. It’s hard to still process you won’t be here in 2023 with us. It comes in waves of sadness and anger. I’m both mad and sad that he never got to meet Brody. However, I made a vow to keep living life to the fullest and honoring him every day. I can’t wait to tell Brody all about you one day and tell him about the amazing man that his middle name came from. 
..
So 2022, thanks for some of the memories and allowing me to enter the next phase of my life as a mom. I’m ready for 2023, but I’m not quite ready to set any new goals yet and I’m totally ok with that!

⚡ WHAT'S BETTER THAN A NEW YEAR'S RESOLUTION?⚡

This year, I'm offering an alternative.

I was listening to podcast a couple days ago and the guest presented a technique used in self-improvement and goal-setting circles  that really resonated with me. He encouraged people to find their 'WHY' by asking as many questions as they could about their goal until they discovered their true motivation. 

For example, you might say...

I want to run a 1/2 marathon.
- WHY?

Because it's been on my list for years?
- WHY?

Because I've always thought of that as being an incredible accomplishment.
- WHY?

Because I recognize that the amount of training, discipline, planning, and effort that I would need to invest to complete this distance would make me feel incredible.
- WHY?

Because I feel like I need a goal outside my comfort zone that I can accomplish?
- WHY?

Because deep down I feel like I am braver and more adventurous than I allow myself to be. 
- WHY?

And so on...

Maybe your goal is more about giving yourself permission to try new things than finishing a race. Maybe it is about focusing on your potential instead of comparing yourself to people you follow online. Maybe it's about believing in your abilities and surrounding yourself with people who will accept you where you're at, and support you in getting to where you want to be.

This year, I encourage you to believe in yourself. Show yourself what you're capable of achieving. Be gentle and patient. Have fun, and go after your WHY.

If you want or need a crew to support you along your path to your personal victories, we'll be right here.

You're welcome here.
Just the way you are.
Every time.

A common misconception people have is that a workout is ineffective if you aren't sore within the next day [or two], however, there is very little to no evidence that supports this. If you're looking to build muscle, a better way to measure this is by tracking how you progress in the gym (sets, reps, intensity, etc.), taking progress photos, or doing body composition scans. To make it simple, have a nutrition and exercise plan that focuses on progressive overload.

1 year ago @jonnyappletreez proposed. 6 weeks later, we got married and since then it feels like both the longest year ever AND like we blinked and missed it. 
We traveled quite a bit: Portland, Buffalo, NYC, Vegas and Mexico. Visited family. Sister got married. The boys turned 13 and 10. We coached Levi’s soccer team. Matthan did horseback riding lessons. We snowboarded a lot. Took the boys camping. They rode snow machines for the first time. We launched @thewildsstory and photographed 3 weddings in our first month. Traveled outside of the US for the first time in a long time. Adopted George. Celebrated @burn.bloom being open 4 years. Became a @lululemon ambassador and hosted my biggest yoga event ever… 
Wow! Now that I write all that out.. I realize we really did do a lot. And I accomplished a lot in my businesses and hit some goals I had set years ago. Im proud of us this year. 
But more than anything, I’m thankful for a partner to do every single day with. All of the hard days that aren’t pictured in the highlight reel. The boring and mundane. The challenging days filled with work and bills and parenting…. And learning to balance it all. I never imagined a love and family unit like this. 
Cheers to a good year. And stoked for another one.

Chapter 36. 🎉

Grateful to be here another day, for everything I have and all I’m excited for in the year ahead. So… This is 36. A year where I take my life back and start with a new mindset. A year where I challenge myself to be my personal best and a year where I give back as much as I fulfill my own dreams.

Here's to new beginnings, epic adventures and all of the amazing people that make my life better. Here's to taking the power into my hands and creating a life beyond my wildest dreams. I've had a hell of a year, and am so ready to start next year with a surgery, strengthen with recovery and become the best version of myself thus far. I have so many ideas to challenge myself and advance in my career, goals, and personal development. But I am also ready to create a healthy balance and make time for the little things. 

So, thank you to everyone who has made my life brighter. Everyone who has been there for me in the good and not so good times. Everyone who has challenged me to grow because you see potential in me. And, thank you to those who taught me lessons. Thank you to those who weren't so kind, because you made me stronger and motivated me in a different way. You helped me see my worth. You helped me grow a positive mindset by leaving what was weighing me down behind.

I hope you all go into the new year with confidence, conviction, kindness and a sense of humor. Life is too short to take yourself, or really anything, too seriously. And remember, age is a mindset. Take care of yourself, be open to the wonder and magic of life, and you will always feel young! Grow older, not up. 😎

Love always,
Kirsten 💖

LEDGE WORKOUT
Full body bodyweight session...
▫️▫️▫️
Took advantage of a nice day to hit a little bit of everything using a concrete ledge/barrier at our local community center. 
- 4 pairs, 3 sets each, roughly 10-12 reps
Pair 1:
1️⃣ Hook Push-up to Pike
2️⃣ Elevated Sprinter Thrust
Pair 2:
3️⃣ Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat
4️⃣ Lying Row to Pulldown 
Pair 3:
5️⃣ Step Up Switch 
6️⃣ Layback Crunch Hip Raise
Pair 4:
7️⃣ Eccentric Tricep 
8️⃣ Eccentric One Arm Bicep
There are several adaptations to each of these that can make them either easier or harder but the general setup and concept is an easy one to follow. As I’ve always said, fitness is everywhere and even if you don’t have access to the facilities or equipment you want, there are always ways to make the most of it. Keep your eyes and mind open and you’ll consistently be surprised with what you find and create.

Yesterday, I finished my ninth Boxing Day at lululemon and thought it was time to share that I've made the decision to step down from my role as Store Manager at the end of January.

I’ve been at lululemon a collective total of eight years and one of the reasons I’ve been around so long is because of our culture and the lifelong relationships I’ve made. I am beyond grateful for the experience of getting to meet, lead and be led by so many great humans over the years and use the lessons that they’ve taught me literally everyday. ((Love y’all))

Full transparency, I’ve been dealing with a combo of with mental illness, burn out, shifting priorities and the nagging feeling that my intuition has been off for quite a while, so I actually don’t have a perfect plan for what's next for me. The one thing that I know in my gut is that it’s the right move to take a step back in order to find an avenue that's more aligned with what’s need to support my physical and mental well-being.

A lot people don’t get to have space for reflection and exploration in the raging machine that is late stage capitalism so I feel privileged that I have the means and the support of my friends, family and husband to take this leap of faith. For real though, @_mike_v_ has been my biggest cheerleader through this and I couldn’t be more grateful.

So there it is, here’s to jumping and trusting that the net will appear. 🖤✨

day four reflecting on the year….

question: Identify a positive “pivot point” - because that occurred something else was set in motion. Then recall your contribution in making that a reality 

I LOVE this question because it’s a reminder that you are an active contributor in your life…that small everyday decisions create a ripple effect on your life. It gives more meaning to the mundane and ordinary. When I look back, I feel so empowered and inspired when I realize that a seemingly insignificant decision I made or conversation I had was what set in motion a major shift or opportunity in my life. 

Let me timeline this trip to Morocco really quick…
-went to a yoga workshop with @elaninicole (2016?)
-got coffee with @elaninicole to learn more about her + her career where she encourages me to consider a career with @lululemon
-go with @elaninicole to a @lululemon event in Denver hosted by @c.line.smith + @annalethen 
-go to workout and get coffee with @c.line.smith to talk life and goals (2017)
-quit my corporate job to work for @c.line.smith and open a new Denver lululemon 
-hire @despicable_d and @_ryland_____ during new store opening where they tell me I should connect with @kaitvanhoff because they think we would hit it off 
-enter giveaway for a yoga retreat to Costa Rica with @kaitvanhoff…and WIN
-go on trip and make lifelong friends with @mernilsen + @mc__kenzie (2018)
-plan reunion trip four years later to Morocco with Mer, Kenz, Kait, and handful of other girlfriends (2022)

There were so many breakdowns, breakthroughs, new relationships, relationships ended, career shifts, and both massive and small courageous moments over those six years I just timelined that led me to the photo you see here (@teagan.maddux). I sat in bed sobbing over work when I decided to look at @elaninicole’s business card, go to her website, and email her asking if she still needed an assistant and wanted to get coffee. Meeting her changed my life and it started with a breakdown in bed and silly email 

I hope you take a moment to consider this question because I promise it will give more meaning to all your unseen efforts

QUICK BODYWEIGHT WARMUP
Move, mobilize, activate...
▫️▫️▫️
5 moves to get a little action going from top to bottom using just bodyweight.
1️⃣ Split Walkout to Plank
Used a tightrope stance as the base to add a little balance element. For a few other options check out #sidewalkout 
2️⃣ Stork Tuck Reaches
Think about controlling the reach and return. Same side repeats usually but occasionally I’ll alternate sides. 
3️⃣ Foot Swivel
One of my favorite foot, ankle, calf and hip movements, both for the body elements but also for the coordination and fun aspects. See #footswivel for more. 
4️⃣ Split Iso Arm Circles
Hover the knee just off the ground and reach big circles (I typically use #xiaopengcircles for this), knee down makes it a touch easier. 
5️⃣ Cross Touch, Step and Reach
Control the movement, try to get up on your toes when you reach and give the body a little twist at the bottom and the top.

Stopping in to celebrate our @lululemon teams is one of my favourite holiday traditions. The energy and coordination across our stores, Distribution Centres, Store Support Centres, and Guest Education Centres is not only inspiring, but incredibly fun to be around. I’m proud, grateful, and wishing you all a safe and happy holiday!

When my athletes run by, first I see their mood—how loose are their shoulders? Are they chatting? Are they smiling? Are they running close together in bonded space (so rare a sight among adults.)

Then, I see their fatigue—how light is their ground contact? How much bounce is in their step? How easily do they push the ground behind away and how much do they have to reach? 

Then, I see their form—what has changed since my last visual scan? How much are we torquing at the knee from the hip? How loose is the thoracic spine? How free-floating is the knee lift and how available is extension? (Forgive me, PTs. I speak in coaches pidgin.)

Lastly, I take some notes for later and move it all to the back of my mind, down my spinal column, and into my body. It’s complicated, the layered systems of anatomy and physiology and psychology seen through a performance lens, but it’s hubris to think your mind will unwind the complication.

Every athlete is capable, after so much investment in the dry matter of training, of using their body to do something that feels beyond it. The coach’s job is to respect that, and get out of the way when necessary.

When I look at a photo of my current stride, I see the many more than 10,000 hours that went into building it on the track and in the weight room, and at home with a book in my lap. I also see a weakened body, whose resources are now directed towards others’ momentum rather than its own. Its job is physical empathy, and its fitness comes as a mirror to my athletes’. In other words, I need to feel what they’re feeling. I need to, after writing the program, watch them move and feel in my own body how to tweak the formula to match the human. 

This body doesn’t feel like it used to. It doesn’t run as fast or as far. But, it’s my lens into the work I do now. I am so thankful to have know the feel of flight, and to have discovered that sharing preserves it.

年底電池快用完了，參加lululemon年度大使聚會前，我走進門市看到自己的照片磚。當年團隊都會邀請老師們：寫下一句你想要與大家說的話。
而我寫下的是：想，是不會發生任何的事。

進場後我們有一段的年末冥想以及分享時間。分享出今年你覺得做得最棒的以及想要改善的地方。我與大家分享的感受：我在團體當中嘗試扮演著給予者的角色。
我做得最好也最差的就是給予者的角色。

從家中小事，愛犬寶哥黏滴滴，媽媽在外研習過夜就會整晚睡在客廳守在門口，我就會捨不得計畫遠行。

疫情前我就是個旅遊好咖。
誒！要不要去加拿大？喔好，走。
誒！要不要去印度？喔好，走。
誒！有個不錯的老師在香港，要不要一起去研習？喔好，走。
現在卻因為擔心家裡與教室而停滯不前。

在教室培訓，新起之秀結業後，何去何從。
會很有既視感地想起小時候，非科班出身的我，圈內也沒有社交連結的情形下，我只能一張一張傳單發（現在可能是社交媒體）招生，104人力銀行亂撒，直到現在才站得住腳。
我每次有機會經過一間健身教室有缺團班的老師，就會主動幫大家詢問有沒有需要的老師還可以安排時段。

我知道這些其實我可以不用作。

聚會到家的時候，跟伴侶分享。
他聽完系列對話，問了我一句：那“妳”在哪裡？
我才意識到，很多時候，我在思考事情時，都是以他人出發，而非自己。

看著自己早期的護照都被蓋滿了還要換新的一本，之於現在，兩點一線，照顧家人，照顧學生，我真的有照顧到自己嗎？

在意的人生活無慮，我就會開心嗎？
我會放心，但不會開心。
因為開心寬心的能量是要自己滋潤的。

站在門市裡看到自己寫下的這句話，好像時光膠囊提醒自己。

Self-love
Sharing
Family
Happiness 
Peace 

先懂得愛自己，有足夠的能量可以分享，於是就聚眾成了家庭（community）（無論是血親或是朋友），因為這樣得到了幸福，平和之心終可圓滿。

新年的期許，將這句話還給自己：想，是不會發生任何的事。讓自己2023年充電回血，迎接更真實的自己😀

The very things I said no to are the exact things I had to say yes to and now do with passion, love and care. It's called living in purpose on purpose.

I take every opportunity to be in purpose, living life as I love it and sharing it with the world.

There are places within each of us that remain eternally private. It’s almost like a blanket of quietude that can never be pierced. Entering that inner sanctuary, where really truly only you as your true self can be, is the work of yoga. That is why, no matter how public things may seem, no matter how much time we spend in class, yoga remains always and essentially a personal practice. The devotional seeds that we each sow on the mat, in between breath, body and mind are our own. Once they take root and the fruits start to show in our lives, we can share the benefits of the practice with all. But turning outward too soon destroys the harvest. So take time to dive deeply down into the layers of yourself that only you can penetrate.

Traveling for the holidays? This post is for you! 🎄

Ain’t nobody got time for $17 sandwiches at the airport or being hungry while stuck traffic. With a little planning, you can save monies, have better food options, and/or just not be hungry and sad during your travel (:

Save this post, + swipe for more tips!

We can't recommend enough to pack a cooler full of food before going on a roadtrip. As far as the airport goes, you can bring food through airport security, just make sure there's no liquids beyond ~3 oz. 

You can also bring icepacks to keep everything cold, just make sure they’re frozen solid. Check airport rules if traveling abroad to other countries.

You could cook meats and proteins ahead of time and transport in Tupperware containers or baggies (Pyrex containers + the silicone reusable bags from Stasher ftw!). 

You could also cook carbs ahead of time (rice, potatoes, sweet potatoes, oatmeal, etc). Lululemon totes are awesome for transporting food around (:

Hope this helps.

Happy #TechniqueTipTuesday!!! 

this week we will be talking about posture during leg extensions during thigh work. 

-It is really easy to sink back into the barre and almost use it as a crutch. However, it’s important to keep your entire core strong to keep a secure center. 
-Your shoulders should stay stacked on top of your hips and your grip on the bar should stay light.
-Make sure to keep your tailbone pointing down to the floor and your hips tucked under. As your leg moves, your upper body shouldn’t. You want to avoid a seesaw motion and instead focus on your leg moving by leading with your thigh, and your core holding the rest of your body still and strong.
-keep your eyes gazing right across the room. Try to avoid looking up or looking down because your eyes can effect your posture.

There is a secret weapon in the Vedic Meditators tool box and it is the art of Rounding. Rounding is a carefully crafted ancient Vedic practice designed to take your meditation to the next level. A specific sequence of gentle yoga asanas, pranayama breathing and meditation.

Rounding is considered to be one of the most purposeful ways in which to fast track accessing greater states of consciousness and to create your mental and physical health’s pure potential.

🪬 No coffee, no stimulants of any description (not even chocolate!!! ).
🪬 No engagement with the outside world. 
🪬 Digital detox 
🪬 Silent mornings 
🪬 44 sessions of rounding, (50 mins each session ) 2,200 minutes in total.

🪬 250minutes of Pranayama breath work
🪬 1,000 minutes of meditation 🪬 750 minutes asana (yoga) practice.

How lululemon impacted my coaching process which has led hundreds of golf transformations in 2022. 

In 2013 I first stepped foot inside of a lululemon store front…. Dallas Galleria to be exact. 

Little did I know how much that brand, company & community would impact my life. 

They were kind enough to take me in & accept me as one of their own right away…

At that time I was a young and energized to coach golfers through golf fitness. 

lululemon mentored me & helped me learn to goal set at a deeper level which was a GAME CHANGER.

Here’s why…

I was always a goal setter. But I never took it as deep as they taught me too…

Here’s what really stuck with me to this day…

WHAT, WHY & HOW.

Define exactly WHAT you want in your life, health & career. 

Draw out WHY you want this so bad. This will fuel your everyday. 

Lastly, have a clear understanding of HOW you will track & monitor your journey. 

Up until this moment I was simply setting goals without a WHY & without the HOW. 

Recently, Lululemon asked me to be a BRAND AMBASSADOR which is one of the coolest honors as a coach. 

I truly believe it happened because I stuck to the process. 

My WHAT, WHY & HOW drives my every day decisions. 

This is HOW I help my clients & community achieve their best lives. 

If you feel like your are STUCK or not getting the RESULTS you want out of your golf swing & game…

Comment “swing” & I’ll be here to talk.

La parte interna del short
En más de 10 años probando y conociendo de productos deportivos, debo decir que Lululemon era de los menos atractivos para mí, por el origen y porque, siendo reales el precio está por encima de la mayoría de las marcas en el mercado en México. Pero hablemos de la experiencia que tuve con los Surge Lined Shorts Special Edition, había leído sobre estos shorts y obvio la curiosidad creció con el paso de las semanas así que me animé probarlo y me encantó.

La parte externa del short 
Una de las cosas más cool que tienen los productos de Lululemon es la etiqueta, en ella agregan detalles de por qué crearon la misma, qué beneficios tiene además de las recomendaciones de uso. La tela externa es una combinación de poliéster reciclado y elástano que viene perforada para una mejor ventilación y secado rápido, el tema del resorte siempre es algo que cuido para que no me lastime cuando me lo pongo y, sobre todo, corriendo largas distancias. 

También lo use en entrenamientos intensos
Obviamente lo teníamos que usar en diferente tipo de entrenamientos, tanto carreras suaves como los de alto impacto en la pista o a velocidad. Si tienes las piernas más delgadas podría moverse un poco o generar rozaduras en la parte interna de las piernas porque a pesar de ser una tela construida en 4 direcciones, como mencioné antes, el mesh interno puede quedar ligeramente flojo aunque el grip (dobladillo Nulux) podría solucionar ese pequeño detalle.

Between 2009-2015, I worked in fashion marketing in NYC and it was an experience! I’ve ridden in an elevator literally rubbing elbows with Michael Kors…worked backstage at multiple fashion shows during NYFW…selected models for market week…placed advertising around the country…was required to wear 4” heels all day, every day - even if it meant my feet went numb.

But over the course of those 6 years, I also realized it wasn’t for me. When I finally was laid off in 2015, it was the best/worst day. 

Worst because no one likes hearing that they’re not wanted in an organization. 

Best because it finally launched me towards a life that I was truly meant to live.

Making a major life pivot in my late-20s was terrifying, and I was considering either PT school or something in health/fitness. I knew I wanted to help people work towards goals and become better versions of themselves. And I vowed to never go back to a job that made me miserable.

Fast forward to 2022 and being able to say I’m a full time coach is a dream come true. And I NEVER imagined I would lead a coaching business; I couldn’t be more proud of @liftrunperform and every coach and athlete aligned with our family.

Last night I was invited to see my photo blown up on the wall at the New Haven @lululemon store for the first time, after 2 years of ambassadorship. Seeing my photo up there was a bit surreal and pretty dang cool - especially after working in fashion/retail and knowing how protected and precious those wall spaces are.

So to the people who are stuck in a rut, wondering if they should make a life change: do it. Be uncomfortable. Embrace failure. Lean on your people to pursue your passion. Capitalize on projects that play to your strengths. Be observant and seek out mentors. Pour yourself into learning.

It’s certainly not easy and you’re going to have to work really really hard. But doing what you love makes it worth it.

"Despite Joe Biden’s economy and three straight cycles of election losses, the RNC’s big-spending days are back with a vengeance.

Perhaps because of these losses both RNC donors and committee members are intensely interested in the committee’s finances, particularly the spending. Late last week, RedState was provided a report dated October 7, 2022 that examined RNC’s 2021-22 spending. It calculated more than $500,000 in private jet expenses, $64,000 at clothing retailers, and $321,000 in floral arrangements.

To determine how that compared with the rest of Ronna McDaniel’s tenure, RedState examined RNC expenditures from 2017 through 2022. In addition to a review of Federal Elections Commission (FEC) data, RedState spoke with current vendors, state party officials familiar with the workings, former staffers (some from McDaniel’s tenure, and some who worked for prior chairs), and several current RNC members to verify numbers and dates. Most were only willing to discuss the matters on background, and all were promised anonymity to avoid potential retaliation.

It is difficult to accurately categorize all of the expenditures because a significant number of transactions seem to be misclassified. For example, nearly $5,000 spent in 2022 at Lululemon, a luxury athletic apparel brand, was classified as “office expense,” as were two expenditures totaling $9,300 at Madison Square Garden in 2017.

Our review found that the amounts spent during the 2021-22 election cycle seem to have been par for the course and possibly even lower than previous portions of McDaniel’s tenure. According to FEC filings, since 2017, the RNC has spent:

 $3.1 million on private jet services
 $1.3 million on limousine/chauffeur services
 $17.1 million on donor mementos
 $750,000 on floral arrangements
 $80,000 in alcohol-related expenditures

Nearly $400,000 has been spent on event tickets and other entertainment activities, including $30,000 for a private box at a Las Vegas Raiders game, $13,000 for Broadway shows, $9,400 at Madison Square Garden, and $43,000 at Top Golf locations in Texas, Nevada, Virginia, and Maryland."

Not every limit needs to be surpassed. Learning to respect our own boundaries helps us learn to respect other people’s boundaries. While in some way we are limitless, that very truth can be confusing when we are faced with a bunch of obstacles. It doesn’t feel like we are limitless beings of light when our leg won’t go where we want it to, or when we can’t lift up how we would like to, or when we don’t have the resources we need to do what we want. In those moments we feel all too limited and something inside of us wants to push through and break out to a new level of reality. But, sometimes it’s ok not to try to achieve. Sometimes it’s ok to accept what is as it is. Sometimes it’s ok to just let the foot go wherever it wants and not worry about how high your lift up is. 

We can all be so hard ourselves, pushing to do more, be more, achieve more. But when is enough really good enough? When is more not necessarily better? Maybe we can let ourselves off the hook for a little bit. And maybe we can use that extra space to breathe. Who knows? Maybe once we let go of the need to do more and be more we will find out that we are happy as we are.

Living with MS is humbling in more ways than I could have imagined. I still enjoy my favorite activities like tennis and practicing and teaching yoga each week, but I’ve accepted that my lifestyle sometimes needs to evolve with my health. This means that I listen to my body, and depending on my MS symptoms, some days I opt for chair yoga or meditation rather than tennis or a vinyasa flow. If I’m having tremors or sharp pains, I’ll just sit, breathe and let my body relax. That’s the magic of yoga, you can adapt your practice for what feels good for your body that day, and there are many ways to tailor exercises for your ability, such as using a chair or adding blocks to reduce the stress on your body. #thisisms

2022 has been one of the most challenging years of my life. I have felt every range of human emotion possible in the deepest ways...the highest of highs and lowest of lows. 

A moment of vulnerability, here is the cliff notes version of how the year has gone: 

I moved to San Diego in January. In April I left a job I loved. In April I started a new job at a startup that I loved. Company shut down and I lost my job 3 months later.  I continued to grow my own business. I started leading @rundelmar. I became the Run Ambassador at lululemon One Paseo (this pic is from my ambassador shoot). Family/life "things" happened, I wont trauma dump on you. I started going to therapy. I started meditating daily. My brother got married. Baby girl niece was born. I started a new job that I love teaching at @thevervestudios & I am still running my health coaching business. And last but not least, I am still in love with @ryan_laclaire who through it all still manages to make me smile, laugh & feel so loved every single day, even on the hard ones (had to add that in because its important you know?).

Truly a rollercoaster. That was a lot. *takes a deep breathe* 🧘🏽‍♀️

Here is what I am calling in for 2023 -- 

•Continuously pouring into the practices that feed my soul & make me feel alive. 

•Letting go and making room for the blessings coming my way. 

•Surrounding myself with people who feel like sunshine & continuing to build community.

•Releasing anxiety and fear that doesn't serve who I am becoming.

•Committing to growth, even in the uncomfortable moments.

•Fun. Play. Joy. Laughter. More of it, please!

My 2023 quote to live by: "You will bloom if you take the time to water yourself" I am ready to blooooommmm! ✨💛🙏🏽

I have about 4 lists I keep throughout my house with my daily goals, that I try to accomplish.  I personally find writing everything out to be a lot more motivating, and having one accessible everywhere as well,  just keeps me on track. 

I also have a morning ritual which has helped me accomplish so many goals, and has improved my mindset, it includes:

Wake up @5:00am, make my bed, take vitamins, eat breakfast, write down the “to dos” and goals of the day, write and say a couple affirmations, journal, read a chapter of a motivational book, and then do meditation for about 20 minutes or however long I need, and then study. I do this all within the first hours of waking up, and it just prepares me for the day ahead, also has improved my mental state 100%

I also put a schedule  to automatically do focus mode/downtime on my phone and any electronic device l have, from 9:30pm-9am(which means I can’t text, call, go on any apps, media, internet, etc.) 
I like to make sure I’m focused on my priorities first, that I finish them, and then I’ll turn it off, but ONLY after Im finished with my rituals🙌🏽

Let’s talk mentality 

I’m sure every single one of you knows, it’s not always easy to succeed and get to where you want to be, in any aspect of life 

But to get over those difficult times, the one essential piece of the puzzle you need to have is a good reason. But what does a good reason look like?

At the end of the day, IT DOESN’T MATTER. Not everyone is gonna have a deep story or some sort of traumatic past that pushes them to chase after their goals and dreams. And that’s more than ok

The only pre requisites for success are hard work, a willingness to stay disciplined to keep going when things get hard, and to stay learning new things that get you to the next step of your path

I struggled with a mentality for years before I got sick, thinking my reasoning for pushing myself in the gym wasn’t “deep enough” and because of that I wouldn’t be able to take it far. But I kept showing up and grinding, why?

Simple, I LOVE the gym. Sure, my reasoning is a lot deeper now, but if something pushes you to upgrade yourself and be a better version of you, and brings you satisfaction and excitement from thinking about and doing it, then that’s all that matters because at the end of the day no matter the reason, it’s gonna get you up and going and keep you levelling up in life

As long as you’re walking a good path that leads to self improvement, then that’s what’s important, that you get better

Whatever gets your chest beating hard with excitement, use it to the absolute fullest and don’t sell yourself short, you have no idea how high you can go. You owe it to yourself to be better. Stay hustling pumps fam🤝🏻👊🏻

Die genaue Zusammensetzung im Moment der Freude ist von den Umständen abhängig & kann uns daher die ganze Bandbreite offenbaren. 

Freude kann ganz still & leise sein, sie kann als ein Gefühl von  Wertschätzung auftreten oder wie ein fantastisches Feuerwerk explodieren 🎆

Wir können vor Freude weinen (das war gestern bei mir auch dabei), Luftsprünge machen oder die ganze Welt umarmen 🤗

Freude verbindet! ♥️

Wir sagen nicht umsonst, dass geteilte Freude doppelte Freude ist – für alle Beteiligten.

Und so durfte ich gestern beim alljährlichen „Mein Dankeschön“ nicht nur einen Abend voller Bhakti Yoga, Yoga des Herzens & der Hingabe, mit den lieben HIER & JETZT Yogis & Yoginis teilen & genießen, sondern zu meiner großen Freude auch noch Geschenke verteilen! 🥰

Allen, die da waren, durfte ich einen Gutschein von @lululemoneurope im Centro überreichen & so Freude am Miteinander & an der Bewegung verschenken, was ein Fest! 🎈

Worüber freust Du Dich in Deinem Leben? 
Über etwas, dass Du geschaffen hast oder Dir durch verschiedene Umstände zugute gekommen ist? 

Welche Umstände & Menschen haben dazu beigetragen? 

Wo hast Du selbst zu Freude &  zum Glück anderer beigetragen? 

Werde Dir der Verbundenheit mit anderen in diesem Guten bewusst & erlaube Dir, sie wertzuschätzen & Dich an ihr zu erfreuen!

Control Your Core 🔥 

Do you train to just complete the reps, or to ‘feel’ the movement? 🤔

Are you going through the motions with your exercises, or is each rep performed with quality? 🤔

One way to test if you have the right amount of control in a movement is to add a pause in the transitional phase 👊

By adding the pause in these 3 specific moves, you are consciously controlling the shortening & lengthening of your abdominals & obliques ➡️⬅️

Keep in mind, our muscles respond to the time spent under tension, rather than the amount of reps 💪

For example, perform 10 press-ups at ‘normal speed’ and see how you feel…

Then, perform just 1 press up lowering for 20 seconds pausing at the bottom for 20 seconds and pushing up for 20 seconds 🕰️ 

See which one you find harder, the 10 reps, or the 1… 😉

Save these 3 for your next core work 📥
