I got to do something this morning with my new friend @shelchen7.

We brought together a group of women of colour + friends who are into running, are interested in running, are re-entering running, etc. Nobody really cared about how fast or slow we each went. This was only a small part of what unfolded.

Truth be told that while I’ve wanted to be part of hosting something like this for a while now, I really did struggle with the concept. 

I don’t like excluding anybody.

I wasn’t raised like that (in fact, that was slapped out of me if I ever thought or behaved that way 👋🏾) nor do I think this way now, as a grown up. I like when everybody can do stuff together. It’s just better.

I can also appreciate how uncomfortable or intimidating it can be to enter a group of people and have that feeling of “everyone is better than me”. 

Running is definitely one of those things that can make one feel this way… particularly in a group setting.

The point today was the bring some people together to simply move our bodies (in the freezing cold no doubt), while being together, and then have time + space to connect and just chat. 

I’m so full of joy from today’s run + gathering. This is what can happen when you reduce a barrier in your mind and just say “sure I’ll come”. And, that can only really happen when it feels comfy to do so.

And thank you for my @lululemon famjam. Today only happened with your partnership. 

We’re doing this again on Jan 22. You’re invited. Stay tuned…

Today while rowing we did repeats of rowing with ours eyes closed. During that time I was hyper aware of the center of my body and if I was off balanced or not. I could feel if I was rushing the slide. I could hear and feel the depth of my oars in the water. That was followed by telling myself to take a deep breath and relax my shoulders. It’s not quite home yet but it’s getting there. Happy Sunday!!

Lululemon Athletica’s (LULU) stock is down 8% after the Vancouver-based athletic apparel retailer reported lower-than-expected profitability and issued weak forward guidance.

Lululemon’s gross margin, a key indicator of profitability, was 55.9% in this year’s third quarter, short of analysts’ average estimate of 56.7%. The Canadian retailer also reported a rise in inventory levels from a year earlier, raising the prospect of price markdowns in coming months.

Looking ahead, Lululemon raised its sales forecast for the full year to $7.99 billion. However, that was below analysts’ average estimate, causing the share price to fall in after hours trading.

Lululemon reiterated that it plans to double its sales by 2027 through the opening of more stores, expanding overseas, and selling more clothing items to men.

The company is also piloting a two-tier membership program to keep customers engaged.

Prior to the latest earnings release, Lululemon’s stock had declined 3% this year to trade at $374.51 U.S. per share.

Twenty years ago this Christmas season, a legend was born.
•
Jordan Birch and Chris Boyd had the idea to mark the holidays with dreadful threads — which came to be dubbed ugly Christmas sweaters.
•
They were both university students when they tried on matching penguin sweaters in a Coquitlam, B.C., mall and exchanged glances.
•
"We put them on and we died laughing," Birch said.
•
Today, both are acknowledged as the founders of the ugly Christmas sweater phenomenon after they organized a themed party at a friend's house.
•
They also own the Canadian trademark to the words "Ugly Christmas Sweater."
•
"Of course, the word 'ugly' and pairing that with a Christmas sweater wasn't common verbiage [at the time]. It was just the most jovial, ridiculous, silly party that we could imagine and it just snowballed from there," said Birch.
•
Over the years, ugly Christmas sweater parties have become a seasonal tradition around the world. Collections from Lululemon, Walmart and Amazon all pop up if you Google the words "ugly Christmas."
•
The demand for ugly Christmas sweaters has even reached the point where environmental advocates have begged consumers to stop buying mass-manufactured sweaters for fear of filling the oceans with micro-plastics.
•
"It would have been different circumstances now if Chris and I had monetized this at the very beginning," Birch said.
•
Instead, they decided early on that they didn't want to spend their lives trying to get rich off the ugly Christmas sweater. So they concentrated on holding events to raise money for charitable causes.
•
"Let's just stay in our lane, stay true to our hearts," said Birch.

HEAR NO EVIL! 
I was talking to this very nice woman that goes to the same gym as I do. She was telling me that she used to love to dance, but then one day her boyfriend at the time told her she had no rhythm.. This comment made such a big impact on her that she basically stopped dancing for years! She told me that she knew deep inside that she did indeed have rhythm, but for some reason it took her years to start dancing again. So, this conversation really hit home with me. Because that same day I had put these lululemon tights on that are shorter than what I normally would wear to the gym and I remembered a comment that was made to me by an ex-boyfriend that I had “big fat thighs”. So, the reason why I’m sharing this is to show how certain things can really mess with you and stay with you for a long time! So for now on let’s work on not listen to mean things,  and I hope to see my friend continue to dance her heart out! So often, we don’t have bad rhythm, or bad bodies- we only have bad taste in boyfriends! 💪🏼💜

To my young creative Jedi your relationship with a brand is only as strong as your relationship with the people who work for the brand. That’s why you gotta work hard on those personal relationships and be nice to people and everyone you come across once you enter the building. The security guard you ignore can turn into the CEO real quick and you don’t want your progress blocked because you wronged someone back in the day when they had no power. Also means that when people inevitably move roles they continue to look out for you as they ascend the food chain. 

When I first started deejaying and promos were like gold dust I realised that if you wanted the tunes then you had to make friends with the post room. Often ignored and berated the post room boys appreciated the coffee, donuts and sandwiches that the skinny African kid was bringing in which is how I got access to records that only the big boy Dj’s had. 

When you come from a place of disadvantage, low budgets and little resources you learn to be creative in pursuit of the dream. 

I swept up hair in a hairdressers in soho for many years to get my Channel 4 job on a youth program called ‘The Word’ 

Worked in a school dinners kitchen to fund £200 courier flights to New York to absorb the culture when my friends were content with watching from afar on MTV. 

At our @lululemon dinner yesterday we were asked to write down our strengths which despite my prowess with the pen was surprisingly difficult to do. Sometimes you take yourself for granted and fail to see the goodness and power inside you. What I’ve learnt is that writing it down somehow tricks my brain into believing my powers are real. So at the moment I feel like I’m a catalyst, for change, am good at persuading people to try the impossible and strive to always bring positive energy into the spaces where I enter. 

Try writing down your powers, pin them up on a wall and navigate the day as if they were real. You might feel a bit silly being honest with the paper but it’s one step closer to manifesting and making things happen. I mean if you don’t believe in yourself how can you get people to believe in you…..

Let’s add some spice to the oldie but goodie, Side Sit Up aka Mermaid. Whenever I add spice I like to start with the original version first and slowly mix in the spice because each spicey addition should emulate the the original exercise. Adding weights or props to a classical or familiar exercise is the easiest way to add spice and variety. As you can see here I started with the original side sit up variation to establish the movement and proper form. Next I added the weight to the side body lift. Because it’s basically the same movement my cues will easily carry over.  The form and muscle activation is pretty much the same for every variation making it a natural transition for my clients. For every variation I cue:
1. Squeeze the top glute to keep the hips stacked. 2. Lift from the pelvic floor and maintain the shoulder girdle connection. 3. Cinch the rib to hip on the body lift. Happy #TechniqueTipTuesday! This week we are going over an exercise you will see in our current weightwork series with the tube. 

-The tube is there to add a balance challenge, but also resistance in your added thigh work. Obviously your arms are your first priority here, so the tube just adds a bonus for your lower body. 
-In the beginning of the series, we start with an extension with one leg up and the tube around your ankles. Keep the tube nice and tight with your leg lifted to stretch it out so there is no “lax”. This will not only give you the best work for the top of your thigh, but it will also help you balance. The resistance gives you something to work against, so it automatically engages your core to help you stay in that balance. 
-Keep the resistance through your arms too. Imagine like you are pushing through thick cement as you press your arms up and pull them down. 
-If the balance on one leg is too much to get good work in your arms, you can always take both feet down hip width apart parallel on the floor so you can focus on just your arms. 

Stay tuned for next week’s tip!

Santosha = acceptance, contentment. The second niyama of Patanjali's yoga sutras.

The pursuit of happiness. We spend a lot of time chasing happiness, but happiness is fleeting. Happiness is found in moments, but it's unrealistic to think we can always stay there. For a long time I thought I was failing at life because I couldn't manage to stay happy all the time. It was a relief to finally learn that what I was chasing wasn't at all realistic. 

Santosha invites us to accept the moment, our lives, and ourselves as they are... to recognize that what we truly need already exists within. This doesn't mean we can't enjoy things, moments, others; on the contrary. When we recognize our inherent wholeness, we know our contentment is not dependent on anything outside of ourselves. And so this awareness frees us to experience life as it comes and goes, without grasping or clinging. Funny how recognizing that we don't truly need anything we open ourselves to an entire universe of experiences and blessings. 🙏💞

Acceptance --> gratitude --> contentment --> a whole new experience of happiness 💖🕉️

 Философия этого бренда мне очень близка, в первую очередь этот бренд  про теннисную эстетику, которая сейчас так актуальна в мире спорта и даже моды. .

.

For office workers who spend 9 to 5 in the heart of Boston, there is no dress code, no policy, and no certainty anymore. Retailers used COVID to peddle new categories of clothing, like “workleisure,” “power casual,” or the most straightforward contender: “hybrid workwear.”

“We’re coming out of style hibernation,” said Kenlyn Jones, an assistant professor of fashion design at the Massachusetts College of Art and Design. “Not too fussy, not too difficult. It’s just true to the wearer, joyful and relaxed.”

A few words of wisdom about how I have been able to create an impact, through personal fundraising and with my Team at LMO.
 
“I have personally raised a record amount this year and feel that just reaching out in the past was not good enough. This year’s approach was to start with a very personal approach in the opening state where I send all my contacts a personal message.  This has taken hours and days to complete but made a significant impact, but what has made my campaign so successful was the multiple follow up on these notes and the sharing of the growing of the Mo with pictures that are a little cheeky. 
 
“This has been a huge amount of WhatsApp messages, emails and IG posts and rather labour intensive but it has generated a better return via social media and enabled me to raise many funds”.
 
My Team at The Landmark Mandarin Oriental, Hong Kong  and I have also gone above and beyond by way of support in the past years. In 2022,  this included serving exclusive Mo cocktails and chocolate drinks at the MO Bar, as well as a MO Moffy post-meal cocktails, available at SOMM and Amber, all donating part of the proceeds to Movember.  In addition, for every guest visiting The Oriental Spa, HK$20 has been donated to support the awareness of men’s wellness, while throughout the month, Team LMO has been growing a Mo or moving for 60 hours.  It’s a legendary effort!

5 Beginner TRX Exercises 🔥 

As SO MANY of you got your hands on a TRX in the massive Black Friday sale, here are 5 exercises to get you started on the straps! 🤝

1. TRX Squat

(Short/Medium Straps)
- Start this move with bent arms and have your body at a slight angle. 
- Lower down by pushing your hips back and straightening the arms. 
- Drive through your heels and push the ground away back to a stand.

2. TRX Low Row 

(Short Straps)
- Facing to TRX, either lift to toes so you are on your heels, or keep your feet flat on the floor
- Keep shoulders down into back pockets with your chest and chin up
- Pull the body towards the straps until your hands reach your tip cage
- Squeeze the lats (side of back). Hold at the top for 1 second before lengthening the arms.

3. TRX Reverse Lunge

(Short Straps)
- Facing the TRX with the straps pulled tight and your elbows tucked into your rib cage
- Lower down into a lunge, lowering the back knee to the floor
- Drive up back to a stand position and repeat

4. TRX High Row

(Short Straps) 
- Facing the TRX with short straps 
- This is similar to the ‘Low Row’, but with your hands face down
- Pull the elbows high in line with your chin
- Squeeze upper back together as if you are squeezing a pen between your shoulder blades!

5. TRX Hamstring Curls

(Knee Height Straps)
- Drive your heels down into the foot cradles and elbows into the floor by your side
- Pull your heels towards your bum
- Pause at the top of the movement then slowly extend the legs away

I hope this helps get you started, or even remind you of a few technique points to improve your TRX training 💪

The use of vegan, next-gen and other Earth-friendly materials is not a fad. Without wishing to get too cynical – that’s just not what we do here – there are plenty of fashion brands working under the guise of sustainability to sell more stuff: a touch of recycled plastic here, a dash of upcycled cotton there. But a small percentage of recycled materials does not offset the impact of using tons of virgin materials. Products last longer than a PR headline.

It’s all a question of commitment. How committed are brands to reducing their impact on the planet? Materials startup Bolt Threads is asking that question to the brands it partners with. Its new Greener Pastures Pledge initiative requires brands to pledge to eliminate their use of virgin leather. In return, brands will get preferential access to Mylo, Bolt Threads’ mycelium-based alternative.

The initiative comes with backing from Ganni which launched a wallet made with Mylo in June. Plenty of other brands have worked with the leather alternative including Stella McCartney, adidas and lululemon, which means we could be seeing some big names pledging to eliminate virgin leather very soon. And if big names commit then that should result in substantial reductions in animal leather use.

You can read more about Bolt Threads and the Greener Pastures Pledge on FUTUREVVORLD.com.

"These strong traffic results were achieved despite 1) similar or lower year over year discounting levels, and/or 2) discounting activity below total sector averages," the analysts said. My favourite movie of all time is Rudy, about a boy with a dream to play football at the University of Notre Dame.

One of my favourite scenes from the movie is when he finally gets accepted at Notre Dame, after completing a few semesters at Holy Cross College. He reads the acceptance letter on a bench outside Moreau Seminary, and then jogs down to the path along Saint Josephs Lake. One of the iconic shots from that scene is when the camera pans back and you get a view of the famous Golden Dome across the lake.

It's always been a dream to meet Rudy and check out some of the spots where the movie was filmed. Today I got to realize one of those dreams when I took a detour on my way to Ontario from Minnesota and visited the University of Notre Dame campus in South Bend, Indiana.

Although the bench from the movie is no longer there, you can see where it was anchored in the ground, and there is a bench on the other side of the path.

After taking a photo of me sitting on the bench, I decided to fly up my drone and get a clip of me throwing an MTA on the lawn outside Moreau Seminary, with a view of the Golden Dome in the background. The soundtrack in the MTA video is from the movie, titled "Tryouts".

If you haven't watched the movie, it is based on a true story and has some special moments.

The real Rudy became a motivational speaker and I have to think that part of the reason I do what I do is because of this movie, which I have watched many times over the years.

A big reason I connect with the movie and story is because my father is my real-life Rudy, a college football player who was selected as an All-Canadian in 1975 at Acadia University.

I have a lot of gratitude today for creating a path that allows me the opportunity to experience moments like this 🙏

A Blessed Thanksgiving 2022..I pray that we keep the feeling and sentiment of gratitude in our lives and heart year-long….

Cultivating a mind-set of #gratitude is proving to be about much more than the manners of a “thank you.” Instead, the principles of #thanksgiving give importance to a #unique way of seeing the world. Evidence suggests that the depth of the #emotion of gratitude is key, not only to our #happiness but also essential to overall #health and well-being:

• It helps to combat #stress and #anxiety lowering #blood pressure, while increasing #energy productivity, and greater #optimism …And, gratitude has been linked to slowing down some of the effects of neurodegeneration that often occurs with age.

• According to UCLA’s Mindfulness Awareness Research Center, expressing gratitude regularly (defined in their studies as the quality of being thankful and readiness to show appreciation), literally changes the molecular structure of the brain. It helps to keep our brain functioning and makes us happier – and more positive. Additional healthy benefits are linked to greater productivity and focus while maintaining an active lifestyle.

• Researchers have found that gratitude lights up the brain’s #reward pathways. And #people who show more gratitude, also had a higher-functioning hypothalamus —  the brain’s center for managing stress, #metabolism and #sleep 

• The Institute of HeartMath Research Center has found that positive emotions like appreciation, significantly lowered levels of the stress hormone, cortisol.

• Robert Emmons, Ph.D., University of California-Davis professor, and director of the university’s Emmons Lab, which creates and shares scientific #data on gratitude (its causes, and its potential effects on #human health and well-being), calls gratitude: “the forgotten factor in the science of well-being." @lululemon #lululemon #family

How often do you incorporate movements that address your weak links? 

We like to do things we’re good at,

So we continue to do that. 😃

We don’t like doing things we suck at,

So we neglect them. 🤨

It’s why some of us absolutely love to squat, and hate a bicep pump. And why some of us hate a split squat but love to sprint. 

Here’s the thing: if you want to expand your capabilities, or even just continue moving pain free: 

You’re going to have to do the things you aren’t good at, and the things you neglect are gonna have to be addressed. 

If you literally do the SAME things everyday you will develop some imbalance. I almost guarantee it. 

My weak point has been my hips / gluteus’s medius, and my deep lateral core muscles. 

If you scroll through the last few months of training you can see I’ve been doing a lot of abductions/ adduction work, side planks, lateral core work, all of the things that run on the outside or even inside of my body. 

Here’s 2 EMOMs I did a few weeks ago during my light weight full body day:

EMOM 1 (12 minutes long, every minute on the minute I did:)
💡10 TRX Rowa
💡Remainder of minute hold 1/2 side plank + Abduction Hold (switch sides each round)

EMOM 2 (12 minutes long, every minute on the minute I did:)
💡12 Walking Lunges
💡 Remainder of Minute choice of cardio 

—-

So you can see how I sprinkle in the things I’m bad at into my sessions.

Odds are you’ll actually end up liking the things you suck at if you do them enough, because when you do them enough you get better at them. And we like doing the things we’re good at😏

Discovering a clothing item you instantly fall in love with can be a visceral experience. The French call it coup de coeur—love at first sight. This was the inspiration for outerwear brand @capedecoeur, with capes in seven styles: The Artiste, The Sainte, The Celestine, The Guardian, The Poet, and new this fall, The Messenger and The Classicist.

The Vancouver-based company was founded by Austrian-born designer Bettina Mueller Reichl (@bettina_mueller_reichl). With over 20 years’ design experience, including with Lululemon Athletica and Kit and Ace, she is no stranger to technical performance wear. Cape de Coeur’s proprietary textile CoeurTex is an ultrasoft, four-way-stretch wind-, rain-, and snowproof fabric custom made in Europe.

For Reichl, the outerwear space needed a facelift. “There is this idea in design, especially luxury design, that ‘the look’ of a garment is its central purpose,” she says. “For us, aesthetic is of course imperative to what we do and certainly a focus, however function is of equal value.”

 また、指導者養成講座でせっかくヨガの資格を手にしたけど、教える場所や機会がないと卒業生からよく聞くことがあります。
僕自身教える場所がなかったから、自分のヨガスタジオを立ち上げたりしました。

まだ法整備もできていないし正直ピースが欠落しているところが多いと思っています。

ただ時代の流れの中で実現できるんじゃないかって思っています。
少し未来になるかもしれないけど、この「THE VILLAGE」がこのヨガ3.0という世界観の土台になったらいいなと思っています。

Most of us know how important it is to practice gratitude. Research has linked gratitude with a wide range of benefits, including strengthening the immune system, improving sleep patterns, feeling optimistic, experiencing more joy and pleasure, being more helpful and generous, and feeling less lonely and isolated. When we cultivate a grateful heart we WIN!!! ✨ Do you set time daily to pause to reflect on gratitude? Here are a few ways to practice. Remember to be fully present and FEEL it. Embody it! 

💕Keep a gratitude journal and add to it everyday.

💕Meditate with your gratitude list, giving thanks for all you have.

💕Post quotes and images that remind you to be grateful around your home.

💕Tell someone you love them and how much you appreciate them.

💕Make gratitude a part of family life, share it with each other during meal time.

💕Write a thank you card to someone you care about.

💕Give back and volunteer for organizations that help others.

Full circle | bucket list moment 🪄🫶🏼💫

One of my first jobs out of college when I moved to NYC was as a seasonal educator at lululemon on 75th + Broadway. #uws 

I had less than $500 to my name when I made the move and slept on a blow up air mattress in my friends’ Harlem apartment for 3 months. Bless @veryseanmcgee + @jamardrich 

It was cold, I was heartbroken from a big break up, I was very low in self confidence. I had zero clue of what I really wanted to do with my life and my gifts.

While it was one of the more challenging seasons of my life it also became one of the most beautiful ones because of the lululemon community taking me in both personally and professionally as a member of their team + family.

It was the first place that I started to learn about the power of having a vision and setting up your life to be in alignment with your core values.

When I decided to make the move to Aspen and knowing only 1 special person @aliewalshdame at the time, Aspen lululemon team also swooped me up here, gave me a job, a home, a community, + so much opportunity to explore my bigger passions in life of becoming a yoga teacher + now transformational coach.

My job is to help people see themselves fully. To see their power, their light, and truly embody their wholeness to the core.

And in my experience, when I started to really see myself more fully and embrace all that I am, life began to roll out the red carpet of miracles for me.

To be seen as a leader and ambassador in my community is very humbling and heart warming. I’ve always felt that Aspen is my forever home and moments like this feel even more life affirming + confirming.

✨Get clear on what you want
✨Do the inner work to clear and integrate what’s holding you back
✨Take aligned action every day
✨Then surrender your desires to the universe and trust the timing of your unfolding.

Thank you for seeing me, @lululemon and the important humans a part of my experience 🍋 

I see you too! I will do my best to return that gift to my community this year!

PR ALERT!

Not for me 😅, but for most of the RUN SQUAD 🔥 Congrats y’all! Not only for running your best race, but for showing up for yourself, trusting the process, and putting in the work to get here!

A PR would have been great, but I knew that wasn’t going down, and in the back of my mind I would have liked to go sub 19:30, but my main goal for this race was to chill the F out.

My race day anxiety generally starts 2 days early 😅. My stomach gets tied up in knots that get tighter the closer we get to race day. My body starts to feel heavy and the idea of holding the paces I know that I am capable of seems impossible. I start self sabotaging by eating a bunch of junk food, drinking less water, and getting crappy sleep.

And for what?!

My friends and family won’t love or respect me less for not running a faster time. My income doesn’t hinge on my race performance. My dogs certainly aren’t interested in my split times.

This race I made an effort to take myself a little less seriously and guess what… I only had to use the bathroom 1 time before the race! #iykyk 😅

It was another awesome event by @jandaracing and I’m proud of my performance! 

For y’all nosey folk (like me) 😂

FAMILY

Fitness Family

As I continue reflecting on all the families in my life, I wanted to talk about my fitness family.

A sports kid, I got to drama school and luckily had friends who wanted to go lift at the gym (I’m looking at you @bmulls327 Chris @carllundsteady @jbuckwald ) while I got on a treadmill in orange vans and tried to run 3 miles as fast as I could (I know what you’re thinking, “yep, checks out”). Which led to me turning to @jonjorgenson in church, and saying, “I think I wanna run a marathon…in 3 weeks.” (Again, “yep, checks out.”) I didn’t know it, but my fitness family was starting to grow and was lifting me up (literally…cause I couldn’t walk after the race). 

My fitness community continued growing when I first tried @tonehouse .  I had just started at lululemon (love you flatiron/union square squad) when one day, @biancapaigefit challenged me to take a class because I had said, “I wasn’t a big fan of group fitness”. I showed up, got my ass kicked, limped outside, called @mamajen.nicholas and said “I think I just found a new obsession”.

Whether it was @ycoolj training me/telling me my pullups were ass, or the many athletes who waxed me in speed work, Tone House helped me cultivate a mindset of getting faster and stronger always…again, community.

This led the guy who wasn’t a big fan of fitness, to teach at TWO different fitness joints (love you @soulcycle and @barrys ) but also led me to @spartan .  Four years of races, two top-3 finishes, four North American Championship qualifications, three World Championship qualifications, and so much blood, sweat and tears… I couldn’t have done it without, you guessed it, my community.

Finally, what started out as a simple message from @zoiii3 telling me I should run @hyroxworld led to a first in my age group in my first Hyrox race, last spring, to a 1st Overall in the Men’s division, 2 weeks ago.  A feat I never would’ve imagined when I started my fitness journey. 

Why am I going on and on about this? Because, I didn’t know it at the time, but with each step, my fitness family was radically changing my life for the better.  To everyone along the way…thank you.  We’re just getting started.

Алимжан @alimzhan_canada — работает IT-рекрутером в Ванкувере, Канада. Он рассказал о том, как происходит отбор специалистов в IT на местном рынке. 
 
Я уехал в Канаду по студенческой визе в 2016 году и получил ПМЖ. Я работал в банке, занимался фандрайзингом для благотворительности и когда осознал, что мое призвание в продажах — решил попробовать себя в рекрутинге. Канадский IT-рынок достаточно мощный, поэтому я выбрал именно IT-рекрутинг. 

Компания TEKsystems в которой я работаю, предоставляет рекрутинг услуги для всех крупных IT-компаний на рынке Северной Америки с 1994 года. Помимо Ванкуверского офиса, у нас также есть офисы в Торонто, Оттаве, Монреале и Калгари. Наши клиенты — это lululemon, Amazon, Microsoft, Salesforce, Big Five Banks, государственный сектор и многие другие компании. 

Для того, чтобы работать с ТЕКsystems необходимо иметь разрешение на работу, квалификации в виде сертификатов и канадский опыт в IT. Вы можете работать как контрактник или постоянный сотрудник на полную ставку. IT-специалисты в постоянном спросе и могут получать по несколько звонков от рекрутеров в день. Поэтому важно отличаться от конкурентов на рынке, показывая реальную заинтересованность в консультанте и в желании построить долгосрочные трудовые отношения с ними.

Do you struggle with mental health? Especially in winter?🤍❄️

My gosh you are not alone, I went on my story today to say how bad my mental health has been the last 4-8 weeks. Like literally the worst, I’m not sure why, probably has something to do with burn out. I have zero energy, truly.

I mentioned how it’s important to show up and put the effort on the days you don’t feel like it but some days you can’t show up and that’s okay. Some weeks I’ve worked out 7x and sometimes 3, sometimes I have to force myself to train lol- yes it happens.

I have been looking at ways to move my body because something is better than nothing and those ways can look like ; yoga, walking, spin class- I’m starting to get into skiing.

For so long I felt like I had to force myself to workout all the time, if I didn’t I had intense guilt. I’ve grown and accepted that some days aren’t good days.

Try to wake up with a positive attitude every morning, be kind to yourself and listen to what you need 🫶🏽

Always prioritize yourself and your health, mentally and physically. I’m slowly feeling better but it’s the longest depressive state I’ve been in a while.

The photo is from tonight’s workout, I didn’t want to go but it turned out to be a really solid and productive leg day, which I enjoyed.

Take care of your body because you love yourself, not because you hate yourself- I say this because I need to hear it and I’m sure you do too.

I love you🥹

Shooting races is hard. That’s why I love them. 

I find joy in the challenges of photography. Mixed light, harsh shadows, fleeting moments? Yes, please. 

In races, there are no redos. Forget creative control, a race is not going to wait for you to adjust exposure or nail focus. 

A race isn’t contained on some cute court or grass field with lines. No, your subjects are going to be actively running from you as fast as they can go, not caring about what’s behind them, or how their down stride face looks.

Want another shot of your subject? Sprint ahead, flip the hips, backpedal, compose, shoot, repeat. Current background not ideal? Just run further, run faster, only 6.2 miles to go. 

Some things make the challenge easier. All involve trust. 

On the lululemon 10k tour I was lucky to have great partners in @kindlyproductions. I shot knowing that great photographers (@stefaniacurto @jaybendlinphoto @fredis_b ) had my back. 

Just as important was having the trust of @robynfarnham and everyone at @lululemon. Thank you for the challenge. 

(PS for the run-photo nerds, shooting above f/3.2 is for cowards 😎 Shoot wide open, you’ll feel more alive!)

A wise philosopher from Compton once shared a timeless piece of advice for self care:

“Check yo self  before you wreck yo self.”

I needed to catch up with one of my girls AND I needed to walk. There is a version of Tasha that would have felt like she needed to sacrifice herself to be there for someone else. This expectation was put ON me BY me.

This version of Tasha does things differently and so we set up a time to talk when I could get to the gym to get my walking done. 

I cared for myself (I walked a 5K) and was able to care for her and everybody felt fulfilled. And there is nothing wrong with that. 

You can do two things at once. You do NOT have to sacrifice your well-being to care for others. You are actually in a better position to care for others when you feel fulfilled and well. 

You know what I can’t do two of though? Sleeves. Anytime I’m walking at the gym, I always have one arm in a long sleeve shirt (my perfectly oversized cropped crew sweater from @lululemon) and one arm out. Oh well. 

Take care of yourselves ‘cause putting yourself last is bad for your health.

this tattoo has been on my wrist for 9 years. the Sanskrit Yama for non-attachment reminds me not to hold on to things, not to be greedy or possessive. 

when I got it, I was grasping at expectations- of myself, of relationships, of what I wanted out of life. holding on so tightly that these things would shatter into pieces right in front of me.

over the years, the meaning has shifted depending on my season of life but it remains my most important and relevant tattoo (thankfully it’s right where I can see it).

right now it’s reminding me that when you hold on too tight to something, your palm is closed. you cannot receive (or be given) anything more or different to what you already have. you think that what you have is the best thing you could possibly hold, but you aren’t open to other possibilities.

when you loosen your grip, your palm is open to seek and find something you didn’t realize you could hold. you have the ability to hold multiple things, or to let go of one or all of them.  but you increase your options and potential. 

open hands. open mind. open heart.

complex core 🫧🤤👈🏼 

Hope this info is easy to digest;

I’d really prefer to sprinkle movements like this into my bigger sessions, but it’s also totally fine to do them all on their own… 

On my cardio days, if I have time I’ll spend some working on movements like this,

Just tends to make more sense (time & efficiency wise) to do these sprinkled into your other sessions to build a resilient core 

Are you getting tired of me talk about how important core training is yet?? 

Well I’m tired of just seeing “ab” workouts online :/ 

Probably isn’t worth your time to spend hours isolating your abs. 

Slide 1: High Tension Isometric: Holding the roller in between my knee and elbow by activity flexing my abs 

Slide 2: Creating and controlling lateral flexion 

Slide 3: Resisting lateral flexion by placing a heavy DB on one side of me. Forcing my core to hold my body straight rather than falling to one side. 

Slide 4: Creating and holding core rotation. We move in more than one dimension as humans, so why would we only train going forward and backward or up and down? 

Slide 5: Resisting rotation by keeping my hips and shoulders squared forward as I move the band out and in. 

Slide 6: Actively flexing on a ball that follows your spines natural curve a little better. Not worrying about crunching all the way but rather focusing on letting my abs do the work for a big stretch and a big squeeze

Berkshire buyin': On Monday, iconic investor Warren Buffett announced that his firm Berkshire Hathaway had purchased a $4.1bn stake in Taiwanese chipmaker TSMC during the last few months. Known to have missed the early wave of investments in tech, passing early on Google and Amazon, Buffett and co. are now — selectively — embracing the industry. A 2016 investment in Apple has worked out spectacularly well, with the iPhone maker now Berkshire’s largest holding, equivalent to a 5.5% stake in the company.⁠
⁠
Although notable, the TSMC investment still barely makes a dent in the holding company’s 12-figure outstanding cash pile. Berkshire’s $108bn is an amount that, at current market prices, could theoretically buy Lululemon ($45bn), Snap ($18bn), Dominos Pizza ($18bn), Spotify ($14bn), Peloton ($5bn), Lyft ($4bn) and soccer team Manchester United ($4bn). Or, if Buffett wanted to put all of his eggs in one basket, he could go for PayPal ($102bn), Target ($87bn)... or two-and-a-bit Twitters (which seemingly go for $44bn a piece).⁠
⁠
Slow and steady wins the race⁠
⁠
After years in which high-growth, expensive, companies have been in vogue, Buffett’s unflashy value investing strategy might begin to identify bargains again, as stock markets have slumped so far this year.⁠
⁠
Indeed, after 40+ years of outperforming the market, Berkshire Hathaway is still on top. Over the last 12-months, shares in BRK are up 10%, whilst the S&P 500 is down 14% over the same time period.⁠

HOW TO DRESS FOR A WINTER RUN!

For all weather conditions with 🥶❄️ winter running that we’ll experience, here are my go-to staples for my winter runs!

💜Trail Running Shoes for Waterproof Footwear. Especially since they have an extra grip when it’s all sloshy and wet outdoors!
💜Compression socks because of the snug fit and the nature of the compression sock to avoid blisters and protect the Achilles tendon! They also help facilitate blood flow! I’m a @procompression fan if you need a rec!
💜Leggings or tights for when it’s cold out. However, either can be restrictive for faster workouts. I’m a fan of shorts with knee-high compression socks for more challenging workouts and tights with high socks for conversational-paced runs. Make sure you get sweat-wicking fabric suitable for the wet conditions that winter running conditions bring! 😉
💜Wear several layers of long-sleeved tops on top of a tank top if you’re not wearing a jacket. I tucked my layers into my leggings to keep the warm air into heat my core. It works! I have a TON of these tops and found a generic brand on Amazon that’s affordable and a bang for your buck because it does the job and keeps ya warm! Since I am rarely running indoors and not a treadmill girl, I’m braving the cold all winter long!
💜I love my running @lululemon running gloves, and ONLY with my @hothandswarmers! If I had to pick ONE absolute winter running staple I need on every run, it’s these! At times, I can tend to become slightly anemic when running heavier mileage during a marathon build, and as a result, my fingers freeze, and I almost feel cold-blooded. I know you or someone you know can relate! @hothandswarmers ARE HEROES FOR US. ALL OF US!
💜A snug beanie or a head warmer keep heat in my head, my ears warm, and my head in the game. Such a game-changer!
💜Depending on HOW cold we’re talking about, I will also have a neck warmer to keep my neck warm; it gets so cold out there, regardless of the pace I’m pushing!

I perform my dynamic warm-up drills and core activation indoors before braving the cold before every run! It makes the cold more bearable from the get-go! 😁🙌🏻

It's that time of year, where we go out for a run and we are so bundled up, we hardly recognize our friends 😄 

That is just the way it is running in winter weather places, and I LOVE it. 

Yes it's cold, but so much better then a treadmill, in my humble opinion.  Being out in the world in the fresh air.  

So here are my top winter running tips: 

🔦🦺 Always dress reflective and have a light.  So that you are visible to the cars and you can see where you are going.  

🧥 Dress warm, but not too warm.  If you are just a little bit cold when you step out the door then you are dressed perfect, because you will warm up once you get moving. 

🧤 Don't forget good gloves and hats.  

👟 Make sure your shoes have good traction on the snow and ice.  Trail shoes work great, or cleats.

I dreamt of this space. 
I dream of this space. 
Since 2016 the seed had been planted. 

It wakes me up in the middle of the night — all of this. 
Sometimes because I’m so excited — other times because my brain wants to remind me I haven’t ordered toilet paper for the bathroom there yet — other times it’s because theres this weird guilty weight of feeling like I’m ruining my business partners life on my chest as we go over budget — and most of the time it’s because I’m just wanting to get out of bed + be there. 

I don’t want to sleep if it means stepping away from there. 
I want to sleep there because I feel like it’s changing so fast even though it’s also at times so… painfully slow. 
I want to soak it all in because as much as I want to always be able to come back to this moment — it just won’t always be possible to this depth. 
I want to just timelapse the entire process to obsess over its evolution. 
I want to bring the hundreds of people in my corner and make my eyes their lens so they can be along for every bit of this, too. Because it’s truly something else — the people that circulate without us even being open. 

Because I dreamt of this space. 
I dream of this space. 
2016 I began my yoga instructor journey while working at lululemon — and one of the first community events I was put on was “local yoga cafe” — a coffee shop + yoga studio in west chester. My vision was always a studio of some sort — and as I started to spend so many days within this concept, it began to leave its imprint on me and I knew I wanted something of its kind one day. 

Every journal, every vision + goal session, every guided meditation where I could see the rest of my life came back to this space. This wellness cafe. Whatever it was — and now it’s here. 

People keep saying “I am so happy + excited for you”, and I will never stop saying that I am so happy + excited for US. Because so many of you weren’t lucky enough to experience The Local when it existed. So many of you haven’t been able to feel that communal space + what it does for your mental health. 

We are so close to being here together + I want to document as much as I can to hold onto it all.. tight.

Os tons pasteis são destaque para esse efeito e visa repassar uma calma e bem-estar no visual;

Conjuntos monocromáticos ou tom sobre tom são destaque nos lançamentos para o Inverno 2023 nessa estética;

Para atemporalidade, as peças surgem em sua maioria lisas ou com logotipo minimalista.

AZUL
O tom pastel do azul é destaque para a moda feminina e masculina.
Conjuntos de malha ajustados ao corpo de top e legging ganham evidência para as mulheres.
Peças mais soltas como regatas e camisas também surgem nesta cor.

ROSA

Destaque principalmente para calças legging e bermudas biker.

VERDE

Aposte na cor principalmente para peças da parte superior, como camisas, tops e casacos.

WAS BEWIRKT DER BAUM IM YOGA FÜR DICH?
Die Baumstellung ist eine sehr gute Asana, um die Muskeln in deinem Standbein zu stärken - von der Hüfte bis zum Fuß. Sie hilft dir auch, Kraft und Länge im Rumpf und in der gesamten Wirbelsäule zu gewinnen, was dir wiederum hilft, deine Haltung von innen nach außen zu verbessern.
Abgesehen davon ist Vrksasana eine Yogastellung, die die Leisten und Adduktoren dehnt und die Hüften öffnet. Außerdem dehnt sie subtil  Brust und Schultern.
Der wahrscheinlich größte Vorteil dieser Haltung ist die gute Wirkung auf den Gleichgewichtssinn, die Konzentration auf die Atmung und die Erdung. Die Stabilität dieser Haltung trägt dazu bei, die Denkaktivität und auch das Nervensystem zu beruhigen.  Ein guter Gleichgewichtssinn und ein starker Rumpf sind unerlässlich, wenn du nachhaltig aktiv und gesund bleiben willst.
🤸🏽‍♂️🧘‍♂️🕉🙏

WHAT DOES TREE POSE DO FOR YOU?
Tree pose is a very good asana to strengthen the muscles in your standing leg - from the hips to the foot. It also helps you gain strength and length in the torso and throughout the entire backbone, helping you to improve your posture inside-out
Apart from this, Vrksasana is a yoga pose that stretches your groin and adductors, opening up your hips. It gives you as well a subtle stretch of the chest and shoulders.
Likely the biggest benefit of this pose is the positive effect it has on your sense of balance, helping you to focus and breath and grounding. The stability in this pose helps to calmdown your thinking activity and also your nervous system.  A good sense of balance and a strong core are essential if you want to stay active and healthy.

Alo or lululemon?

The truth is: I hated how I looked 
in this picture when I was first told this was the photo going up on the walls of @lululemon 

Every time I would look at it, it triggered an obsession of self deprecating thoughts. I became obsessed with picking apart the way my stomach and armpits looked. Instead of celebrating my dreams coming true from my hard work, I cried on and off for hours when someone sent me a “sneak peak” of the shot being mounted on the wall. 

It’s been over a decade long struggle with bulimia and binge eating disorder. And as a chef’s daughter; food is still, and will forever be a big part of my life.

I’m currently at 18 months and this has been my longest stretch of recovery from my binge-purge cycle. ✨

There is so much shame and guilt associated with these disorders, especially in the yoga community. This is a stigma I’m determined to shine light on, and help change during my tenure as an Ambassador. 

I now look at this picture with extreme fortitude and happiness. I see a human being up there with flaws, that make her unique and real, and I’m really fucking proud of her. 

So here’s me on my soap box letting everyone and anyone who is or has ever struggled with the journey to loving themselves know, that you are not alone. 🖤

El pasado sábado 12 de noviembre una de las citas más esperadas en cuanto a moda deportiva tenía lugar por fin. La firma canadiense lululemon organizaba un evento muy, pero que muy especial en Green Patio, una antigua imprenta de Madrid transformada en el espacio perfecto para esta celebración. Fue en ese enclave donde casi doscientas personas invitadas por la marca se reunieron con el objetivo de practicar ejercicio y pasar una mañana de sábado diferente, llena de música y mucho deporte. 

Tras el éxito de la apertura de su tienda online, lululemon aterrizó en España físicamente el pasado 2 de septiembre en Passeig de Gràcia, Barcelona. Solo dos semanas después se abrían las puertas de su nuevo espacio en la Calle Serrano de Madrid, y las colas eran tan largas como cabría esperar. No es para menos, lululemon se ha consolidado como la firma de moda deportiva de culto en países como Estados Unidos o Canadá, y en cuestión de un mes y medio, también en nuestro país. Por eso, este era el momento perfecto para aquello que tan bien define la firma y la que constituye una de sus razones de ser: crear comunidad.

Happy #TechniqueTipTuesday!! This week we are going over one of the sections of our new warm up with hand weights! We will be talking about straight arm plank, and then transitioning into side plank. 

-While up on your hands with 1 weight in your hand, make sure your feet are slightly wider than your hips. This will make it easier to balance and to keep your shoulders and hips squared off to the floor.
-Hold the tuck and hold your core strong so that way you can keep your hips and your shoulders even to the floor and pointing down.
-As you lift your arm to the side, you need to stabilize through your core so you don’t lean over. Your goal is to keep your entire body in place, even when your arm is lifting.
-Hold your arm at a T at shoulder height when the teacher cues you to rotate to your side plank, stack your hips and shoulders to face the side wall. Keep your arm reaching forward at shoulder height.
-Squeeze your side obliques to lift your hips to the ceiling.

Cold Season Mental Health Tips 🥶

Watch Your News Intake 🗞️
Try limiting your news exposure to 30 minutes, then shifting your attention to something more uplifting, positive tv shows or movies you enjoy.

Start a Gratitude Journal 📔 
Take five minutes a day, and keeping a gratitude journal can significantly elevate your mood and mental outlook. At the end of each day, write down at least one thing that you are grateful for that day. 

Bundle Up and Go Outside 🧣
30 minutes of moderate exercise a day can boost your energy, help you sleep better, and improve your mood thanks to the endorphins that are released in your brain. Bundle up with your mates and go for a walk with some hot cocoa.

Meditate 🧘🏾‍♀️ 
You know this one was definitely on my top five. Meditation is a good practice, even if only for five to ten minutes a day. Try to do it once a day whether in the morning, afternoon, or evening. 

Stay Connected 📲
Don’t retreat into further isolation because it’s harder to get together with friends and family due to flu, Covid, and other cold weather illness. Continue to safely see your network either virtually, through bundled-up outdoor activities, or just regular phone calls. Loneliness can be devastating to your mental health, so try to nurture your connections, even if your instinct is to hibernate. 

Stay warm hearted my yoga friends ❤️

One of the fun things about having my ambassador pic up in @lululemon are the texts and messages I get from people posing with my picture. 

Saturday, I got this message from one of my Zumba ladies:

“She shouted and the whole store heard her say:” mom! It’s your Zumba coach - how awesome!!!” With a squeal 🙌🏼🥰” 

This baby was a baby when her mom started taking my class. Not only did it make me feel some type of way for her to shut the store on my behalf 😂 but it means that I had made enough impression on her mom that she had shown her my face at one point or another and talked me as her “Zumba coach.” 

Sometimes group fitness calls feel like a thankless job. It’s a lot of practicing, a lot of putting your body through the ringer and a lot of money. But when you put on that mic and start that music, you are affecting lives far beyond what you can see or comprehend; possibly for generations to come.

If no one has told you, you are respected and appreciated. I know the struggle. I know the stress. I know the tears. I know the fight to call what we do a “real” job (that’s another post). You had the guts to lead and I’m proud of you. 

For everyone reading this post, keep going. You don’t have to have your picture on the wall. Just have the desire to help people be their best selves in your heart, including yourself. 

Happy Monday! ✨☀️💙🙏🏿

A little bit more about [mo]re than a run 

[mo]re than a run has already raised over $280,000 for mental health and suicide prevention.  The goal is to unite the running community across Australia and New Zealand for a common cause.  On the 26th of Movember runners from all over Aus/NZ will run will run either a 10km, 30km or 60km distance, united and connected as a community to make an impact. 

The 10km distance represents 
10km for the one in ten men around the world living with an anxiety disorder

The 30km distance represents 
30km for the 30% rise in the number of Australian men dying by suicide over the last decade.

The 60km distance 
60km for the 60 men we lose to suicide each hour, every hour around the world.

It is grass roots community initiatives like this that can make an impact through the power of conversation and connection to community. 

If you feel compelled to get involved please do so and you can get more information at morethanarun.com.au or via @more_than_a_run if you want to take part in the run.

戶外瑜伽&冥想體驗

每天，我們從醒來的那一刻，就不斷地接收各種不同的資訊，不論重要與否、簡單或複雜，各種念頭、想法盤據在心裡，即使不覺得有壓力，也很難認為自己是過著輕鬆寫意的生活。日子就像陀螺般轉啊轉，不自覺中時光已悄悄流逝，卻想不起來自己到底在忙什麼？

記得很久以前，第一次使用維基百科的時候，在查詢的過程中總會發現新的未知，點下去這個未知內容裡，又會有源源不絕的未知，這種無窮無盡的搜尋方式，一個不留神，就會忘記自己一開始到底要查什麼。其實日常生活中也很容易發生類似的情形，我們的心思大多紛亂，常在過去和未來之間跳躍。如果毫無察覺，注意力就會無法集中，造成生產效率低落，不是瞎忙就是一事無成，被擔憂恐懼綁架，把自己搞得身心俱疲。

很多人覺得要靜靜坐在那裡什麼都不想很難，其實可以嘗試著從短時間開始，從觀察呼吸或身體掃描開始，呼吸的時候除了感受到氣流通過鼻子進出體內，也可以感受那氣流是否有味道？是通暢還是阻塞？是乾燥還是濕潤？又或者是冷冽還是溫熱？感受身體跟地面或椅子接觸的感覺，頭部或肩膀的重量，皮膚的感受...等等。如果一不小心分神，也不必懊惱，回想一下是什麼佔據心裡，再重新回到呼吸或當下與周遭環境的連結即可。 透過正念冥想，可以幫助我們更有覺知地觀察身邊所發生的事物，各種感官也會變得更加敏銳，專注力提升後較容易將任務依照重要性高低，有條理地一一完成，就有機會從緊繃高壓的自我中解放。

等待許久，很開心疫情終於見到曙光。在美好陽光普照的早晨中，我們一起用瑜伽與冥想開啟能量豐盈的一天，並向大家宣告lululemon在高雄地區的實體社群活動即將蓄勢待發，歡迎更多朋友和我一起參加精彩的熱汗活動。

Ridgedale Center, Minnetonka, MN

7/10

Ridgedale is one of the three remaining dale malls in the Twin Cities and having gone to all of them this was my least favorite. Just because it was my least favorite doesn’t mean Ridgedale wasn’t good. It just wasn’t what I was expecting, which was for the whole mall to be like the Nordstrom wing.

The Nordstrom wing of this mall is beautiful. It has a sleek design, containing unique lighting features, many upscale brands, and has a more upscale feel than the rest of the mall. Some of the stores in this wing are UNTUCKit, Hammer Made, and Tommy Bahama.

The rest of the mall still is upscale from a store and restaurant perspective, it just doesn’t feel as high-end as the Nordstrom wing. The other portion features tenants like TUMI, lululemon, and The Cheesecake Factory. There is also a Dick’s House of Sport, which is a new experiential-based concept store by Dick’s Sporting Goods.

The mall is configured in an atypical plus shape that leads to each of the four anchors and other stores. At the mall’s focal point is a grand center court, similar to the one at Altamonte Mall in Orlando. The center court here is a great place to hang out. There are big skylights and a plethora of comfortable seating as well as a Jamba Juice and Caribou Coffee for beverages.

Ridgedale is a unique mall that bridges the gap between high-end brands and typical mall stores in a manageable-sized space making it a popular alternative for area residents instead of Mall of America. This mall is worth checking out if you feel inclined to.

It’s release day on @dynamicpilatestv ! This class, Daisy Duke 2022 is probably my favorite class of 2022! It literally has every component I need as I navigate through this #menopausejourney ! Who knew fitness would play such a game changing role for #menopauseweightloss and relief! What are my main objectives in a class for building muscle and burning fat? 1. Lift heavy weights (I mean heavy! Heavy enough to feel the struggle after 10 reps). 2. HIIT (get your heart rate up for short bursts. Traditional cardio is not beneficial for women over 40! So stop doing cardio everyday! ). 3. Work the entire core in all directions! Bloating and midsection weight gain is inevitable however incorporating rotational core exercises really helps with the midsection bloat. A strong core is imperative for lifting heavy weights. Without a strong core I would not be able to lift as heavy as I do without injury.  4. It’s gotta be fun! Bottom line is you have to stay consistent and if your workouts are fun and fresh it’s easier to stay on track and constant. Here is another tip which most Pilates teachers will not tell you…. Pilates is NOT the only form of exercise and it should NOT be your only source for fitness. I own a Pilates studio and co own a Pilates app @dynamicpilatestv . You would think I only do Pilates, however only 2 of my workouts per week are Pilates based.  I lift weights at home and attend a fun fitness class that incorporates lots of HIIT and weights.  The variety has really helped me stay on track and meet my goals. I feel should mention cardio again…. Stop the cardio if you are over 40! Seriously! I was running 5 days a week and gaining weight like a newborn! Once I swapped the cardio for HIIT the weight gain stopped! It’s not about working out harder, but working out smarter! “mind body connection”

몸의 감각을 찾아가는 과정을 통해 더 세밀한 움직임 지도를 만들어 가는 시간을 나누어보려 합니다. 

새는 날기 위해 물고기는 헤엄치기 위해 사람은 움직이기 위해 존재합니다. 인간의 움직임은 매우 다양하고 자유로운데 비해 우리 삶은 그러치 못합니다. 매번 똑같은 움직만 반복한다면 그 이상의 움직임은 점점 어색해지고 퇴화하게 될 것입니다.  모든 스포츠활동에 기반이 되고 운동을 하는데 필수적으로 필요한 1. 모빌리티 트레이닝과 2. 전신을 연결하는 플로어 무브먼트를 통해 자유로운 움직임을 경험해보세요!! 

1. Mobility Training (최세환) 

목 부터 발 끝 까지 모든 관절을 움직여 기름칠 합니다. 몸을 직접 컨트롤하며 움직임을 익혀보고 평소 부족했던 움직임을 체크해볼 수 있는 시간을 갖습니다. 특히 회전움직임(CARs)을 기본으로 알려드리고 플로어 무브먼트를 하기 위해 필요한 움직임들을 알려드립니다. 

관절은 혈액공급이 거의 되지 않는 무혈관조직으로 움직임여야만 영양분 공급이 원활해집니다. 특히 회전움직임을 했을 때 가장 많은 영양분을 공급 받게 되고 끝 범위 움직임을 반복적으로 해봄으로써 관절의 기능을 되살아나게 합니다. 

이렇게 움직임을 재설정한 후 플로어 무브먼트를 접근한다면 한결 부드럽고 안전하게 배울 수 있게됩니다. 

2. Movement Program (변신혜, 금나리)

-Perception (인지) 항상 자각될 수는 없으나, 몸에 집중하여 즉각적으로 느껴지는 신체의 감각을 자각하여 움직임을 확장합니다. 

-Floor movement 두 발로 서는 자세의 중심이 아닌 플로어(바닥)으로 더 가까이 중심을 두고, 발에서 손 , 등, 무릎 ,어깨 등으로 무게중심이 이동하여 자연스럽게 흐르는 중심에 대한 이해와 안전한 몸의 사용법에 대해 익힙니다. 

-Contact improvisation 전문적인 지식을 가지고 있지 않거나,  춤을 못 추는 사람도 얼마든지 즐길 수 있는 몸으로 하는 언어 즉 ‘컨택’을 통해 가지고 있는 몸에 대한 지식을 통합하고 움직임의 시야를 한단계 넓혀가는 과정의 한 걸음이 되길 바랍니다.

I have always been a playful type. It is one of my best traits for sure. I’m like a self contained party in a 6’ frame. I feel it’s one of the ways I’ll stay young forever. 
If you’ve ever visited an old folks home and I’m sure many people have, I’ve noticed this interesting split. Some people get super crotchety, angry and unpleasant and some get sweeter and friendlier. I don’t think it has much to do with their age or pain or condition. I think it’s whether they feel content with how their life played out, the people they touched, and the contentment in their heart. 
I hope at the end of mine, I’m the kind of nice old lady that feels the contentment of a life well lived. I think the only way to guarantee that though is to be the best version of myself at every moment. Not to say to be happy all the time or make mistakes because that’s impossible, but to be this fun loving, jovial and kind person as much as possible. It is always possible. 
I mentioned this concept once before but I think about a life resume. At the end of my life, I’m going to see all these amazing experiences. Not whether I had a Gucci purse. I will see this well lived, full life. One lived as authentically as possible. One with lots of laughs, a bunch of tears, lots of love, and even more fun. I want my life resume to be jam packed with vitamin A-mazing. I want it to be full of friends, full of love, and full of things I didn’t regret not doing. Even shitty experiences are learning ones. But we only grow from having them, the good, the learning, the fun, and the gruesome. We hope for less gruesome and work for the good and fun. My ledger is heavily weighted on the good and fun with sprinkles of learning to make the good ones feel even better. 
I have this feeling I’ll be the old lady cracking jokes at all the young hooligans coming in to visit their grandparents.

It’s been a week. So much change but more realization than anything. I continue to evolve in ways I never anticipated. My world view shaped by my interactions and the people I meet, the conversations I have, and this life I continue to live to its fullest. 
There are so few people in my specific circumstances. So few that it is at once unique in the most amazing of ways and isolating and scary in that I feel utterly alone with no roadmap. I have perspectives and knowledge of the genders that give me glimpses into areas I wish I was still ignorant of. I almost wish I didn’t know some of the things I do. It’s a TMI type of thing. For example, Do you really want to know what kinky stuff your parents are into?  Yuk. Sometimes ignorance really is bliss. 
In a span of just 3 years and really a lot less, I went from living one life as one person (at least on the outside), and in an incredibly short time, am this seemingly other person. Even if to me, I’m the same person inside, letting myself be this person on the outside changes everything. And then add in the most important piece, everyone treats me differently. I’ve been excluded from one inner circle and been invited into another. From straight culture to queer. From boy to girl. From cis to trans. From good looking guy to Amazon queen. Lol. From the top of society’s food chain to almost the bottom. Although I still have tons of privilege and live in a wonderful welcoming city thank god. My inner circles continue to shift. 
I have learned so much this past week I wish I could share. These nuggets of knowledge, but alas I would be forsaken for shattering the blissful ignorance of a few I hold dear. Some knowledge is a burden, one I will gladly carry for you.

#DoTeam 模特生活日記
@lululemon 美國廣告拍攝

不管在國外拍多少次拍攝，對我來說都很有挑戰
不同於台灣的制式和架構。
美國的拍攝更自由，更放鬆，更沒有參考和標準答案
品牌想看到你的個性，想看到你的內在 
然後全部濃縮在一次次快門裡面。
用一個眼神，一個表情告訴他們 你是誰。
他們想知道
你的氣質如何能夠和他們的商品混合成更有趣的靈魂。
這 真 的 很 難。

因為在展現自我的同時，你又不能強過商品。
而且每個商品都有不同的特性和樣貌。
你也不該只有一招在鏡頭前面。
這是模特和藝人在拍攝時候最大的不同。
我們駕馭商品，讓造型看起來合理且確實。
勾起你心裡的慾望。

但當粉絲看到偶像明星的時候，他們的慾望
是希望自己變成他們

「但當消費者看到模特的時候，
是要能夠看到自己存在可以變得更美好的未來。」

重點從來都不是 要擺什麼動作。
重點是 你穿了什麼，你是誰，你感受到了什麼。
帥不帥 美不美？ 是那麼的主觀以及可以被操弄。
動作 眼神 也只是想法和意念的延伸。

這也是模特在國外，
往往會感受到自己的價值更高
因為我們是設計的參與者，
是設計師藍圖的最後一步，
是平等的參與整個團隊的合作。
而不只是會說話會走路，被貼上價錢的人型立台。

這才是真正模特

我們站在商品前展現自己
卻又和團隊平行前進 
同時可能 又把一部分的自己隱藏在商品之後
為的是讓真正重要的事情被凸顯。

也許我是比較old school 
所以常常在堅持一些自己內心想太多的自我準則。

但這在我心中，才是我一直想前進的，真正的模特的方向。

happy as a clam these days

here’s a lil reminder for anyone who needs to hear it right now :))

basically all it is is that you are NOT defined by your career, sport, other people’s perceptions of you or even limitations you place on yourself. As I transition from cross to track, into the final weeks of the semester and holiday season, I need to be reminded of this. 

I’ve never been good with transitions, I try to play it cool but on the inside I feel like i’m just a jumbled confused mess when things change. In these moments I let school define my happiness and I let how I felt on the run that day impact my life negatively. 

Honestly, I am stressed about school right now and worried for track season. I got a not so great score on a physics exam last week that I still haven’t been able to let go. Track season last year was a nightmare so I’m working on having an open mind this year but it still just takes time. 

This post is a good reminder for me too though, that the “things” in life: school, running… can’t take over your life. If you don’t control them, they will control you and that is no way to live. Remember who you are, it’s all going to be okay. 

My physics exam will be better next time. You live and you learn and do better next time. I hope y’all have the best week and make sure to socialize. Friends and a community are important for keeping us all sane :))

November is Crohns and Colitis Awareness Month 💜

As a #crohnie who is open about it, feel free to ask questions, or read on! I’m also still on my mission to raise funds for the foundation, and will be hosting 4 EVENTS THIS MONTH you can support! 

Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis are diseases that inflame the lining of the GI (gastrointestinal) tract and disrupt your body's ability to digest food, absorb nutrition, and eliminate waste in a healthy manner. These are lifelong diseases and people can experience acute periods of active symptoms (active disease or flare), and other times when their symptoms are absent (remission). It is time to raise more awareness, more funds and help find a cure!

This month I have some fundraising initiatives happening in support of @getgutsycanada and the @crohnscolitiscollectiveco! That means NEW apparel, NEW times to connect(woo!!), events open to everyone for a donation! If there is a way you want to get involved, or come ride/connect/ support - let me know! Also huge thanks to my @lululemon community for supporting me this month and helping me put these together ✨

還記得今年五月lululemon高雄門市剛開幕的時候，另外兩位大使還沒出現，因此由我代表接受電視新聞的訪問。對於一個與品牌還在陌生階段的我，跟門市夥伴順稿時，在某個段落不假思索就說出了他們（指lululemon）如何如何...當下立刻被糾正說：『妳現在是我們的人，所以新聞稿的主詞都要用我們喔。』

經過了半年的相處後，的確是很真切地感受到了被當作一份子的歸屬感。我們一起攀岩、瑜伽，一起手做療癒植栽，一起從僵硬尬笑到自然放鬆拍團體照。

前幾天，我們一起在野外，像孩子般玩跳跳床跟飛盤，豐盛的晚餐過後，一起度過了深度自我探索的夜晚，在分享了許多價值觀的看法後，對彼此更加熟識了解。隔天早上，我們一起在和煦暖陽的沐浴中，用心感受周遭的一切，感受微風吹過皮膚髮梢，帶來森林的氣息；因著秋天轉黃的葉子被風緩緩地從空中片片散落，也同時間跟樹上的鳥語和鳴伴出悅耳的聲響。

短短不到24小時的時間，共體感的凝聚力在這樣的活動中逐漸發酵擴散。記得當時新聞講稿中提到，品牌希望能讓大家更重視自己的身心靈幸福。而在這段時間以來，明白了這不只是一個口號，在lululemon的文化當中，就是希望能把每一個文字上的標語，用行動化為你/妳我生活中的一部分。很榮幸跟大家一同努力把美好生活實踐在我們的日常裡。

Be you. Be well.

Who doesn't want to walk out of the Apple store with a shiny new iPhone, having only spent a fraction of the price at the store? Or buy an 85" TV from Best Buy and only pay 10% of the price in the store? 
-
Well, if something seems too good to be true, you should be cautious and assume there is more than meets the eye!
-
When you buy a big ticket item, most stores will give you the option at checkout to "buy now, pay later". 
-
Everyone from Amazon to Walmart to Lululemon does this. On the surface, it seems appealing because they qualify you for the loan quickly and you don't have to shell out a bunch of dough. 
-
The number of young people that are regularly using "buy now, pay later" has skyrocketed in the last couple of years. In a recent survey, 61% of 18-24 year olds said they have used one of these loans. A year earlier this number was only 38%!! 
-
Most "buy now, pay later" offers are FAR worse than what Apple has. A lot of them have countless hidden fees and a ton of fine print. And if you miss a payment for any reason, it will be damaging to your credit score and there can be steep penalties that you have to pay. 
-
Some people might try and use 0% loans to their advantage by borrowing money to purchase an item and then use the money they didn't spend to invest in the stock market. 
-
BUT this is risky. Imagine if you decided to do this in January of this year? You would have lost 20% of what you invested since the market is down and you'd risk not having enough to pay your monthly payments on the loan. 
-
It doesn't mean you should never use one of these loans. If you use it responsibly and ensure that it doesn't cause you to spend money you wouldn't normally spend, there's nothing wrong with it. As a rule, if you aren't able to easily pay for the item in cash, you should NOT get a loan to buy it.

If you’re feeling lost lately, maybe it’s because you’re straying too far from your path.

Let me explain.

We all are told that we have the power to create the life we want. But I believe that we have the power to create greatness within the path that’s meant for us. 

There’s a lot of distractions out there. Our mind will try to convince us to stray from our path. It will tell us there’s something better out there. Or that were not good enough. Or that we should just stay within our comfort zone. Be complacent and comfortable because it’s safe.

Safe isn’t an option.

To stay on your path you’ve gotta take a chance. And that means betting on yourself. Bettering yourself. Taking risks. Getting uncomfortable. Dealing with things not going to plan. Dealing with pain. Rejection. Getting told no a thousand times until you find a worthy yes. Looking fear in the face. Pivoting. Making changes. Listening to your gut. Your body. Your mind. The universe speaks to you if you listen. Yeah it’s a bit “live laugh love” with crystals energy, but I believe it. 

Distractions are there to hold you accountable. I can’t tell you how many times this week I’ve listened to the voices in my head and wanted to give up or take a long break. 

But what would that do long term? 

I realized I had to take a moment, breathe and get the fuck back up. 

In the end, the only way to success on your intended path is to give a middle finger to distractions and come back from setbacks stronger. There’s no other way.

You either give in and give up.
Or give it your all. 💙

到底汽車點樣移入商場？網友照片分享神秘過程！
.
商場中庭位置經常有不同展覽展出，其中一個最受歡迎的展覽必定是車展，各位sis可能不明白為什麼男人那麼喜歡擁有屬於自己的車，除了希望有自己的私人空間外，更想外出時能不用再乘搭公共交通工具夠到達目的地 ！但家又有沒有想過到底一架車那麼巨形，是如何從商場外運進來的？怎看也沒有一個大門能讓汽車進入。
.
日前，有一名網友解答大家這個問題，並分享汽車是如何被移進商場的過程。首先工人們需要齊心合力把車輛移到鐵板並抬高，令它能穩固地安放在機械台，然後再慢慢從商場大門口降落到展覽的樓層，過程不但困難，也是極度危險， 稍一不慎便會發生悲劇，令人看得膽顫心驚～
.
對這個有趣且緊張的情況，不少網友紛紛留言表示 “這解決了我一直以來的問號”、“終於知道車是如何進去的”、當中更有不少 幽默感爆錶的留言，「 我以為要把商場拆掉重建才能把車安放進去」、 「我一直以為是未有商場先有車」、「不是由一架汽車模型演變而成的嗎？」留言越來越誇張，不知道這貼文又有否令你長知識和解決問號呢？
.

One of the best and also one of the worst times to be a runner 🍁 🌞 Best because it’s sunny but cool enough to not overheat, shorts are still acceptable *just* and, you know those fresh morning when the cold air hits your face but the sun is also shining? GLORIOUS. There really isn’t much that beats chasing the winter sunrise.

On the other hand, worst because dark mornings and darker evenings from about 4pm 🔦 Pulling on my kit has felt impossible Monday through Friday. I’ve gotten myself in SUCH a tizz about running in the dark. In previous years, I’ve never have thought twice about it - that’s not to say I wasn’t responsible and safe, I’d never go out without wearing ALL the hi-vis gear but, with all the horrific news about runners over the past 18 months, I just can’t do it. I read somewhere that 67% of female runners stop running outdoors during November and February and it made me rly rly sad. I asked a lot of you about how you felt about running during winter months and many of you felt the same, but many offered up some tips so I’m going to be trying those next week. Thank you ✨

3) Spikes or Cleats
Game changer for icy and snowy trails. 

4) Warm Gloves
I love my Sherpa lined Mitton’s! If you run cold like me, and/or have Raynaud’s syndrome (poor circulation) Mitton’s over fingered gloves are much better. 

5) Hand and Toe warmers

6) Fleece lined leggings 

Enjoy those trails and stay warm and happy!!

The Healing is excited to announce our BIPOC Men Yoga Teacher Certification Scholarship. 

BIPOC Men make up less than 1% of yoga instructors nationwide. Additionally, most BIPOC communities don’t have the same access to yoga and other avenues to address their wellness and mental health needs.

As a part of our commitment to normalize wellness for the BIPOC community, The Healing is proud partner with lululemon and lululemon ambassador and mindful performance coach, Jeremy Walton, to offer yoga scholarships for BIPOC men in pursuit of their 200-Hour teacher certification.

We believe representation matters. More BIPOC instructors in this space will lower barriers of entry for our community, ultimately fueling our mission to normalize mental health practices for BIPOC men and the resulting impact on the communities around them.

The Healing Yoga Scholarship 2022-2023 Cohort will receive:
● $2500 scholarship to cover the full cost of a 200-hour teacher certification
● Mentorship from yogi and mindful performance coach, Jeremy Walton
● Community activities and resources for our 2022-2023 cohort

Healing after three years of serious gastrointestinal illness is remarkable gift. 

I’ve gone from spending nearly everyday in agonizing pain, to being able to digest food and living life *mostly* normally again. 

I full-heartedly believe that my recovery is because of 3 things: 
✨Community - when I first got sick I was quarantined during the pandemic; I’d go days where I barely spoke to anyone and I was miserable. 
Between @yogalofttucson + @lululemon, I’m literally ALWAYS surrounded by amazing people. I’ve found a community that I feel safe in and I’m extremely thankful. 

✨Nutrition - I realized that I had become so terrified of food because of GI pain, that I basically stopped eating. 
Once I started researching the microbiome, I realized that my low fiber diet was causing the majority of issues. Now that I’m working on introducing more fiber and diversity into my diet, the difference is night and day! 
It’s a huge practice of letting go of fear, and trusting my body. 

✨Nervous System Regulation - I’ve always known that stress is hard on the body, especially digestion. But I’ve never been able to kick it - even with yoga,  meditation practices, and therapy. 
I didn’t realized that my nervous system starts in my spine, and if my spine isn’t in optimal alignment, things get… complicated. 
Thanks to @DrEvinPing at @TheSourceTucson I’m FINALLY seeing + feeling  improvement in my nervous system regulation! 
I’m able to sleep (I feel like I’ve been catching up on 30+ years of no sleep 😂), and that constant feeling of ‘something’s wrong’ has become a thing of the past. 

Im experiencing a miracle and I’m not taking it for granted. 

To everyone who has seen me and held me along the path - Your kindness has helped me tremendously. 

To everyone dealing with chronic illness - I see you, and I’m proud of you and everything that you’re doing.

Last week in NYC, we brought together leaders and young women from the Girls Opportunity Alliance Network for a roundtable discussion on the opportunities and challenges facing grassroots organizations serving girls and were joined by our partners @CAREorg and @UNICEF. Participants from 10 different countries had a chance to exchange ideas and best practices for empowering girls and to create new connections with one another—with artist @zovi_live_illustration doing live drawings to reflect the top takeaways! They also engaged in a session on mindfulness and wellbeing led by @unfoundation and @lululemon and a session on digital fundraising led by @lightful. 

Check out some of the wisdom they shared:

🌟"Sometimes people tell me that our organization’s goal to support 100,000 girls in India is just a drop in the ocean. But what I want to say to them all is that in every drop there IS an ocean.” -Dhirendra, @Milaan_Foundation

🌟”I get so much energy from meeting these leaders. We are all committed to supporting girls, whether we come from Kenya or Vietnam or New York City. We come from different places, but we share a common purpose.” -Wanjiru, @SamburuGirlsFDN

🌟”When we make these connections across organizations, it’s transformational. We truly can go further together.” -Vilma, @Maia_Impact

Huge thanks to our participants:  @TheActionFoundation, @AkiliDada, @BOSEJAGirls, @DandelionAfrica, @GirlUpUganda, @TheHarpswellFoundation, @KakenyasDream, @Maia_Impact, @Milaan_Foundation, @PacificLinksFoundation, @RaziasRayofHope, @SamburuGirlsFdn, @StudioSamuel

HOW do you motivate to WANT to practice something you’re not good at? I think I made a connection in understanding how difficult it is to show up and do something that is good for you but yet makes you feel somewhat inferior and incapable of doing. I can jump, flip and fly (well maybe not fly) but the simple act of staying still in a yoga pose is something that is incredibly challenging for me and quite frankly~unpleasant and painful. I can understand NOW how my clients feel about their struggles to find time to work on and stay committed to their fitness to become healthier and fit. I realize that exercise doesn’t come easy to others like it does to me, just like Yoga does not come easy for me. Sooo…will I ever get better at it? Well I can either believe NO or I can focus on PRACTICE. I may never even be close to being perfect but with practice, it can bring on progress and change for the better. And maybe that’s where I need to shift my focus instead of accepting frustration and not trying. Thx @valerie.griffiths for a great yoga class yesterday where your teaching allows us to take and do what WE need from it, even if it’s taking a 15 minute shavasana when everyone else is still doing yoga poses. 🤣 #thesweatlife#lululemon #yoga#progressisprogress #workonyourself#balance #lululemonambassador#motivate #challengeyourbody#beebe #personaltrainer

Sirsasana or the Yoga Headstand was a pose that I absolutely admired for the first year of my practice…. But didn’t dare attempt. The idea of being upside down on my head terrified me. Not to mention I had no core strength. What if i fell in class? 

However this fall I dove headfirst ☺️ into learning this pose from the foundations up. I am now holding this pose in class, which I never thought I ever would have the ability or confidence to! 

Yoga class can seem really daunting  when you are starting… As a newbie, I used to look around the room at all the Lululemon yogis bending into poses I had never seen before. I was intimidated. “Ill never be able to do that,” I scoffed to myself back in the car. 

But once I started learning about the fundamentals of yoga and what it really is meant to be about….. being with each breath, and meeting yourself where ever you are in your practice…. I found my confidence to simply exist where I am. I kept arriving at the mat with acceptance… and not envy, not fear and with no expectation of “getting better”. 

And thats what allowed me to slowly build, slowly add more, slowly fold deeper. And it lead me to this confident headstand in the backyard. 

So many people tell me yoga scares them, they feel intimidated, they feel that its too competitive, or showy for them…. I just try to gently remind them…. Yoga isn’t any of that. Not fundamentally. Yes western culture has morphed yoga into that at times…but yoga can be sitting cross-legged or yoga can be in a handstand with your toes on your head in scorpion pose. As long as you are present in your body and with your breath…. You are doing yoga. You are a yogi ♥️

And you DONT NEED NAME BRAND FITS TO BE A BADDIE

I went to play pick up volleyball last night randomly as I saw a post on IG. Mostly people using she/her pronouns so I was by far the tallest. I was also for sure the strongest. But I definitely wasn’t even close to the best volleyball player. I was quite surprised how girlie I’ve become. In some ways, it was irritating me and in others, it was a bit validating too. I wasn’t trying to suck at playing or be sucky with my forearms hurting me from bumping, but here it was. My forearms bright red, me not being aggressive or competitive, just happy to be there having fun. I’ve never been competitive with sports as long as I felt I played well for me. The score in the end was irrelevant. I did find it funny how I was so tentative. I would never go for the ball. Lol. If it came to me or if it was obviously mine, I have decent enough skills to do the job. Lucky for me, I’m tall as I was actually good at the net and had a few tip ins. 
I think part of the reasons are obvious but I came to a realization this morning. I’m afraid, deathly afraid even, of hurting someone else. If I allowed myself to play to my best and be more competitive, I don’t know if I would have the self control to know when or where to stop. So it’s just easier to play it safe and not do it. I can’t risk hurting someone even if that means not giving it my all. 
Maybe this is a result of who I am or how I was raised but I really dislike confrontation. I wish I had a little more in me. I went for a walk with a friend a few days ago and this creepy dude stops in front of us, doing the whole up and down look. Felt like I needed a shower right then and there. The friend goes off on the guy. Lol. Me I’m standing there in disbelief. Lol. Both for the gall of the creepy dude and the way this friend just made him feel as small as an ant. I would’ve just smiled awkwardly and tried to extricate myself as quickly as possible.  That doesn’t always go as planned though so I wish I dad a bit more fight in me that way. 
I had fun at volleyball. I def go back. I might even try to spike. 

Softly. Lol
